research.direction: Parcel-scale soil water balance for vineyards driven by Sentinel-2 (FAO-56 single/dual Kc with Kcb from NDVI/fc, Ks/FTSW, root-zone depletion), forced by ERA5-Land: a concrete recipe for AgriWatch (Colab + GEE + Drive registry), tested on the user's own data
research.summary:
Plan_v5 already proposed FAO-56 with pyfao56 at a high level. This adds verified parameters, design rules for grassed rainfed vineyards, and a prototype run on the local registry data. Scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-1-geoworldlook-agriscreen/0b6bc240-34e1-5fd3-a139-3c46967fd603/scratchpad/wb/ (wb_proto.py, run_station.py, run_vineyard.py, run_dual.py, paired_diff.py). They import the repo QC and anomaly functions read-only. The harness reproduces the v1.0 baseline exactly: ERA5-L RZ R=0.583 [0.50,0.665], n=2976; POD 0.574, FAR 0.571, n=312.

Results:

(1) A water balance does NOT give better daily soil-moisture anomalies than ERA5-Land.
- FAO-56 bucket at the ISMN grass plot (Hargreaves ET0, S-2 Kcb): R=0.625 [0.545,0.693].
- Paired block-bootstrap dR vs ERA5-L 0-100 cm: +0.04 [-0.04,+0.12], so no proven gain.
- ERA5-L 0-28 cm (depth-matched): R=0.691, dR=+0.108 [+0.049,+0.167].
- The bucket is significantly worse than 0-28 cm: dR=-0.066 [-0.104,-0.027].

(2) The bucket wins on timing. It reproduces the yearly date when 20-30 cm soil enters its dry regime (equal-quantile threshold, n=9 years):
- bucket: MAE 14-20 d, Spearman 0.89;
- ERA5-L 0-28 cm: MAE 37 d;
- current ERA5-L 0-100 cm SMA layer: MAE 66 d, bias +60 d.

(3) At point scale S-2 adds little to the balance.
- S-2 Kcb vs climatological Kcb: +0.015 R.
- SR 2.5 m vs 10 m: changes FTSW by at most 0.006.
- TAW +-30%: shifts summer stress days by 10-30 per season.
So TAW and the vine Kcb design decide precision, not pixel size.

(4) Two naive designs fail, consistent with Campos 2012 and Almeida 2024.
- Whole-pixel NDVI to Kcb saturates in a grassed vineyard: FTSW < 0.4 from early June every year. The VINEYARD_06 NDVI curve is driven by the inter-row (May weeding dip, August grass senescence, autumn regrowth).
- Feeding same-season NDVI into Kcb damps drought: Kcb_mid 0.42 in 2022 vs 0.74 in 2021; season Spearman with ISMN falls from 0.79 to 0.64 (n=9, directional only).

Recipe:
- Dual-source, two-layer (vine + cover crop, WaLIS-like) FAO-56 balance.
- FAO-56 wine-grape priors, verified from the pyfao56 table transcription: Kcb 0.15/0.65/0.40; stages 30/60/40/80 d from April; hmax 1.75 m; Zr 1.0-2.0 m; p 0.45.
- S-2 used for structural vigour and inter-row phenology, not as same-season Kcb.
- Penman-Monteith ET0 from ERA5-L.
- TAW prior with uncertainty, plus inverse calibration from cheap vine observations.
- Phenology-specific stress index and days-to-stress forecast.
- The S-2 canopy anomaly stays as the observed-impact tier for 'alert' (EDO logic).

Honest limits:
- No vine truth exists yet.
- The ISMN reference is a grass plot. Its 20/30 cm sensors lose contact in the cracking clay (QC-4 in Condom_QC.md, not applied in qc_insitu), so summer values are censored.
- Season-level tests have n=9.
- Most literature numbers are snippet-level; publisher sites were blocked.

methods.name: M1. Dual-source, two-layer FAO-56 vine water balance (new step_08_water_balance)
methods.description:
A daily loop per parcel.

Layers:
- top 0-0.4 m: shared by the cover crop and the vine;
- bottom 0.4-1.2 m: vine only.

Fluxes:
- Vine transpiration: T_v = Ks_v*Kcb_v*ET0, taken from both layers in proportion to available water.
- Cover-crop transpiration: T_c = Ks_c*Kcb_c*ET0, taken from the top layer only.
- Soil evaporation: FAO-56 Ke with Ze=0.10 m, REW about 9 mm, TEW from theta, few = 1 - fc_vine - fc_cover.

Rules:
- Ks follows FAO-56 eq. 84 from start-of-day depletion.
- p = 0.45 + 0.04*(5 - ETc), clipped to 0.1-0.8.
- Rain fills the top layer, then the bottom; the excess drains.
- FTSW_vine = 1 - (Dt+Db)/TAW.

Outputs to the registry (new product WB_VINE):
- FTSW;
- Ks_vine;
- T_vine (mm);
- deficit to RAW (mm);
- FTSW z vs 1991-2020 DOY climatology, from a reference run with climatological Kcb for pre-S-2 years.

Priors:
- FAO-56 wine grapes: Kcb 0.15/0.65/0.40; stage lengths 30/60/40/80 d from 1 April (mid-latitude wine); hmax 1.75 m; Zr 1.0-2.0 m (use 1.2 m); p 0.45.
- Cover fraction from the parcel attribute inter_row already planned in Plan_v6 D-033: bare 0, alternate rows 0.5, all rows 1.

Implementation:
- Own numpy loop of about 150 lines; a working prototype exists in run_dual.py.
- Alternative: pyfao56 1.4.3. It accepts a precomputed ETref and daily Kcb/fc/h via its Update class, but it is single-layer, so the cover-crop compartment needs own code.
methods.why_better_than_ndvi_only:
The NDVI anomaly only says the canopy is greener or browner than in other years, and it mixes vine, inter-row grass and management. The balance converts weather, soil and canopy into the variable viticulture actually uses: FTSW and Ks, linked to predawn water potential (Lebon 2003; Pellegrino 2004). It separates vine from cover-crop competition and is aware of phenology.

In the prototype the top-layer drying onset matched the in-situ dry-onset date with MAE 14 d and Spearman 0.89. The current SMA layer has MAE 66 d.

It also creates parcel-specific levers (TAW, vigour, inter-row management). These are the only levers available, because all 15 vineyards share one ERA5 cell.

evidence.citation: Own prototype (this study), scratchpad/wb/run_station.py, run_dual.py, paired_diff.py; ISMN Condom 2016-2024, harness identical to step_07.validate_anomalies
evidence.finding: Baseline reproduced exactly (R=0.583, n=2976; POD/FAR 0.574/0.571). Station bucket vs ISMN 20-30 cm: R=0.625 [0.545,0.693], dR vs ERA5-L RZ +0.04 [-0.04,+0.12]. Yearly dry-onset date (equal-quantile threshold): bucket MAE 20 d, dual top layer MAE 14 d (Spearman 0.89 both), ERA5-L 0-28 cm MAE 37 d, ERA5-L 0-100 cm MAE 66 d (bias +60 d); n=9.

evidence.citation: FAO-56 (Allen et al. 1998) Tables 11, 12, 17 and 22, as transcribed in pyfao56 v1.4.3, tools/tables.py (downloaded from PyPI)
evidence.finding: Wine grapes: Kc 0.30/0.70/0.45, hmax 1.75 m; Kcb 0.15/0.65/0.40; Zr 1.0-2.0 m, p 0.45; mid-latitude wine stage lengths 30/60/40/80 d (210 d, April start).

evidence.citation: Lebon E., Dumas V., Pieri P., Schultz H.R. 2003. Funct. Plant Biol. 30:699-710
evidence.finding: Vineyard (VSP) water-balance model. Relative transpiration is a bilinear function of FTSW, and transpiration is partitioned between vine and soil. Validated against neutron-probe FTSW over 4 seasons in Alsace (good in 3 of 4 years). Close relation between field soil water storage and predawn water potential.

evidence.citation: Celette F., Ripoche A., Gary C. 2010. WaLIS. Agric. Water Manag. 97:1749-1759
evidence.finding: Two-compartment model for an intercropped vineyard (bare soil, barley, tall fescue in southern France). Vine and cover water stress were simulated well. The most influential parameters were maximum vine transpiration, soil evaporation, runoff, and the TTSW of each crop. The worst errors occurred in winter.

evidence.citation: Celette F., Gaudin R., Gary C. 2008. Eur. J. Agron. 29:153-162
evidence.finding: Cover-crop roots deplete the topsoil in spring, before vine uptake. Vines shift their roots deeper in deep soils. Winter recharge is better under cover.

evidence.citation: Fandino M. et al. 2012. Agric. Water Manag. 112:75-87 (SIMDualKc, Albarino vineyard with active ground cover)
evidence.finding: Separate Kcb values for vine and active ground cover, plus Ke. The model was accurate only when the observed cover fraction, density and height were used. Kcb_full for the vine was 0.30/1.15/0.90 before scaling by Kd. TDR-validated.

evidence.citation: Almeida et al. 2024. Water 16:2567 (rainfed winegrapes, SIMDualKc + Landsat-derived fc)
evidence.finding: Calibrated Kcb 0.15/0.60/0.52 for a rainfed vineyard. Available soil water RMSE < 12 mm against a profile to 1.85 m. ETc_act/ETc was 36% between veraison and maturity. Vegetation indices could not fully track plant condition under water stress.

methods.data_needed:
Inputs:
- ERA5-Land daily: already ingested; add the Penman-Monteith bands (M2).
- Sentinel-2 10 m NDVI per parcel for all months, as a stats-only ingest without SR. Today S2_MONTHS=(4,10).
- Parcel attributes: inter_row, row_spacing_m.
- Soil available-water prior (M4).

Outputs:
- New registry rows: gwl_observations product WB_VINE (FTSW, Ks, T, deficit) and gwl_anomalies (FTSW z).
methods.feasible_in_colab_gee: Yes. After the GEE point extraction this is CPU-only numpy: 15 parcels x 36 years of days runs in seconds. pyfao56 and pyet are pip-installable (verified on PyPI: pyfao56 1.4.3, pyet 1.5.0). It fits run_task as task_water_balance between task_anomalies and task_validate.
methods.expected_gain:
No higher daily R against ISMN should be expected: the prototype gives dR +0.04 [-0.04,+0.12] vs ERA5-L RZ.

Real gains:
- Onset timing of seasonal drying: MAE 14-20 d vs 66 d for the current SMA layer (n=9).
- Vine units on the card: mm, FTSW, Ks.
- Physically defensible parcel differentiation via TAW, vigour and inter-row cover.
- A basis for days-to-stress forecasts.
methods.risks:
- TAW dominates: Zr 0.9 to 1.6 m (TAW 126 to 224 mm) shifts stress days by 20-30 per season.
- ERA5 precipitation errors propagate; rainfall spatial variability is the main error source (Plan_v5 L11).
- Absolute FTSW saturates without calibration. The prototype shows 80-122 days below 0.4 in VI-IX every year, which is partly real for rainfed clay vineyards.
- Winter refill and runoff on clay are weak points (Celette 2010; Gaudin 2014).
- Equifinality if too many parameters are calibrated.
methods.validation_plan:
Parameters are fixed from the literature and pre-registered before any run. Calibration years 2016-2020, test years 2021-2024.

(a) Station machinery check (done): grass parameters at the ISMN plot against the 0-30 cm profile. Report R with a paired bootstrap against ERA5-L, and the dry-onset MAE. Onset MAE is robust to QC-4 contact-loss censoring.

(b) Repeat at the 21 other SMOSMANIA stations in data/7_isismn_data (ERA5-L and S-2 per station from GEE). Report the median and spread.

(c) Vine level: pilot observations (M7).

(d) Closure checks: annual ETa vs precipitation, and T_vine within the FAO range.

methods.name: M2. FAO-56 Penman-Monteith ET0 from ERA5-Land in GEE (Hargreaves only as fallback), benchmarked against Meteo-France SAFRAN/SIM2
methods.why_better_than_ndvi_only:
ET0 drives depletion, and the FAO-56 Kcb tables are defined against PM ET0. The current local file has no Tmax, radiation, humidity or wind, so the prototype had to use Hargreaves with Tmax approximated as 2*Tmean - Tmin.

Hargreaves overestimates in humid climates and misses VPD and radiation anomalies during heatwaves (2019, 2022). In the prototype, ET0 x0.85 vs x1.15 changed summer stress days by 10-30 per season.

evidence.citation: Pelosi A. et al. 2020. Water 12:1669 (ERA5-Land vs UERRA vs interpolated stations for ET0)
evidence.finding: ERA5-Land outperformed UERRA. ET0 nRMSE 17% (kriging of stations 14%); nBIAS < 5% averaged over 18 stations. Wind scaled 10 m to 2 m by about 0.75.

evidence.citation: Vanella D. et al. 2022. J. Hydrol. Reg. Stud. (ERA5 and ERA5-Land vs 66 stations in Italy, 2008-2020)
evidence.finding: Air temperature was best, then RH, Rs and wind (wind weakest). ERA5-Land gives slightly more accurate ET0 than ERA5. Best in temperate climates.

evidence.citation: Hargreaves vs Penman-Monteith under humid conditions (ASCE J. Irrig. Drain. Eng. 2007) and the Veneto 35-station study (search snippets)
evidence.finding: Hargreaves tends to overestimate ET0 in humid conditions and needs local calibration. Calibrating the two parameters against PM gave only limited improvement (Droogers and Allen 2002).

evidence.citation: Meteo-France, Donnees changement climatique - SIM quotidienne (data.gouv.fr)
evidence.finding: All SAFRAN/SIM meteorological parameters on the 8 km grid for metropolitan France, as compressed CSV, updated regularly. Use it as an independent ET0 and precipitation benchmark. The definition of the ETP column must be checked in the documentation.

evidence.citation: AgriWatch repo step_01_ingest.py (ERA5_LAND_BANDS)
evidence.finding: The pipeline already reads ECMWF/ERA5_LAND/DAILY_AGGR, including temperature_2m_min. Adding the PM bands is a configuration change in the existing sync_era5_land_point.

methods.data_needed: ERA5-Land DAILY_AGGR PM bands: GEE point extraction for 1991 to today, cached in 12-month chunks. Optionally ERA5_LAND/HOURLY wind for scalar speed. SIM2 CSV for the Condom cell, a one-off download for the benchmark.
methods.feasible_in_colab_gee: Yes. The extraction pattern is identical to the existing ERA5 sync. PM in pyet or pyfao56 runs on CPU in Colab. The SIM2 files are large, so filter to one grid cell once and store on Drive.
methods.expected_gain: Removes a systematic forcing error: the Hargreaves humid-climate bias and the Tmax approximation. Expected daily ET0 nRMSE is about 15-20% (literature), and lower at dekad scale. The SAFRAN precipitation check quantifies the dominant error of the whole balance. It also enables SPEI-3 at no extra cost.
methods.risks:
- ERA5-L wind and radiation biases.
- The vector-averaged wind in DAILY_AGGR.
- The SIM2 ETP formula must be confirmed before treating it as a PM reference.
- Last-dekad ERA5-L values are provisional (about 5-day latency).
methods.validation_plan:
- At the Condom SAFRAN cell, compare ERA5-L PM vs SIM2 ETP and vs Hargreaves: monthly bias, nRMSE, and summer heatwave dekads.
- Compare ERA5 vs SAFRAN precipitation: dekadal bias and dry-dekad agreement.
- Rerun M1 with each ET0/P source and report the spread of stress days per season as forcing uncertainty.

methods.name: M3. Sentinel-2 to Kcb without circularity: structural vigour plus phenological-window unmixing of vine vs inter-row

evidence.citation: Own prototype run_vineyard.py and run_dual.py (VINEYARD_06, S2_10m and S2SR_2.5m)
evidence.finding: Single-source whole-pixel Kcb: FTSW < 0.4 on 82-122 of 122 days in VI-IX in every year. Dual-source with S-2 same-season vigour: Kcb_mid 0.42-0.74 across years, season Spearman vs ISMN 0.64; with fixed FAO vine Kcb, 0.79 (n=9). SR vs 10 m changes FTSW by at most 0.006.

evidence.citation: Campos I. et al. 2010. Agric. Water Manag. 98:45-54 (irrigated grapes, La Mancha)
evidence.finding: Kcb = 1.44*NDVI - 0.10 and Kcb = 1.79*SAVI - 0.08. Measured Kc = 0.96 x modelled, r2 = 0.67 against eddy covariance.

evidence.citation: Campos et al. (follow-up study of the same remote-sensing water-balance approach in deficit-irrigated vineyards, Albacete; exact reference not verified)
evidence.finding: VI-derived Kcb overestimates the actual crop coefficient under water stress. Ks was 0.2-0.4 in July-August.

evidence.citation: Pantaleoni Reluy N. et al. 2022. OENO One 56(1):145-159 (user-supplied full text)
evidence.finding: Vineyard NDVI is about 0.3 in Nov-Mar (no vine canopy). Inter-row cover is often weeded from April to mid-May in southern France and dries out in summer in non-irrigated vineyards, so its influence on NDVI is small by late June.

evidence.citation: Allen R.G., Pereira L.S. 2009. Irrig. Sci. 28:17-34; Pereira L.S. et al. 2020. Agric. Water Manag. 241:106197
evidence.finding: Density coefficient Kd from fc, h and ML; Kcb_full mainly from height. The A&P approach was tested on vineyards among other crops, with regression slopes near 1 and R2 >= 0.90 except for orchards. The exact Kd formula is quoted from memory.

evidence.citation: Guevara-Torres D.R. et al. 2025. Remote Sens. 17(19):3365
evidence.finding: Spectrally unmixed Sentinel-2 vegetation indices improve grapevine Kc prediction (Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay), and the models transfer across regions and cultivars. Inter-row vegetation produces mixed pixels.

evidence.citation: Williams L.E., Ayars J.E. 2005. Agric. For. Meteorol. 132:201-211
evidence.finding: Weighing lysimeter: grapevine Kc is a linear function of the percent shaded area under the canopy (about 0.017 per % shade).

methods.data_needed:
- S-2 L2A 10 m red and NIR per parcel for all months (stats only; SR not needed for the balance).
- Parcel row spacing and inter-row management.
- Optionally IGN BD ORTHO 20 cm once per parcel for canopy width and row geometry (F3 Z15).
methods.feasible_in_colab_gee: Yes. Change the ingest month filter for a 10 m stats-only path; the SR path stays IV-X. Monthly and phenological-window composites per parcel are cheap in GEE.
methods.expected_gain: Removes the saturation and the circular damping of drought found in the prototype. Lets real vigour differences between the 15 parcels enter physically: vine Kcb_mid derived from S-2 ranged 0.42-0.74 across years at one parcel. Kcb then matches the FAO and rainfed-literature range (0.60-0.65 mid-season).
methods.risks:
- NDVI_bg, NDVI_full, ML and Kcb_full for VSP vines are not verified; Rallo et al. 2021 tables were not retrieved.
- Row orientation and spacing effects.
- Missing vines (Roux 2025 found methods work best without them).
- Evergreen weeds in winter bias the cover-crop signal.

methods.name: M4. Parcel TAW/TTSW: soil-map prior with an uncertainty ensemble, then inverse calibration from cheap vine observations
methods.description:
1. Prior:
- French national AWC map (Roman Dobarco et al. 2019, GlobalSoilMap 90 m, with uncertainty; dataset DOI 10.15454/9IRARJ), downloaded once and clipped to the parcels; or
- OpenLandMap water content at 33 and 1500 kPa at 6 depths, 250 m, available in GEE.
2. Combine with a rooting depth of 1.0-2.0 m into a 5-member TAW ensemble (p10-p90). Run M1 for each member and publish FTSW and stress days as a band.
3. Calibrate per parcel once observations exist:
- Gaudin et al. 2017 slope method: in dry summers, the change in predawn water potential is linear in cumulative ET0 with a slope proportional to Kcb/TTSW;
- or the inverse modelling of Roux et al. 2025 from ApeX shoot-growth scores, weather and S-2 (MAE 30 mm, under 1 h of fieldwork per plot).
4. Station check: the ISMN texture (clay 45%, sand 13%) with the Saxton and Rawls 2006 pedotransfer function gives theta_FC 0.41 and theta_WP 0.27.
methods.why_better_than_ndvi_only:
In the prototype, TAW is the dominant parcel-specific parameter. TAW +-30% or Zr 0.9-1.6 m moved summer stress days by 10-30 per season, while SR vs 10 m moved FTSW by at most 0.006.

Pellegrino 2004: FTSW is a valid indicator of vine water deficit only if TTSW is correctly estimated.

NDVI-only monitoring cannot express soil water capacity at all, yet capacity explains most between-parcel differences in vine water status (Gaudillere 2002: soil differences persist whatever the year).

evidence.citation: Own prototype sensitivity (run_vineyard.py, run_dual.py)
evidence.finding: Days with FTSW < 0.4 in VI-IX, 2016-2025: Zr=0.9 m (TAW 126 mm) gives 83-118; Zr=1.6 m (TAW 224 mm) gives 70-122. TAW x0.7 vs x1.3 moved 2016 from 122 to 103 days and 2023 from 116 to 94 days.

evidence.citation: Pellegrino A. et al. 2004/2005. Plant and Soil 266:129-142
evidence.finding: A single relationship between predawn potential and FTSW for two Syrah vineyards and two years, similar to Lebon 2003. FTSW is usable as a deficit indicator provided TTSW is correctly estimated. The lower TTSW limit lies above -1.5 MPa water content except in the top 0-0.2 m.

evidence.citation: Gaudin R. et al. 2017. Agric. Water Manag. 182:13-23
evidence.finding: Changes in predawn potential are linear in cumulative ET0 during dry Mediterranean summers, with a slope related to Kcb/TTSW. This gives site-specific Kcb/TTSW (49 sites per vineyard; Shiraz 2003, Mourvedre 2005).

evidence.citation: Roux et al. 2025. Agric. Water Manag. (HAL hal-05223516): Retrieving total transpirable soil water in a rainfed vineyard using vine shoot growth, weather, and Sentinel-2 data
evidence.finding: Inverse modelling of TTSW on 6 rainfed plots in southern France: MAE 30 mm vs benchmark methods, lower uncertainty than the soil-based benchmark, under 1 h fieldwork per plot. Best without dead or missing vines. Author list not verified.

evidence.citation: Roman Dobarco M. et al. 2019. Geoderma 344:14-30; OpenLandMap water content at 33/1500 kPa (Hengl and Gupta 2019) in the Earth Engine catalogue
evidence.finding: French AWC with an uncertainty assessment (GlobalSoilMap specification, dataset 10.15454/9IRARJ). OpenLandMap gives volumetric water content at 33 and 1500 kPa at 0-200 cm, 250 m, as GEE assets.

evidence.citation: TTSW ranges reported for French and European vineyards (search snippets: Gruber and Schultz; OENO One 2019 scenarios; Rivesaltes study)
evidence.finding: TTSW of 50-175 mm across three vineyards with a common predawn-FTSW relation; 100/200/300 mm scenarios; 145 mm measured at Rivesaltes. 100-300 mm is the plausible span.

methods.data_needed:
- AWC raster: OpenLandMap in GEE, or the RUM France raster downloaded once to Drive.
- ISMN texture: already present.
- Later: 4-6 predawn water potential dates per parcel in a dry summer, or weekly ApeX scores (pilot).
methods.feasible_in_colab_gee: Yes. Sampling OpenLandMap in GEE is trivial. The RUM raster is a one-off download and clip in Colab. Inverse calibration is a 1-D optimisation per parcel with scipy.
methods.expected_gain: Turns the largest unknown into an explicit uncertainty band on the card. After calibration, parcel-specific stress timing improves: a TTSW error of about 30 mm (Roux 2025) corresponds to roughly a week of onset uncertainty, versus about a month for an uncalibrated +-30% TAW.
methods.risks:
- 90-250 m soil maps cannot resolve parcels inside one cooperative.
- Vine roots in fractured molasse or limestone go deeper than the mapped soil.
- Predawn potential is not equal to soil water potential in wet soil (Groenveld 2023).
- ApeX is not specific to water (Pichon 2023).
methods.validation_plan:
At SMOSMANIA stations, compare TAW priors (pedotransfer from ISMN texture, OpenLandMap, RUM France) by dry-onset MAE and anomaly R.

In the pilot, use leave-one-date-out and leave-one-parcel-out tests of TTSW calibrated from predawn potential, reporting the TTSW error in mm and the error in onset date.

methods.name: M5. Phenology-aware vine water-stress index, FTSW anomaly and days-to-stress forecast inside the EDO-style status
methods.why_better_than_ndvi_only:
Vine water deficit is judged by timing. A moderate deficit after veraison is often desired, and the same anomaly means different things for different wine targets (F3 on Laroche-Pinel 2021). The NDVI anomaly cannot separate a desired moderate deficit from damage, and it reacts late.

The index expresses stress in the units viticulturists use, keeps the EDO cascade with observed impact as the last tier, and gives lead time through the forecast.

evidence.citation: Gaudin R., Kansou K., Payan J.C., Pellegrino A., Gary C. 2014. J. Int. Sci. Vigne Vin 48:1-9
evidence.finding: Covers 102 site-variety-vintage situations, mostly rainfed. Uses a daily single-reservoir FTSW model with five deficit classes from decreasing FTSW thresholds over four periods between flowering and harvest, anchored to predawn potential. The resulting index correlated with yield per vine, berry weight, sugar and acids (not anthocyanins). Winter FTSW simulation is the main weakness.

evidence.citation: EDO Combined Drought Indicator factsheet v4.1.1 (JRC 2026), user-supplied full text summarised in docs/evidence/F3
evidence.finding: Alert is based on a vegetation (fAPAR) anomaly as the impact tier, with persistence and transition classes. Combining precipitation, soil and vegetation reduces false alarms.

evidence.citation: Mira s-Avalos J.M. et al. 2024. Agric. For. Meteorol. 359:110281
evidence.finding: A vineyard soil water-balance model converting FTSW to midday stem potential was validated in 129 Spanish scenarios. It reproduced the seasonal course while slightly overestimating. The most sensitive parameter was the FTSW at which stomatal conductance starts to decline.

evidence.citation: FTSW and predawn-potential classes (Riou and Payan 2001 via secondary source; Carbonneau classes via DPIRD extension sheet)
evidence.finding: FTSW > 0.4: no stress; 0.21-0.40: weak; 0.07-0.21: moderate; < 0.07: strong. Predawn classes start at 0 to -0.2 MPa (no deficit). Exact cut-offs are to be confirmed in the originals.

evidence.citation: Own prototype run_dual.py
evidence.finding: Modelled onset dates of FTSW < 0.4 vary between years (01 June to 13 July). The VI-IX mean FTSW z vs 1991-2020 ranked 2017, 2019 and 2023 driest and 2018 and 2024 wettest. At season level (n=9), FTSW z, NDVI z and ERA5-RZ z are statistically indistinguishable (Spearman with ISMN 0.65, 0.64 and 0.77).

methods.data_needed:
- M1 outputs.
- Degree days from ERA5 Tmean.
- 10-day forecast precipitation and ET0 (Open-Meteo is already in step_06).
- Optional per parcel: cultivar and production target (Plan_v6 card attribute).
methods.feasible_in_colab_gee: Yes, CPU-only. New card fields: ftsw, ftsw_z, vine_stress_class, stress_index_by_phase, days_to_stress, ftsw_band.
methods.expected_gain:
An alert expressed in vine terms with phase and timing. It separates 'dry soil' from 'vine stress in a sensitive phase' and adds 1-10 days of lead time.

At station level the timing skill is proven (onset MAE 14-20 d); skill against vine status is not yet proven.
methods.risks:
- Threshold values are not verified: the Gaudin 2014 cut-offs were not retrieved, and FTSW 0.4 comes from secondary sources.
- Cultivar hydraulic behaviour differs (Colombard, Ugni blanc and Tannat in Gers).
- Forecast precipitation skill is limited.
- Users may read 'stress' as 'damage'; keep the F3 Z7 card wording.

methods.name: M6. Depth-matched ERA5-Land soil layer (0-28 cm) as the operational soil-warning layer, plus multi-station validation with QC-4 applied
methods.description:
1. Compute SMA from ERA5-L layers 1-2 (0-28 cm, thickness-weighted 7/21) alongside 0-100 cm.
2. Use 0-28 cm, or the M1 FTSW z, in 'warning'; keep 0-100 cm on the card.
3. This extends F3 proposal Z8 from a validation fix to an operational choice, now with a significance test.
4. Validate at all SMOSMANIA stations, applying the QC-4 contact-loss flag (documented in Condom_QC.md but not implemented in qc_insitu).
5. Metrics: R with a paired block bootstrap, Spearman, dekadal POD/FAR/CSI, and dry-onset MAE.
methods.why_better_than_ndvi_only: It improves the soil tier that every vineyard shares, which is the cheapest gain available. At Condom it beats both the current 0-100 cm layer and the FAO-56 bucket on daily anomalies.

evidence.citation: Own analysis paired_diff.py and run_station.py (ISMN Condom 20-30 cm, 2016-2024)
evidence.finding: ERA5-L 0-28 cm: R=0.691 vs 0.583 for 0-100 cm; dR=+0.108 [+0.049,+0.167] (paired 30-day block bootstrap, n=2976). Onset MAE 37 d vs 66 d. Dekadal events at z <= -1: POD 0.47 vs 0.57, FAR 0.59 vs 0.57, so event skill did not improve.

evidence.citation: docs/evidence/Condom_QC.md (QC-4) and own check of daily minima
evidence.finding: 20 and 30 cm sensors read 0.01-0.07 m3/m3 for 70-205 days per year (2017: 205 days below 0.15 at 20 cm) in a soil with 45% clay, where the pedotransfer wilting point is about 0.27. This is contact loss in shrink-swell clay, so summer reference values are censored.

evidence.citation: Nunez-Ibarra et al. 2025, EGUsphere preprint (summarised in F3 from full text)
evidence.finding: ERA5-Land is the best of 4 gridded products for root-zone dynamics. Absolute values can carry tens-of-percent bias, so work on anomalies and use Spearman on deseasonalised series.

methods.data_needed: Already available: ERA5-L layers 1-2 and ISMN Condom. For the other SMOSMANIA stations, ERA5-L point series from GEE (21 stations are in data/7_isismn_data).
methods.feasible_in_colab_gee: Yes. One line in step_04.era5_anomalies plus a QC-4 rule in step_07.qc_insitu. The multi-station run needs a GEE extraction loop.
methods.expected_gain: +0.11 R at Condom for anomaly tracking and earlier detection of drying onset.
methods.risks:
- Matching the sensor depth is not the vine root zone; ISMN Condom only goes to 30 cm.
- Event POD fell at the -1 threshold, so choose by a pre-registered metric.
- Single-station result until the multi-station run.
methods.validation_plan:
Pre-register R, dR with a paired bootstrap, and onset MAE as primary metrics, and POD/FAR/CSI as secondary.

Run on all SMOSMANIA stations with at least a 20 cm sensor and report the median and per-station results on the card. Switch operationally only if the median dR > 0 with a CI excluding 0.

methods.name: M7. Validation ladder for a vine water-stress product (what can be validated now and what needs the 2027 pilot)
methods.description:
Level A (now, free): ISMN Condom plus the SMOSMANIA network, to check forcing, bucket, TAW priors and timing (M1, M6). Use onset dates and event metrics that are robust to QC-4 censoring.

Level B (cheap, per parcel, retrospective):
- Cave de Condom harvest records per parcel (yield, sugar, acidity, harvest date) against the season stress index (Gaudin 2014 found such correlations).
- Must-sugar delta13C at harvest: one sample per parcel per year, from the cooperative's must samples. Lab cost of tens of euros per sample is an estimate, not verified.

Level C (2027 pilot, 3-5 parcels):
- Weekly predawn water potential (pressure chamber) from flowering to harvest.
- ApeX iG-Apex scores weekly (under 1 h per plot), which also feed the Roux 2025 / Gaudin 2017 TTSW calibration (M4).
- Check whether the national ApeX crowdsourced dataset (2019-2025, 11,481 fields) contains Gers fields.

Out of scope: sap flow and eddy covariance in the vineyard (cost). ICOS crop towers can only check ET0/ETa machinery (Plan_v5).
methods.why_better_than_ndvi_only: Today the vegetation layer is validated only against soil moisture, an indirect target. This ladder validates against vine-physiology targets (predawn potential, delta13C, shoot growth, yield) and makes the alert defensible to EO and viticulture experts.

evidence.citation: Gaudillere J.P., van Leeuwen C., Ollat N. 2002. J. Exp. Bot. (carbon isotope composition of grape sugars)
evidence.finding: Must-sugar delta13C correlates significantly with summer predawn potential. It ranges from -20 to -26 per mil from dry to wet ripening conditions, and soil-related differences between plots persist across years. A companion 2001 study found R2 = 0.81 (n=36) with minimum predawn potential.

evidence.citation: Pichon L. et al. 2023, OENO One (iG-Apex vs predawn potential, 55 fields, Tavel 2008-2012); Ogoumond, Tisseyre, Pichon 2026, OENO One (summarised by Vinetur)
evidence.finding: iG-Apex is usable for field-scale monitoring over about -0.2 to -0.8 MPa predawn but is not specific to water. The national ApeX app collected 34,233 observations on 11,481 fields between 2019 and 2025.

evidence.citation: Gaudin et al. 2014 (as in M5)
evidence.finding: A water-balance FTSW stress index correlates with yield, berry weight, sugar and acids across 102 situations, so harvest data are a valid retrospective target.

evidence.citation: Groenveld T. et al. 2023. BMC Plant Biol. (summarised in F3)
evidence.finding: Predawn leaf water potential is lower than soil water potential in wet soil for 30 cultivars, so a predawn-to-FTSW calibration is reliable mainly in dry conditions.

methods.data_needed:
- Level A: ERA5-L and S-2 per SMOSMANIA station from GEE.
- Level B: cooperative records and must samples.
- Level C: pressure chamber (rent or borrow), observer time, ApeX app.
methods.feasible_in_colab_gee: Level A is fully feasible now. B and C are data-access and fieldwork tasks; the analysis code is a small addition to step_07.validate_anomalies (new references with reference=PSI_PD, D13C, APEX).
methods.expected_gain: The first quantitative link between AgriWatch status and vine water status. Claims on the card become testable numbers instead of literature thresholds.
methods.risks:
- delta13C integrates only veraison to harvest.
- Cultivar differences.
- Access to cooperative data.
- Small n per season.
- ApeX is not specific to water.

not_recommended: Mapping same-season whole-pixel NDVI to Kcb (e.g. Campos 1.44*NDVI-0.10, or Allen-Pereira on raw vineyard NDVI) in grassed rainfed vineyards. In the prototype it saturated (FTSW < 0.4 from early June every year) and damped the drought signal (2022 Kcb_mid 0.42 vs 0.74 in 2021). Literature agrees that VI-based Kcb overestimates under stress (Campos 2012; Almeida 2024).

Selling the water balance as 'more accurate soil moisture'. At Condom the bucket's dR vs ERA5-L RZ was +0.04 with a CI spanning 0, and it was significantly worse than ERA5-L 0-28 cm (dR -0.066 [-0.104, -0.027]). Its value is vine units, timing, parcel parameters and forecasts.

Using SR 2.5 m as an input to the water balance. It changed FTSW by at most 0.006 and S-2 Kcb added only +0.015 R over a climatological Kcb. Spend effort on TAW and Kcb design instead; keep SR for maps.

Absolute FTSW thresholds (e.g. 0.4) as alarms before TAW and Kcb are calibrated. The uncalibrated model flags stress every summer; use FTSW anomaly, phase-specific ranks and uncertainty bands until pilot data exist.

Hargreaves (especially with Tmax approximated as 2*Tmean - Tmin) as the operational ET0 when ERA5-Land provides all Penman-Monteith inputs. Keep it only as a calibrated gap-filler. Do not use the ERA5-Land potential_evaporation variable as ET0; it is not FAO-56 reference ET (own knowledge, unverified here).

Thermal energy-balance ET (TSEB / Sen-ET / DisALEXI) as the core for 0.7-4 ha parcels in Gers now. GRAPEX-type successes rely on towers, UAV or Landsat-scale fusion, and F3 already found Sen-ET parcel errors too large. Revisit with TRISHNA or LSTM thermal missions, or as the Landsat check in F3 Z13.

Full per-parcel calibration of SIMDualKc, AquaCrop or STICS without field data. These are over-parameterised (equifinality); a WaLIS/Gaudin-level two-compartment or single-reservoir FTSW model is the defensible complexity.

Calibrating Kcb or TAW on the ISMN grass plot and transferring them to vines. The station only validates forcing and bucket machinery; its 20-30 cm summer values are also censored by contact loss (QC-4).

Validating any summer vine-stress product on raw ISMN 20-30 cm July-September values without QC-4. Sensors read 0.01-0.07 m3/m3 in 45% clay for 70-205 days per year; use onset dates and wet-season anomalies instead.

research.direction: Remote sensing of vine water status beyond NDVI. Covers SWIR and red-edge indices and CCC/CWC retrieval, separating the vine canopy from the grassed inter-row (including whether 2.5 m SR is fine enough), thermal at the scale of a 3 ha parcel, and phenology-aware anomaly baselines. Each option is judged against the AgriWatch v1.0 baseline using free data in Colab and GEE.
research.summary:
This answer builds on F3 (Z1-Z15) and does not repeat it. I re-ran the v1.0 validation on the local Drive registry and ISMN files. The baseline reproduces exactly: SR NDVI anomaly vs ISMN 20-30 cm R=0.433 [0.242,0.594], n=245; ERA5-L root zone R=0.583 [0.500,0.665], n=2976. I then tested about 20 alternatives on the same days with a paired block bootstrap (30-day blocks, 1000 resamples). Scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-1-geoworldlook-agriscreen/0b6bc240-34e1-5fd3-a139-3c46967fd603/scratchpad/exp/ (common.py, e0_baseline.py, e3_phenology.py, e4_orbit.py, e5_orbit_strat.py, e6_alerts.py, e7_lag.py, e8_cross_index.py). The repo was not modified.

Main findings:

(1) No Sentinel-2 index tracks root-zone soil moisture better than NDVI, and none adds anything to ERA5. Partial r given ERA5 RZ (the extra information an index carries once ERA5 is known) is n.s. for every index: SR NDVI 0.106 [-0.108,0.298], NDMI 0.094, NDRE 0.077, CRSWIR -0.048, NDMI/NDVI -0.015. SWIR indices with the best baseline are not better than plain NDVI: ΔR(NDMI) = +0.016 [-0.054,+0.071]; ΔR(CRSWIR) = -0.016 [-0.099,+0.050]. Over time, ERA5 already contains what S-2 says about soil moisture at Condom. The only real value S-2 can add is parcel-specific (cross-sectional), and one station cannot validate that.

(2) New and real: acquisition geometry biases the vineyard anomaly. The two relative orbits (about 10:59 and 11:08 UTC) disagree. In 108 pairs of scenes from different orbits taken at most 3 days apart (VI-IX), vineyard NDVI differs by -0.035±0.031 (p=5e-21). The station grass plot shows no such effect (-0.007, p=0.07). In VI-IX this gives a 0.52 z offset between orbits (+0.31 vs -0.21) and asymmetric z≤-1 counts (23 vs 12). It is consistent with row-structure directional effects (CESBIO; Sozzi 2019). A climatology split by orbit removes the bias (+0.05/+0.04); R is unchanged (ΔR -0.012, n.s.), and 28 of 29 historical alerts survive.

(3) A per-parcel harmonic baseline, fitted on the other years (FORDEAD-like), gives a small but significant paired gain for SWIR indices: NDMI ΔR +0.039 [+0.010,+0.065]; CRSWIR +0.047 [+0.019,+0.071]. NDVI gains +0.011 (n.s.) in IV-X and +0.044 [-0.021,+0.094] in VI-IX. Three other baselines give no gain:
   - thermal-time (GDD) alignment: 0.410 vs 0.430;
   - Whittaker smoothing: 0.419;
   - 30-day trailing composite: 0.408.
   No lag improves the fit either: the best match is with the concurrent 30-day mean of ISMN (r≈0.49-0.51 in VI-IX), falling to 0.31 at a 60-day lag.

(4) The inter-row signal is large. In summer the vineyard NDVI anomaly correlates with the station grass plot (136 m away) at r=0.70 (VI-VII) and 0.79 (VIII-X), against 0.20 in IV-V. The vineyard keeps some information of its own: partial r(vineyard, ISMN | grass) = 0.25 [0.04,0.44]. Raw vineyard NDVI falls from 0.50 in April to 0.445 in May, which reflects inter-row management.

(5) 2.5 m SR cannot isolate rows. Rows 2.2-3 m apart are a 0.33-0.45 cycles/m pattern. That is 7-9 times above the 10 m Nyquist frequency (0.05 c/m), where the S2 MTF is already only 0.15-0.3, and 2.5 m sampling would itself alias it (it would need ≤1.1-1.5 m). Paired R for 10 m and SR is identical (0.426 vs 0.433).

(6) Under the current design the CI on R is ±0.18, so no improvement can be shown unless results are paired. Paired ΔR CIs are about ±0.03-0.06 for the same index and ±0.06-0.13 across indices. In the literature, S-2 vs Ψstem R² ranges from 0.40 (Laroche-Pinel 2021, 36 plots) to 0.72 (single vineyard). These are mostly within-season covariation, not anomaly skill. Thermal is the physiologically direct signal, but at 2.9 ha a Landsat TIRS pixel (100 m) gives only about 3 footprints, dominated by the inter-row surface. The decisive gap is truth for vine water status: δ13C of must per parcel (R²=0.81 with predawn Ψ in Bordeaux) and ApeX shoot-growth observations are cheap and suit a cooperative of 15 vineyards.

Correction to F3 Z14: S-2 ingestion is limited to IV-X (S2_MONTHS=(4,10)). The 'winter background' increment cannot run on the current data until ingestion of XI-III is enabled.

methods.name: M1. Anomaly baseline aware of geometry and phenology: per-parcel harmonic model, other years only, plus orbit term
methods.description: Replace the pooled 'other years ±15 DOY' z-score in step_04.scene_anomaly with a per-parcel, per-index harmonic model, fitted with each scene's own year left out. Model: v = a0 + a1·cos ωt + b1·sin ωt + a2·cos 2ωt + b2·sin 2ωt + c·orbit. With more parcels, use geometry covariates from GEE metadata instead of the orbit dummy: SENSING_ORBIT_NUMBER, MEAN_INCIDENCE_ZENITH/AZIMUTH_ANGLE_B8, and the solar angles, optionally crossed with row azimuth from M4. z = residual / SD of training residuals, so every z carries the parcel's own noise level, which serves as an uncertainty for the dashboard. A simpler fallback is a DOY climatology split by orbit. This targets two concrete defects. First, the pooled climatology mixes two viewing geometries over a row-structured canopy, which shifts z by about 0.5 SD between orbits. Second, the SD of a pooled z estimated from about 5-15 reference scenes is noisy.
methods.why_better_than_ndvi_only:
This is not a new index. It fixes the error model for any index, including NDVI. Measured locally:
- Orbit bias: VI-IX mean z +0.31 (late orbit) vs -0.21 (early orbit) with the pooled baseline; +0.05 / +0.04 when split by orbit.
- Paired ΔR vs the pooled baseline: NDMI +0.039 [+0.010,+0.065]; CRSWIR +0.047 [+0.019,+0.071]; NDVI +0.011 (IV-X, n.s.) and +0.044 [-0.021,+0.094] (VI-IX).
It also makes the SWIR indices from Z11/Z14 usable: with the pooled baseline they lose to NDVI, with the harmonic one they are on par.

evidence.citation: Own computation, not literature: e4_orbit.py on gwl_observations.csv (VINEYARD_06 vs SMOSMANIA_Condom_poly, S2_10m, VI-IX 2016-2026)
evidence.finding: 108 pairs of scenes from different orbits ≤3 days apart: vineyard NDVI early minus late = -0.035 ± 0.031 (t-test p=4.7e-21). Grass plot: -0.007 (p=0.066). Pooled z by orbit in VI-IX: -0.205 vs +0.312. Scenes with z≤-1: 23 in the early orbit vs 12 in the late orbit.

evidence.citation: Own computation, not literature: e5_orbit_strat.py / e8_cross_index.py, paired block bootstrap vs ISMN 20-30 cm z (n=245 days)

CESBIO MultiTemp blog (Hagolle et al.), '[Directional effects] Effects of crop orientation on surface reflectance' and 'Validation of DART simulations of vineyards using VENµS multi-angular observations'
evidence.finding: Row orientation relative to sun and view changes vineyard reflectance and NDVI by sometimes >10% relative. Vineyards are the worst case because of wide row spacing. DART reproduces the effect.

evidence.citation: Sozzi M., Kayad A., Sartori L., Marinello F. (2019) Evaluation of shadow effects in satellite images of vineyards with different row orientation (conference), HAL hal-02610140
evidence.finding: 48 vineyards with S2, RapidEye and Pleiades vs UAV pure-vine data. Off-nadir view had a stronger effect than solar shading. Adding geometry terms raised regression R² by 13.4% for Sentinel-2.

evidence.citation: Dutrieux R. et al. (2021) / FORDEAD python package (INRAE UMR TETIS), Zenodo record 12802457
evidence.finding: A per-pixel seasonal model trained on the first years of the S-2 archive; anomaly = departure of observed index from the predicted seasonal trajectory; designed for CRSWIR. That the model is a two-harmonic periodic function is from my memory, not verified in these sources.

methods.data_needed: Already available: gwl_observations S2SR_2.5m / S2_10m per scene. Add per-scene metadata from GEE at ingest (SENSING_ORBIT_NUMBER, MEAN_INCIDENCE_ZENITH/AZIMUTH_ANGLE_B8A, MEAN_SOLAR_ZENITH/AZIMUTH_ANGLE); for now the UTC time is a proxy. Optional: row azimuth per parcel from M4.
methods.feasible_in_colab_gee: Yes, fully. It is pure pandas/numpy in step_04 plus 5 metadata fields in step_01 ingest. No new downloads and no extra GPU/SR.
methods.expected_gain: Correctness: removes a systematic ±0.25 z bias tied to the orbit, so alerts no longer depend on which satellite track saw the parcel. Skill vs soil moisture: about +0.01 for NDVI (n.s.) and +0.04-0.05 for NDMI/CRSWIR (significant when paired). Every z gets a defensible per-parcel uncertainty. Does not turn S-2 into a better soil-moisture tracker than ERA5.
methods.risks:
- The harmonic fit only sees IV-X, so the edges of the season (April, late October) are extrapolated. Check residuals by month.
- Splitting by orbit roughly halves n_ref.
- Geometry effects depend on row azimuth, so the orbit coefficient must be per parcel, not shared across the 15 vineyards.
- Leave-one-year-out lets future years enter the baseline, which is fine for a retrospective climatology but must be frozen (e.g. 2016-2025) for operations.
- Gains are small and could be site-specific: replicate on the other 14 vineyards before claiming them.
methods.validation_plan:
Write these criteria down before running:
(a) Geometry test: in pairs ≤3 days from different orbits, the mean z difference between orbits must fall from 0.52 to <0.1.
(b) Non-inferiority vs ISMN 20-30 cm z: paired ΔR lower CI bound > -0.03 for NDVI. Adopt for NDMI/CRSWIR only if the lower bound > 0. Report partial r given ERA5.
(c) Stability: the number of dekad-to-dekad class flips must not increase.
(d) On all 15 vineyards: the size of the orbit bias should vary with row azimuth from M4, which serves as a physical plausibility check.

methods.name: M2. Validation redesign: paired skill differences, ERA5-conditional value and a vine-water-status truth (δ13C of must, ApeX shoot growth, small Ψstem campaign)
methods.description:
Make improvements measurable, and measure the right thing.
(i) In step_07.validate_anomalies, report ΔR between candidate and baseline on the same days with a block-bootstrap CI, partial r given ERA5 RZ, Spearman, and a 30-day-mean ISMN target alongside the same-day target.
(ii) Replicate the soil-moisture test on other SMOSMANIA stations: extract S-2 statistics around each station in GEE. These are mostly grass plots, so this tests indices generally, not vines.
(iii) Add parcel-level truth for the 15 vineyards, which is the only way to validate what S-2 uniquely provides (cross-parcel differences):
- δ13C of must sugars at harvest per parcel per vintage. It integrates water stress from véraison to harvest, the cooperative can sample it, and lab cost is low.
- ApeX-Vigne shoot-tip observations: a free app; growers or advisors spend about 10 min per parcel per week from flowering to véraison.
- Optionally 3-4 dates of Ψstem with a borrowed pressure chamber (IFV / Chambre d'agriculture du Gers) on 3-5 contrasting parcels.
methods.why_better_than_ndvi_only: Today the vegetation layer is validated against soil moisture, an indirect target where ERA5 already explains everything S-2 can: partial r given ERA5 ≈ 0.1, n.s., for all indices. Unpaired CIs are ±0.18, so no index or baseline could ever be shown to beat NDVI; paired CIs shrink to ±0.03-0.13. A δ13C or ApeX ranking across 15 parcels tests the parcel-specific claim that EO experts will actually question.

evidence.citation: Own computation, not literature: e0_baseline.py and e8_cross_index.py
evidence.finding: Unpaired 95% CI of R for SR NDVI is [0.242,0.594], about ±0.18. Paired ΔR CI is about ±0.03-0.05 for the same index under different baselines, and ±0.06-0.13 across indices. Partial r(S2 index, ISMN | ERA5 RZ) ranges from -0.05 to 0.11 at VINEYARD_06, all n.s. Using the 30-day mean of ISMN as target lifts r from 0.488 to 0.506 (VI-IX).

evidence.citation: Gaudillère J.-P., van Leeuwen C., Trégoat O. (2001) The assessment of vine water uptake conditions by 13C/12C discrimination in grape sugar, J. Int. Sci. Vigne Vin; Gaudillère, van Leeuwen, Ollat (2002) J. Exp. Bot. 53:757
evidence.finding: Δ13C of grape sugar at ripeness vs minimum predawn leaf water potential: R²=0.81, n=36. Soil-driven differences between parcels persist whatever the annual water balance. Genotype also affects the value, so parcels must be compared within a cultivar.

evidence.citation: van Leeuwen C. et al. (2009) Vine water status is a key factor in grape ripening and vintage quality for red Bordeaux wine. J. Int. Sci. Vigne Vin 43(3):121-134
evidence.finding: Stem water potential and sugar δ13C are both reliable at plot scale; δ13C is the cheap, integrative option.

evidence.citation: Pichon L., Tisseyre B. et al. ApeX-Vigne / iG-Apex (OENO One 2022, HAL hal-04050137; 2024 Ψpd prediction from iG-Apex + weather)
evidence.finding: A free app for shoot-growth observations. iG-Apex was usable to monitor vine water status at field scale over 55 fields (Tavel, 2008-2012) against Ψpd. The authors say it is not specific to water constraint. Thousands of crowdsourced observations exist for 2019-2021.

methods.data_needed:
- Existing: ISMN Condom and the gwl registry.
- Other SMOSMANIA stations: .stm files are already in data/7_isismn_data; S-2 must be extracted in GEE.
- Field: about 15 must samples per vintage (sugar δ13C, commercial isotope lab); ApeX observations; optional Ψstem.
methods.feasible_in_colab_gee: Statistics: yes (step_07 only). Multi-station extraction: yes (existing extract_satellite pattern in GEE). Field truth: needs the cooperative's agreement and about one season; no EO cost.
methods.expected_gain:
Does not change the indices. It changes what can be claimed.
- Detectable ΔR improves from about ±0.18 to ±0.05.
- With 15 parcels, a Spearman ρ ≥ 0.52 (two-sided, α=0.05) between seasonal S-2 anomaly and δ13C would be the first direct evidence that the vegetation layer sees vine water status.
This is the step that makes the work defensible to EO and viticulture experts.
methods.risks:
- One vintage gives only n=15 parcels, so expect wide uncertainty; plan 2-3 vintages.
- δ13C differs by cultivar (Ugni Blanc, Colombard, etc.): compare within cultivar or add a cultivar effect.
- ApeX depends on grower diligence.
- Other SMOSMANIA sites are not vineyards.
- A negative result is possible and must be published as such.

methods.name: M3. Cross-sectional parcel anomaly: double difference against the other AOI vineyards on the same date
methods.description: For each scene, subtract the AOI median of the same anomaly (M1 z) across the 15 vineyards, optionally weighted, from the parcel's own anomaly. The result is a relative anomaly: 'this vineyard is drier or browner than its neighbours today'. Show it next to the absolute temporal anomaly, not in its place. The double difference cancels common-mode terms: regional weather, which ERA5 already captures; residual atmospheric correction and thin-cloud errors; and, for parcels with similar row azimuth, part of the geometry effect. FORDEAD uses the same idea with a correction factor from the median of large stands.
methods.why_better_than_ndvi_only: All 15 vineyards share one ERA5 cell, so their parcel-specific information is the cross-sectional part. Locally, the common mode is strong: in summer the vineyard NDVI anomaly correlates with the grass plot 136 m away at r=0.70 (VI-VII) and r=0.79 (VIII-X). The current anomaly is therefore dominated by a signal ERA5 already provides. The relative anomaly isolates what is genuinely new, such as soil water-holding capacity, rootstock, vigour or inter-row management.

evidence.citation: Own computation, not literature: e0_baseline.py (E2)
evidence.finding: r(vineyard NDVI z, grass-plot NDVI z) on the same days: IV-V 0.20 (n=57), VI-VII 0.70 (n=73), VIII-X 0.79 (n=112). Partial r(vineyard, ISMN | grass) = 0.254 [0.043,0.437]; partial r(grass, ISMN | vineyard) = 0.176 [-0.002,0.359].

evidence.citation: FORDEAD documentation (INRAE TETIS), via Theia blog
evidence.finding: Optionally corrects the vegetation index with a factor computed from the median of the index over large stands of interest, which removes common-mode variation.

evidence.citation: Gaudillère et al. 2002 (see M2)
evidence.finding: Differences in water status between parcels driven by soil persist across years whatever the annual water balance. This supports testing whether S-2 parcel rankings repeat across dry years.

methods.data_needed: Scene statistics for all 15 vineyards; the pipeline already supports this via MONITOR_CONFIG VINEYARDS, though only VINEYARD_06 is in the local copy. Same clear-sky mask per date.
methods.feasible_in_colab_gee: Yes. Reuse task_scene_stats outputs; this is a few lines in step_04 and a new product, e.g. S2SR_2.5m_NDVI_REL, in gwl_anomalies.
methods.expected_gain: A new parcel-specific layer, 'vineyard worse than neighbours'. It cannot be validated at the station, because it removes exactly the regional soil-moisture signal. Its value has to be shown with M2 parcel truth or with repeatability of parcel ranks across dry years. Expect lower noise than the absolute anomaly because common-mode errors cancel.
methods.risks:
- In a uniform drought (2022, 2026) every parcel is stressed and the relative anomaly is about 0: never use it alone for alerts.
- With 15 parcels the median is robust, but a cluster of similar parcels can bias it.
- Parcels with different row azimuths keep different geometry residuals unless M1 covariates are used.
- Small parcels (0.68 ha) are noisier.
methods.validation_plan:
(a) Repeatability: Kendall W of the 15-parcel ranking over VII-VIII across 2019, 2022 and 2026, compared against a permutation null.
(b) After one vintage: Spearman with δ13C/ApeX (M2), threshold ρ ≥ 0.52.
(c) Noise: the dekad-to-dekad variance of the relative anomaly in wet years should be lower than that of the absolute anomaly.

methods.name: M4. Vine canopy vs inter-row: row geometry from IGN BD ORTHO (20 cm RGB+IRC, Etalab) with fixed-fraction and temporal unmixing
methods.description:
What 2.5 m SR cannot do (no row recovery), take from free VHR imagery:
(1) Download BD ORTHO RVB and IRC (colour infrared) tiles for the 15 parcels. With a local FFT or Gabor analysis (Delenne et al. 2008/2010), estimate row azimuth and inter-row width, and threshold an IRC greenness index to get the vine-canopy cover fraction fc_vine. Also measure the vine vs inter-row greenness contrast on the flight date.
(2) Use row azimuth as a geometry covariate in M1.
(3) Unmix S-2 (native 10 m for NDVI, 20 m for NDMI) into a vine part and an inter-row part. Fix fc_vine from the orthophoto and estimate the inter-row endmember dynamically: from the parcel's own XI-III signal when the vine is leafless (requires changing S2_MONTHS ingest to all months; 10 m is enough, no SR) and/or from nearby permanent grassland reference pixels. Solve vine = (R_parcel - (1-fc)·R_interrow)/fc.
(4) Report the inter-row anomaly as its own diagnostic: is the parcel anomaly vine or grass?
methods.why_better_than_ndvi_only:
Parcel NDVI in summer mixes vine (fc ≈ 0.3) with drying grass or soil. Locally, the parcel anomaly tracks the grass plot at r=0.7-0.8 in summer, and raw NDVI drops 0.50 → 0.445 from April to May through inter-row work. Separating the parts makes the alert interpretable (vine vs cover crop). It is the only way to approach a vine-only signal with free data.
On 2.5 m SR: rows 2.2-3 m apart are 0.33-0.45 cycles/m, 7-9 times above the 10 m Nyquist frequency (0.05 c/m), where the S2 MTF is already only 0.15-0.3. Super-resolution cannot restore that frequency, and 2.5 m sampling would alias it anyway, since it would need ≤1.1-1.5 m GSD and in practice ≥3-4 pixels per period. Locally, SR NDVI anomaly R=0.433 vs 10 m 0.426, identical.

evidence.citation: ESA Sentinel-2 MSI Technical Guide, Mission Performance
evidence.finding: System MTF at Nyquist is 0.15-0.3 for 10 m bands and <0.45 for 20/60 m bands, so there is essentially no signal at the row frequency (~0.4 c/m).

evidence.citation: Nguyen et al. (IGARSS 2023) On the role of alias and band-shift for Sentinel-2 super-resolution; L1BSR (arXiv 2304.06871)
evidence.finding: Real detail can only be recovered from aliasing and band shift, and the authors deliberately target ×2 (5 m), not ×4. Resolution is capped by the blur kernel of the sensor.

evidence.citation: Delenne C., Durrieu S., Rabatel G., Deshayes M. (2010) From pixel to vine parcel, Comput. Electron. Agric. 70:78-83; Delenne et al. 2008 local FFT
evidence.finding: Local FFT on VHR aerial images: 88% of 114 vine plots detected. Row orientation and inter-row width within 2° and 6 cm of manual measurements.

evidence.citation: De Petris S. et al. (2024) Comput. Electron. Agric. 222 (row/inter-row unmixing of S2 NDVI with UAV fractions, 21×21 moving-window least squares)
evidence.finding: MAE 0.15 (row) and 0.10 (inter-row) NDVI vs UAV; 16% relative error for vine NDVI. Shows that unmixing works only with external fraction maps and has substantial error.

evidence.citation: IGN Géoservices BD ORTHO; data.gouv.fr (Licence Ouverte Etalab 2.0, open since 1 Jan 2021)
evidence.finding: BD ORTHO is free at 20 cm in RGB and IRC (colour infrared) and refreshed every 3-4 years per département. Enough to resolve 2.2-3 m rows and measure fc_vine.

evidence.citation: Own computation, not literature: e0_baseline.py monthly medians (S2_10m, clear ≥0.9)
evidence.finding:
Median NDVI by month (IV→X):
- VINEYARD_06: 0.50, 0.445, 0.49, 0.49, 0.43, 0.44, 0.58;
- grass plot: 0.67, 0.70, 0.66, 0.55, 0.415, 0.42, 0.68.
The vineyard dip in May reflects inter-row management, not water.

methods.data_needed:
- BD ORTHO RVB+IRC tiles for Gers (one or two editions; check the vintage per département on geoservices.ign.fr).
- S-2 ingestion extended to XI-III at 10/20 m (change S2_MONTHS; no SR needed).
- Parcel polygons (existing).
- Optional permanent-grassland reference polygons near the AOI.
methods.feasible_in_colab_gee: Partly. Orthophotos are downloaded from IGN (7z tiles) into Colab/Drive, not GEE. FFT row detection runs on CPU with numpy/scipy. Winter S-2 comes through the existing GEE ingest with a config change. Unmixing is plain numpy.
methods.expected_gain: Interpretability first: a per-parcel label of whether the anomaly comes from vine or inter-row, plus fc_vine, row azimuth and spacing as permanent parcel attributes; these also feed M1 and M5. A gain for vine water stress detection is uncertain. Fixed-fraction unmixing amplifies errors by about 1/fc ≈ 3×, and the best published vine-NDVI error is about 0.15 MAE even with UAV fractions. Treat it as an experiment with a stated chance of a negative result.
methods.risks:
- The orthophoto is a single date every 3-4 years and the vineyard can change (replanting, missing vines).
- IRC radiometry is not calibrated, so use it for geometry and fc only.
- NDVI does not mix linearly in reflectance: unmix bands, then compute the index.
- Grass in the inter-row of a managed vineyard (mown, alternately tilled, shaded) differs from open grassland.
- Winter ingest adds scenes and GEE quota.
methods.validation_plan:
(a) Geometry: FFT azimuth and spacing vs manual measurement on 15 parcels (expect ≤3°, ≤10 cm).
(b) On the orthophoto flight date: does the S-2-unmixed vine minus inter-row contrast rank parcels like the orthophoto IRC contrast does (Spearman across 15 parcels)?
(c) At the station, the unmixed inter-row anomaly should correlate with ISMN 5 cm and 20-30 cm at least as well as the parcel anomaly does; the vine part is expected to correlate less, which is fine.
(d) Final test against δ13C/ApeX (M2).

methods.name: M5. Use S-2 as a parameter, not a detector: dual-component (vine + inter-row) water balance giving FTSW and a Ψpd proxy
methods.description:
Extends the existing Plan_v5 (single-crop FAO-56) to the structure that WineEO/Sat'Irr and WaLIS use. ERA5-Land drives a daily soil water balance with two transpiring components:
- vine: cover fc_vine from M4, Kcb from S-2;
- inter-row grass: cover and green fraction from the S-2 inter-row endmember of M4, including winter.
The grass competes for water in the topsoil. Outputs are FTSW and a predicted predawn Ψ through the published FTSW-Ψpd relation (Lebon 2003; Pellegrino 2006; stress threshold FTSW ≈ 0.4). S-2 enters through parcel parameters and covers, never as an anomaly threshold.
methods.why_better_than_ndvi_only: The local tests show S-2 adds no temporal information on soil moisture beyond ERA5 (partial r ≈ 0.1, n.s.), but S-2 is the only parcel-specific information. A model that combines ERA5 timing with S-2 parcel structure (how much vine and how much competing grass) produces a vine-relevant quantity in physical units, Ψpd/FTSW, rather than a z-score of greenness. That answers the 'NDVI is too simplistic' criticism directly.

evidence.citation: Own computation, not literature: e0_baseline.py (E0/E1)
evidence.finding: Partial r(S-2 index z, ISMN 20-30 cm z | ERA5 RZ z): NDVI 0.106 [-0.108,0.298]; NDMI 0.094; NDRE 0.077; CRSWIR -0.048. No S-2 index adds information on soil moisture over time.

evidence.citation: Celette F., Ripoche A., Gary C. (2010) WaLIS — a simple model to simulate water partitioning in a crop association: the example of an intercropped vineyard. Agric. Water Manag. 97:1749-1759
evidence.finding: Water balance model for vineyards with an intercrop (grass) in the inter-row, partitioning transpiration between vine and grass. Details are from my memory, not verified in this session.

evidence.citation: Lebon E. et al. (2003) Funct. Plant Biol. 30:699-710; Pellegrino A. et al. (2006) Eur. J. Agron. (cited in Plan_v5 L07/L08)
evidence.finding: Vineyard water balance with FTSW. FTSW ≈ 0.4 is the threshold for stomatal closure; FTSW is linked to predawn leaf water potential.

evidence.citation: ESA WineEO / TerraNIS Sat'Irr (Plan_v5 L01)
evidence.finding: Operational industry chain: water balance plus fCover from S-2, a dual balance for row and inter-row, at 2.5 m SR.

methods.data_needed:
- ERA5-Land daily with radiation, wind, dewpoint and Tmax for FAO-56 ET0. The current CSV lacks these; Tmax ≈ 2·Tmean − Tmin is only a stopgap for Hargreaves.
- SoilGrids for TAW.
- M4 outputs (fc_vine, inter-row endmember).
- ISMN profile 5-30 cm.
- M2 parcel truth.
methods.feasible_in_colab_gee: Yes. ERA5-Land variables come from GEE (ECMWF/ERA5_LAND/DAILY_AGGR); the balance runs in Colab (pyfao56, or a custom ~200-line dual-component model). No GPU.
methods.expected_gain: The largest potential gain in vine relevance: a daily parcel FTSW/Ψpd proxy with explicit inter-row competition. At the station, soil water at 0-30 cm should at least match ERA5 RZ (R 0.58). The real gain is at parcel scale and must be shown against δ13C/ApeX.
methods.risks:
- Overlaps the unapproved Plan_v5: decide jointly.
- Equifinality: many parameters (TAW, rooting depth, grass Kc, Ze) and only one soil-moisture profile, which is under grass, not vines.
- Precipitation errors dominate the balance.
- FTSW-Ψpd relations are cultivar- and site-dependent.
- The largest effort of all the options.
methods.validation_plan:
(a) Station: simulated 0-30 cm soil-water anomaly vs ISMN profile 5/10/20/30 cm weighted by layer thickness (F3 Z8). Paired ΔR vs ERA5 RZ alone, with KGE; also the timing of the first autumn rain event.
(b) Parcel: Spearman of simulated season-integrated stress (days with FTSW<0.4 between véraison and harvest) vs δ13C across 15 parcels, ρ ≥ 0.52.
(c) Sensitivity analysis on TAW and grass cover, reported with the result.

methods.name: M6. Thermal at parcel scale: Landsat 8/9 ΔT anomaly and WDI, with ECOSTRESS as an optional add-on; start with a go/no-go feasibility check
methods.description:
Step 0, a 0.5-day go/no-go in GEE: for 2013-2026, count Landsat 8/9 Collection-2 L2 scenes (ST_B10) in VI-IX that are clear over the parcel. Also count how many 100 m TIRS footprints lie fully inside each parcel after a 30-50 m inner buffer. 2.9 ha is about 3 footprints; the 30 m product is resampled, not independent.
If there are ≥6 clear scenes per year with ≥1 pure footprint, compute:
(a) ΔT = LST − Ta(ERA5-Land hourly at overpass), as an anomaly vs other years and cross-sectionally vs the AOI vineyards as in M3;
(b) Moran's WDI: a vegetation index-temperature trapezoid whose vertices come from ERA5-Land hourly radiation, VPD and wind, with fc from S-2. It is designed for partial cover, which suits vineyards with fc ≈ 0.3.
ECOSTRESS (70 m, variable overpass time, afternoon views useful for stress, since 2018) through NASA AppEEARS as an optional extra. Two-source energy balance partitioning (TSEB, GRAPEX-style) only as a research follow-up.
methods.why_better_than_ndvi_only: Canopy temperature responds to stomatal closure within hours to days, while NDVI and NDMI respond only after structural change. This is the only free-data channel that could see physiological stress before canopy damage. USDA/GRAPEX showed thermal ET capturing an imposed stress that reflectance-based ET missed. At 3 ha, however, the composite LST is dominated by the inter-row surface: dry soil and grass are 10-20 K warmer than the canopy. Without partitioning, ΔT mostly measures surface dryness, which ERA5 already has. Expect a gain only in severe events.

evidence.citation: NASA Landsat Science: Landsat thermal data provides insight to vintners (USDA ARS GRAPEX)
evidence.finding: Thermal bands picked up stress during critical periods of crop development that were not reflected in surface reflectance. At 30 m, fused thermal ET captured an imposed stress on 2 of 4 blocks that the reflectance-based ETc missed (California, large blocks).

evidence.citation: Knipper K. et al. (2019) Irrig. Sci. (GRAPEX DisALEXI data fusion, Pinot noir vineyards, CA); TSEB resolution study with UAV (3.6-30 m)
evidence.finding: Daily ET at 30 m from fusion with MAE 0.59 mm/d at flux sites. At Landsat 30 m, TSEB overestimated H and underestimated LE compared with finer grids, so separating vine transpiration from inter-row flux depends on pixel size.

evidence.citation: Moran M.S., Clarke T.R., Inoue Y., Vidal A. (1994) Estimating crop water deficit using the relation between surface-air temperature and spectral vegetation index. Remote Sens. Environ. 49:246-263
evidence.finding: WDI = 1 − ET/ETp from a trapezoid of Ts−Ta vs vegetation cover. It extends CWSI to partially vegetated fields without measuring foliage temperature.

evidence.citation: ECOSTRESS JPL news digest (April/May 2026); TRISHNA (CNES / Wikipedia); Copernicus LSTM (Airbus press)
evidence.finding:
- ECOSTRESS is approved through FY2026, with possible operations to FY2029 subject to the 2026 Senior Review.
- TRISHNA (57 m, ~3-day revisit) is planned for 2026/2027; sources disagree.
- LSTM (50 m, ~3 days) has its first launch targeted for about 2028.
Parcel-scale thermal becomes realistic with these missions.

evidence.citation: Bellvert J. et al. (2013/2014) CWSI of grapevine from airborne/ground thermal (cited in F3 Z13)
evidence.finding: CWSI vs leaf water potential R² ≈ 0.83 with canopy-only pixels. It needs calibration by phenological stage and cultivar, and it relies on pure canopy pixels that satellites cannot provide at 3 ha.

methods.data_needed:
- Landsat 8/9 C2 L2 (GEE: LANDSAT/LC08|LC09/C02/T1_L2, ST_B10, QA_PIXEL).
- ERA5-Land hourly (Ta, dewpoint, radiation, wind) at overpass (GEE ECMWF/ERA5_LAND/HOURLY).
- S-2 fc.
- Optional ECOSTRESS L2 LST through AppEEARS (Earthdata login). I believe it is not native in GEE, but this is unverified.
methods.feasible_in_colab_gee: The Landsat part is fully in GEE. ECOSTRESS needs the AppEEARS API from Colab. TSEB is possible with the pyTSEB package but is research-grade.
methods.expected_gain: Uncertain to low at 2.9 ha. My rough estimate is 4-8 clear VI-IX scenes per year before 2022 (L8 only) and about 8-15 from 2022 (L8+L9); this must be checked in step 0. Possible detection of severe heat-and-drought events (2022, 2026) a few weeks earlier than NDVI. Interpretation stays ambiguous between vine and inter-row without TSEB. Its most valuable output now may be the go/no-go result itself, plus readiness for TRISHNA/LSTM.
methods.risks:
- About 1 pure 100 m footprint per parcel: parcel edges, roads and woods contaminate it.
- Landsat passes about 10:30 local solar time, before the afternoon stress peak.
- Ta from a 9 km ERA5 cell can be biased; the cross-sectional differencing in M3 cancels that bias.
- ECOSTRESS geolocation and overpass times vary; future of the mission uncertain.
- Overlaps F3 Z13: merge, don't duplicate.
methods.validation_plan:
Go/no-go thresholds written down in advance: ≥6 clear VI-IX scenes per year and ≥1 pure TIRS footprint per parcel. If go:
(a) ΔT/WDI anomaly vs ISMN 20-30 cm z on Landsat days, paired against NDVI anomaly on the same days.
(b) Event test: the 2022 and 2026 summers should show WDI or ΔT anomalies ≥1 SD in ≥12 of 15 vineyards.
(c) Cross-sectional ΔT rank vs δ13C (M2).

methods.name: M7. SWIR water-content indices (NDMI, i.e. MSI or Gao NDWI with B8A/B11; CRSWIR) at native 20 m with the M1 baseline, as a second 'water' channel
methods.description:
This narrows and corrects F3 Z11/Z14 rather than repeating them.
(i) NDMI, MSI (=B11/B8A) and Gao's NDWI with B8A/B11 are monotonic transforms of the same band ratio: MSI = (1−NDMI)/(1+NDMI). Test one of them, not three; published R² differences between them are noise.
(ii) Compute from native 20 m bands, because 20 m bands after SR have 4-9% reflectance consistency error (ARCHITEKTURA §4).
(iii) Use the M1 harmonic baseline, under which NDMI and CRSWIR stop losing to NDVI.
(iv) Keep it on the dashboard as 'canopy water content anomaly'. Admit it to the status logic only if it beats NDVI when paired.
methods.why_better_than_ndvi_only: Physically, SWIR absorption responds to the water content of the canopy (EWT×LAI), not only to greenness. The literature reports S-2 NIR-SWIR indices vs Ψstem or Ψpd with R² of 0.4-0.7 in vineyards. Locally, however, against soil moisture NDMI/CRSWIR only equal NDVI: harmonic NDMI vs pooled NDVI ΔR = +0.016 [-0.054,+0.071]. The likely reason is that at canopy scale SWIR indices track LAI and canopy structure more than leaf water status, so they move after the stress, like NDVI. This is my physiological interpretation, not verified in this session.

evidence.citation: Own computation, not literature: e0_baseline.py, e3_phenology.py, e8_cross_index.py
evidence.finding: Pooled baseline vs ISMN 20-30 cm z (IV-X): NDVI SR 0.433, NDMI SR 0.409, CRSWIR SR -0.370, NDRE SR 0.382, NDMI/NDVI 0.312. With the harmonic baseline plus orbit term: NDMI 0.449, CRSWIR -0.417. Paired vs pooled NDVI: NDMI +0.016 [-0.054,+0.071], CRSWIR -0.016 [-0.099,+0.050]. Not better.

evidence.citation: Laroche-Pinel E. et al. (2021) Towards vine water status monitoring on a large scale using Sentinel-2 images. Remote Sens. 13(9):1837
evidence.finding: 36 plots, 2018-2020, more than 2500 Ψstem measurements. Best ML model on Red, NIR, Red-Edge and SWIR bands: R²=0.40, RMSE=0.26 MPa. Mainly Syrah.

evidence.citation: Giannico V., Garofalo S.P., Brillante L. et al. (2024) Temporal vine water status modeling through ML ensemble and Sentinel-2 under semi-arid conditions. Remote Sens. 16(24):4784
evidence.finding: Random forest on S-2 vegetation indices vs Ψstem: R²=0.72, but in one Montepulciano vineyard over two irrigated seasons. That is within-season, single-site skill, not anomaly skill.

evidence.citation: Cohen Y., ..., Helman D. (2019) Can time series of multispectral satellite images be used to estimate stem water potential in vineyards? ECPA 2019; Helman et al. (2018) Remote Sens. 10:1615
evidence.finding: 82 Israeli vineyards: S-2 NIR-SWIR moisture indices beat Planet VIS-NIR for Ψstem. The Planet global model reached r=0.78 (N=970). These correlations largely reflect seasonal co-decline of Ψstem and canopy, which is my interpretation.

evidence.citation: Delval L. et al. EGU22-3908 (Belgium, grassed inter-rows), and a Rías Baixas conference abstract (NDWI vs MSI)
evidence.finding: NDWI/EVI was best, with R² up to 0.67-0.72 vs Ψpd under the driest conditions. NDWI R² 0.54-0.67 and MSI 0.53-0.63; these are near-identical because the two are transforms of each other.

methods.data_needed: Native B8A, B11 and B12 per scene, already in the step_01 rasters, plus the M1 baseline. EVI would need B02 for NDWI/EVI; the bands are already in the rasters.
methods.feasible_in_colab_gee: Yes. compute_indices already computes NDMI and CRSWIR. Add a native 20 m path and MSI is not needed. No new downloads.
methods.expected_gain: About 0 to +0.02 ΔR vs NDVI against soil moisture (n.s. locally). The value is complementary: a water-specific map and anomaly on the dashboard, and an input candidate for M3 and M5. Do not expect it to fix 'NDVI is too simplistic' by itself.
methods.risks:
- Pixel noise from SR in 20 m bands (keep native resolution).
- SWIR is more sensitive to row and soil geometry than NDVI (CESBIO: the performance target is missed in SWIR for vineyards).
- Higher CRSWIR means drier, so sign errors are possible.
- Literature R² values are within-season and not transferable to anomalies.
methods.validation_plan: Paired ΔR vs NDVI under the same M1 baseline, IV-X and VI-IX. Promote to the status logic only if the lower CI bound > 0 and partial r given ERA5 > 0. F3 event test: 2022 VII-IX anomaly ≤ -1 in ≥12 of 15 vineyards. Parcel-truth test as in M2.

methods.name: M8. Biophysical retrievals (SL2P / LEAF-Toolbox in GEE: LAI, FCOVER, CCC = LAI·Cab, CWC = LAI·Cw) as alternative vegetation variables
methods.description: Run the SL2P or SL2P-CCRS networks (CCRS LEAF-Toolbox, native in GEE) on the S-2 archive for the 15 parcels. Compute anomalies of CCC and CWC with the M1 baseline. Use FCOVER or LAI as structural parcel attributes for M4 and M5.
methods.why_better_than_ndvi_only: In principle these are physical variables: CWC in g/cm² and CCC in g/cm². CCC is sensitive to chlorosis and leaf yellowing under late drought; CWC to canopy water. In practice the PROSAIL turbid-medium assumption is violated by vineyard rows. LAI from radiative-transfer methods is strongly underestimated in clumped vines, and I found no CWC validation for crops. Locally, NDRE (a CCC proxy) is weaker than NDVI (0.38 vs 0.43). Expect little gain; anomalies may still work because the structural bias is roughly constant within a parcel.

evidence.citation: Kang Y. et al. (2022) Evaluation of satellite Leaf Area Index in California vineyards for improving water use estimation. Irrig. Sci. (DOI 10.1007/s00271-022-00798-8)
evidence.finding: Six LAI approaches (Landsat, S-2) vs ground truth in 4 vineyards. Radiative-transfer methods significantly underestimated high LAI in clumped vines (RMSE about 0.97-1.27). Empirical Cubist models reached 0.3-0.48 but did not transfer between sites. S-2 red-edge adds complementary information.

evidence.citation: Zarco-Tejada P.J. et al. (2005) Assessing vineyard condition with hyperspectral indices: leaf and canopy reflectance simulation in a row-structured discontinuous canopy. Remote Sens. Environ. 99:271-287
evidence.finding: Vineyards need a row-structured canopy model (rowMCRM coupled with PROSPECT) that accounts for row orientation, vine dimensions, soil and shadow. A turbid-medium model is inadequate.

evidence.citation: LEAF-Toolbox / SL2P validation (Fernandes, Djamai et al.; Brown et al.)
evidence.finding: SL2P is in GEE. Validation covers LAI, FCOVER and fAPAR. Forests show a 20-50% LAI bias for LAI>2, and target user requirements are met for only 31-51% of comparisons. No CWC validation was found.

evidence.citation: Own computation, not literature: e0_baseline.py, e3_phenology.py
evidence.finding: NDRE (CCC proxy) vs ISMN z: 0.382 (SR) and 0.369 (10 m), vs NDVI 0.433. Partial r given ERA5 = 0.06-0.08, n.s. No harmonic gain for NDRE in IV-X (0.365).

methods.data_needed: S-2 L2A bands plus sun and view angles (in GEE). LEAF-Toolbox code (public GEE repository).
methods.feasible_in_colab_gee: Yes, natively in GEE, run per scene over 15 small parcels.
methods.expected_gain: Low for drought detection: likely on par with NDVI or NDMI. Moderate as structural parcel attributes (LAI and FCOVER trends, vigour) for M4 and M5, and for alignment with EDO's fAPAR (F3 Z12).
methods.risks:
- Row-structure bias.
- The CWC product is unvalidated.
- Neural-network retrievals extrapolate outside their training space (inter-row soil and grass mixtures).
- Adds complexity without proven gain.
methods.validation_plan: Same protocol as M7: paired ΔR vs NDVI under the M1 baseline, partial r given ERA5, the 2022 event test, and the parcel-truth test. Adopt only as a structural attribute unless the lower CI bound of ΔR > 0.

research.top_recommendation:
Do M1 and M2 first: about 5 person-days, no new data, all in the existing step_04/step_07 code.

Step 1 (M1). Replace the pooled 'other years ±15 DOY' z-score with a per-parcel harmonic baseline. Fit it with each scene's own year left out, and either add an orbit/geometry term or split the climatology by orbit. This removes a measured systematic error, a 0.5 SD offset between the two S-2 orbits that appears only at the vineyard (p=5e-21), and gives each z a per-parcel noise level. On the same days it improves NDMI and CRSWIR (ΔR +0.04 to +0.05, significant) and leaves NDVI unchanged or slightly better.

Step 2 (M2). Switch validation to paired ΔR, partial r given ERA5, and a 30-day target, and write the acceptance thresholds down before running anything. Unpaired CIs of ±0.18 cannot show any improvement.

Then reframe the vegetation layer honestly. Against soil moisture, no Sentinel-2 index beats NDVI and none adds information beyond ERA5 (partial r ≈ 0.1, n.s.). The value S-2 can add is cross-sectional ('this vineyard vs its neighbours', M3, 1.5 days). Its proof must come from cheap vine-water-status truth across the 15 parcels: δ13C of must at harvest plus ApeX shoot-growth observations from the 2027 season, with Spearman ρ ≥ 0.52 as the stated criterion.

After that, invest in M4: row geometry and vine cover fraction from the free IGN BD ORTHO 20 cm IRC, plus winter S-2 ingestion. It feeds M5, a dual vine + inter-row water balance (FTSW and a Ψpd proxy) that extends Plan_v5. That is the professional answer to 'NDVI is too simplistic': S-2 parametrises a physically meaningful vine water-status model rather than serving as a greenness threshold.

Thermal (M6) gets only a half-day go/no-go check now, ahead of TRISHNA and LSTM. Stop claiming any precision gain from 2.5 m SR: rows cannot be resolved by physics, and paired R is identical to 10 m.
not_recommended: Separating rows from inter-rows with SEN2SR 2.5 m, or claiming SR improves detection. Rows 2.2-3 m apart are 0.33-0.45 cycles/m, 7-9 times above the 10 m Nyquist frequency (0.05 c/m), where the S2 MTF is already only 0.15-0.3. Sampling at 2.5 m would itself alias the rows; resolving them needs a pixel of 1.1-1.5 m or finer. Measured locally: SR NDVI anomaly R=0.433 vs 10 m 0.426, identical. Use SR only for map display.
Anomaly windows aligned on thermal time (GDD base 10 °C). Tested: r 0.410 vs 0.430 (IV-X) and 0.439 vs 0.436 (VI-IX), no gain.

Whittaker-smoothed per-year trajectory anomalies as a precision improvement. Tested: r 0.419 vs 0.430. The smoothing is non-causal, so it is unreliable at the end of the series in near-real-time. A 30-day trailing composite (Z3) gave 0.408. It may still help stability, but not skill vs soil moisture.
Testing MSI and Gao-NDWI (B8A/B11) as separate indices from NDMI. They are monotonic transforms of the same band ratio (MSI = (1-NDMI)/(1+NDMI)), so published R² differences between them are noise.

Promoting NDMI, CRSWIR, NDRE or NDMI/NDVI into the status logic on the current evidence. With the best baseline, paired ΔR vs NDVI is +0.016 [-0.054,+0.071] (NDMI) and -0.016 [-0.099,+0.050] (CRSWIR). NDMI/NDVI is worse (0.31). None adds anything to ERA5 (partial r -0.05 to 0.11, n.s.).

Replacing the anomaly with a seasonal increment against the April background of the same year. r drops to 0.18-0.24, although partial r given ERA5 is 0.21 [0.02,0.39], so it is a possible complementary diagnostic only. The winter version (F3 Z14) cannot run until S-2 ingestion covers XI-III; S2_MONTHS is currently (4,10).
Lag windows for the vegetation response. With the 30-day ISMN mean, r peaks at lag 0 (0.488) and falls to 0.31 at 60 days; no lag improves the fit.

Generic NBAR c-factor BRDF normalisation (Roy et al.) to fix the orbit bias. It uses fixed global BRDF shapes that cannot represent the row-azimuth-dependent anisotropy of vineyards; split by orbit or use geometry covariates (M1) instead. This is my judgement, not verified in the literature during this session.
