TVDI or other contextual triangle indices at AOI scale. Their dry and wet edges depend on the scene and are unstable over a small AOI, while WDI with vertices from meteorology (M6) is physically anchored.
PRI, SIF or other photosynthesis-based stress signals from space at parcel scale. S-2 has no 531 nm band, and SIF exists only at 300 m (FLEX) to 7 km (TROPOMI).

Using absolute SL2P LAI or CWC values for vineyards. Radiative-transfer retrievals strongly underestimate clumped vine LAI, and CWC is unvalidated for crops. Use them at most as anomalies or structural attributes (M8).
Sentinel-3 LST sharpening (already rejected in F3), and ECOSTRESS as a primary operational layer: irregular overpasses, and the mission is approved only through FY2026, pending the Senior Review.
Reporting unpaired R with separate CIs as evidence that one method beats another. The CIs are ±0.18, so they overlap for every candidate tested; always use paired ΔR with a block bootstrap.

research.direction: Improving the soil-moisture layer (currently ERA5-Land 0-100 cm, one ~9 km cell shared by all 15 vineyards; anomaly R=0.583 vs ISMN Condom 20-30 cm)
research.summary:
Before searching the literature, I tested the main options on the local data. The scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-1-geoworldlook-agriscreen/0b6bc240-34e1-5fd3-a139-3c46967fd603/scratchpad/sm_analysis/ (a1 to a7). The repo was not modified.

(1) The baseline reproduces exactly. ERA5-Land 0-100 cm vs ISMN Condom 20-30 cm gives R=0.583 [0.500, 0.665], n=2976 days. Spearman is 0.596.

(2) Much of the remaining error sits in the reference station, not in ERA5.
- Extended triple collocation (ERA5, Sentinel-1 SWI, ISMN) estimates each source's correlation with the unknown common signal: ERA5 0-100 cm 0.81 [0.74, 0.88]; ERA5 0-28 cm 0.89 [0.82, 0.95]; ISMN 20-30 cm only 0.72-0.78.
- Seven SMOSMANIA stations 31-138 km away correlate with Condom 20-30 cm anomalies at only R=0.34-0.54. The ERA5 Condom cell correlates with those same stations about as well (0.29-0.63).
- The Condom 20-30 cm sensors read below 0.10 m3/m3 on 813 of 2976 days, mostly July-October. The soil there is 41-46% clay, so such low values are physically implausible. The likely cause is shrinkage cracks breaking sensor contact; this is a hypothesis, not checked. It affects exactly the drought season.
- The 5 cm sensor drifts: annual maxima fell from about 0.39 to 0.31 m3/m3 after 2020.

(3) Matching the depth raises the annual R, but almost only in winter.
- ERA5 0-28 cm gives R=0.691 (paired gain over 0-100 cm: +0.106 [+0.05, +0.16]). ERA5 layer 2 (7-28 cm) alone gives 0.693.
- In the vine season (April-October) the gain shrinks to 0.627 vs 0.640. In winter (November-March) it is 0.52 vs 0.77.
- For dekadal drought events with the operational 1991-2020 climatology, 0-28 cm does worse: skill score (HSS) 0.342 vs 0.416. So the operational warning layer should not be switched on this evidence.

(4) Sentinel-1 becomes useful once it is filtered.
- The existing change-detection series at the station (S1_CD_A, 50 m buffer) is weak raw: R=0.38 vs 5 cm on 35-day anomalies.
- After an exponential filter with T=10 days (I tested T from 5 to 40), it reaches R=0.555 [0.47, 0.63] vs 20-30 cm. That is close to ERA5 0-100 cm (0.583).
- It also carries information ERA5 does not: its correlation with the station after removing the ERA5 part (partial correlation) is 0.21-0.30.
- An equal-weight average of the ERA5 0-100 cm and Sentinel-1 anomalies gives R=0.631. The paired gain is +0.047 [+0.006, +0.089].
- Weights from triple collocation add nothing over equal weights (0.703 with weights fitted on other years vs 0.708 fitted on all years). This matches Yilmaz et al. 2012.

(5) The 35-day moving anomaly is the wrong tool for drought.
- It lowers R to 0.41, because 89% of the ERA5 0-100 cm anomaly variance is the slow component.
- The ±7, ±15 or ±30 day window for the day-of-year climatology barely matters (R 0.581 / 0.583 / 0.591).
- Against the 1991-2020 climatology, 20.6% of days in 2016-2024 fall at z ≤ -1.
- z = -1 corresponds to percentiles 14.5-19.9 depending on the month. Skew reaches 0.95 in October.

(6) With one station no candidate is significantly better for drought events. All differences in event skill have year-block bootstrap intervals about ±0.15-0.2 wide.

**What the literature says to expect.**
- Sentinel-1 surface soil moisture products at 1 km reach a median R of about 0.53-0.54 (Copernicus SSM 1 km in Madelon et al. 2023; Balenzano et al. 2021, 167 stations).
- The fused Sentinel-1 + ASCAT SWI product (SCATSAR-SWI) reaches a median R of 0.61 vs in situ.
- Applying the SWI filter improves every satellite product (Beck et al. 2021).
- For the filter constant, T=14 days was best against 30 cm sensors in SW France (Albergel et al. 2009), consistent with our T=10.
- There is no peer-reviewed Sentinel-1 soil-moisture validation over vineyards that addresses row orientation. The French S2MP plot-scale product explicitly excludes vineyards and orchards. Faridani et al. 2025 report R² of only 0.23-0.41 in hillside vineyards.
- In SW France, the SMAP/Sentinel-1 1 km product did worse than SMAP at 9/36 km (El Hajj et al. 2018).
- ERA5-Land runs offline without data assimilation; Beck et al. 2021 attribute differences between such models mainly to precipitation quality. This motivates trying Météo-France SIM2 (SAFRAN-ISBA), which is forced by the dense French rain-gauge network and is open data, and SMAP L4 (in GEE) as alternative or third members.

**Net assessment.** Swapping ERA5 for another product will not give a large, provable precision gain. What makes the layer more precise and defensible to EO experts is:
- (a) multi-station validation with consistent depth and climatology baseline, plus triple collocation, so differences become measurable;
- (b) a parcel-level Sentinel-1 SWI as an independent second source, fused with ERA5-Land by equal-weight z-score averaging, as the EDO/GDO soil moisture anomaly ensemble does;
- (c) testing SIM2 and SMAP L4 as independent model members.

Most web sources were readable only as search snippets; publisher sites, Copernicus Land, HESS, HAL and GEE pages were blocked by the proxy. Access levels are marked per item.

methods.name: M1. Multi-station validation with consistent depth and climatology baseline, plus triple collocation (21 SMOSMANIA stations)
methods.why_better_than_ndvi_only:
On soil moisture, Sentinel-2 adds nothing here: ERA5 + S-2 + S-1 was not better than ERA5 alone (Plan_v4). The real limitation is the reference.
- Triple collocation at Condom puts the ISMN 20-30 cm correlation with the true signal at only 0.72 [0.64, 0.79]; ERA5 0-100 cm is at 0.81 and ERA5 0-28 cm at 0.89.
- So the headline R=0.58 is capped by the point sensor, not just by ERA5.
- With one station, no candidate change is distinguishable for drought events: event-skill differences have intervals about ±0.15-0.2 wide.

Multi-station validation with triple collocation is the standard (CEOS LPV / Gruber et al. 2020) that EO experts expect. It is also the only way to prove any of the improvements below.

evidence.citation: Own computation on local data (sm_analysis/a4_tc_fusion.py): extended TC on [ERA5 RZ, S1-SWI T=10, ISMN 20-30 cm], n=2976
evidence.finding: Correlation with the unknown truth: ERA5 0-100 cm 0.81 [0.74, 0.88], S1-SWI 0.77 [0.69, 0.86], ISMN 0.72 [0.64, 0.79]. With ERA5 0-28 cm in place of 0-100 cm: 0.89 / 0.71 / 0.78. The point reference caps the achievable R at about 0.72-0.78.

evidence.citation: Own computation (sm_analysis/a5_window_neighbors.py): 20-30 cm anomaly correlation between Condom and other SMOSMANIA stations
evidence.finding: Neighbouring stations 31-138 km away correlate with Condom at R=0.34-0.54. The ERA5 Condom-cell 0-28 cm correlates with those stations at 0.29-0.63, about as well as Condom itself.

evidence.citation: Own computation (a2/a6): Condom QC
evidence.finding: 20-30 cm mean below 0.10 m3/m3 on 813 of 2976 days (July 123, August 223, September 183, October 111) in 41-46% clay (static_variables.csv). 5 cm annual maximum drifts from 0.39 to 0.31 m3/m3 after 2020. The 5 cm vs 20-30 cm climatology-anomaly R is only 0.27.

evidence.citation: Own computation (a7_events_ci.py): dekadal HSS with year-block bootstrap, Condom only
evidence.finding: Baseline HSS 0.457 (common-period climatology). All candidate differences (0-28 cm, S1, fusion) have 95% CIs spanning zero, about [-0.09, +0.21].

evidence.citation: Gruber et al. 2020, Validation practices for satellite soil moisture retrievals: What are (the) errors?, RSE 244:111806
evidence.finding: Community good-practice validation protocol (error estimation incl. TC, pre-processing, statistical reporting), endorsed by CEOS LPV.

evidence.citation: Balenzano et al. 2021, Sentinel-1 soil moisture at 1 km resolution: a validation study, RSE 263:112554
evidence.finding: Quantifies the spatial representativeness error between a 1 km pixel and point sensors. A dense network (4-5 sensors/km²) gives RMSE about 0.06 and R 0.71; one sensor per km² adds about 0.02 m3/m3 of error.

evidence.citation: Yilmaz & Crow 2014, Evaluation of assumptions in soil moisture triple collocation analysis, J. Hydrometeorol. 15:1293-1302
evidence.finding: Cross-correlated errors bias TC more than non-orthogonal errors; TC generally underestimates true random error. Choose independent triplets (model, active, in situ).

evidence.citation: Núñez-Ibarra et al. 2025, EGUsphere preprint (read in full in F3, section 1.4)
evidence.finding: Recommends Spearman on deseasonalised series and thickness-weighted sensor profiles; ERA5-Land root zone represented better than the surface layer.

methods.data_needed: Local ISMN .stm files for 21 SMOSMANIA stations (already in the repo; 2025-2026 would need a new ISMN download). GEE point extraction: ECMWF/ERA5_LAND/DAILY_AGGR (volumetric_soil_water_layer_1..4), COPERNICUS/S1_GRD, NASA/SMAP/SPL4SMGP/008 (root zone). Nothing else.
methods.feasible_in_colab_gee: Yes. Point and buffer extraction of about 21 sites × 3 products is minutes per station with the existing _cached_extract. pytesmo is installed (tcol_metrics available). ISMN parsing already exists (read_ismn_stm / qc_insitu). Extra code: a loop over stations, a percentile-matched event function and a station-block bootstrap.
methods.expected_gain:
The product itself does not change; what changes is how precisely we can measure it. The paired difference CI should shrink from about ±0.06 (one station) to an estimated ±0.02-0.03 pooled over 8+ Atlantic stations. That makes a 0.03-0.05 gain (fusion, depth choice) statistically decidable.

It also gives a defensible headline: ERA5 correlation with the true signal is about 0.8 (triple collocation), next to R=0.58 against a point sensor whose own correlation with the truth is about 0.75. Event POD/FAR become baseline-consistent: the current 0.574/0.571 mixes the 1991-2020 product baseline with the 2016-2024 in-situ baseline.
methods.risks:
- SMOSMANIA plots are grass or fallow, not vineyards.
- The Mediterranean stations have a different climate, so stratify.
- Triple collocation assumptions: independent and linear errors, stationarity, and similar depth support. ERA5 0-28 cm and S1-SWI are closer in depth than ISMN 20-30 cm, which may inflate their scores. Report triple-collocation CIs and treat the results as indicative.
- Data gaps at some stations (10 cm series at Condom ends in 2020).
- The ISMN floor-value flag is a hypothesis; confirm with the network operator (Météo-France CNRM) or the literature.
methods.validation_plan:
Write the metrics and decision rules into docs before computing.
- Calibration years 2016-2021, test years 2022-2024 (consistent with STATION_CONFIG TEST_PERIOD).
- Per station: R, Spearman, ubRMSD of anomalies, and HSS/POD/FAR with percentile-matched thresholds, each with a block bootstrap.
- Pooled: median and station-block bootstrap.
- Triple collocation per station with bootstrap CIs.
- Output in gwl_validation_metrics with segment = anomaly_clim / anomaly_35d / events_dekad_pmatched / tc_rtruth.

methods.name: M2. Parcel-level Sentinel-1 SWI (per-orbit change detection plus exponential filter, T about 10 days) as a second, independent soil-moisture source
methods.description:
In GEE, for each vineyard (interior with a 10 m inner buffer) and for the station:
- Take S1 GRD IW VV (and VH), averaged in linear power over the parcel.
- Compute the relative wetness per relative orbit, as the existing s1_change_detection already does: dry and wet references are the 5th/95th percentiles per orbit over 2016-2021. Optionally normalise to a reference incidence angle with a per-orbit regression.
- Flag wet canopy (ERA5 precipitation in the preceding 12 h; dew risk on 06 UTC passes when ERA5 dewpoint depression is small) and frost (t2m_min < 0).
- Apply the recursive exponential filter (Albergel et al. 2008, gain form for irregular sampling) with T=10 days to get a daily Soil Water Index.
- Anomalies: z against a day-of-year climatology from 2016 onward. Optionally CDF-match to ERA5 1991-2020 (Reichle & Koster 2004) because the S1 record is short.
- Store as product S1SWI_T10 per site in gwl_observations. Show it on the card as a radar soil-moisture index, not as volumetric water content.

If the vineyard-level tests fail, fall back to an AOI-level S1-SWI (all parcels plus surroundings) or to CGLS SWI 1 km (Z10).

evidence.citation: Own computation (a3_s1.py): S1_CD_A at the Condom 50 m buffer, 1644 obs, 4 orbits
evidence.finding: Raw change detection vs 5 cm (35-day anomalies): R=0.384 [0.31, 0.45]; ERA5 layer 1 on the same days 0.613. SWI vs 20-30 cm climatology anomaly: T=5 0.527, T=10 0.555 [0.47, 0.63], T=20 0.540, T=40 0.510. By orbit: lower incidence (orbits 132 at 31.8°, 8 at 35.2°) R=0.38/0.42; higher incidence (30 at 41.8°, 110 at 44.8°) 0.34/0.35. Observations per year fall from about 240 to about 120 in 2022-2024 (S-1B loss).

evidence.citation: Own computation (a6_season_partial.py)
evidence.finding: Partial r(S1-SWI, ISMN | ERA5 0-28 cm) = 0.21; | ERA5 0-100 cm = 0.30. S1-SWI R by season: April-October 0.51, June-September 0.45, November-March 0.62.

evidence.citation: Albergel et al. 2008, From near-surface to root-zone soil moisture using an exponential filter, HESS 12:1323 (SMOSMANIA)
evidence.finding: A recursive exponential filter with one parameter T gives a root-zone index from surface data at SMOSMANIA stations. T is optimised per station by Nash-Sutcliffe; there is no clear link to soil texture, and a single median T of about 15 days performs nearly as well.

evidence.citation: Albergel et al. 2009, An evaluation of ASCAT surface soil moisture products with in-situ observations in Southwestern France, HESS 13:115
evidence.finding: The best SWI vs 30 cm in-situ correlation was obtained at T=14 days (two stations).

evidence.citation: Beck et al. 2021, Evaluation of 18 satellite- and model-based soil moisture products using in situ measurements from 826 sensors, HESS 25:17
evidence.finding: Applying the SWI smoothing filter improved every satellite product (SMAP L3E-SWI median R 0.72). Satellite products overall 0.66, open-loop models 0.69, models with assimilation 0.72.

evidence.citation: Bauer-Marschallinger et al. 2019, Toward Global Soil Moisture Monitoring With Sentinel-1, IEEE TGRS (DOI 10.1109/TGRS.2018.2858004)
evidence.finding: TU Wien change-detection method behind CGLS SSM 1 km. Good agreement over plains and agriculture, poor in forest and steep terrain. Positive biases during the growing season, while small-scale rain or irrigation changes are captured.

evidence.citation: Balenzano et al. 2021, RSE 263:112554; Madelon et al. 2023, HESS 27:1221
evidence.finding: Sentinel-1 surface soil moisture at 1 km: R=0.54, error about 0.07 m3/m3 over 167 stations (Balenzano). In Madelon et al. the median R of the Copernicus SSM is 0.53, below coarser products (0.67-0.77). CoperSWI correlation exceeds 0.5 only where 1 km pixels are crop-dominated.

evidence.citation: Bauer-Marschallinger et al. 2018, Soil Moisture from Fusion of Scatterometer and SAR: Closing the Scale Gap with Temporal Filtering, Remote Sens. 10(7):1030
evidence.finding: SCATSAR-SWI (ASCAT + S1, exponential filter, 1 km) has median R 0.61 vs in situ and 0.71 vs a water-balance model. Basis of the CGLS SWI 1 km product.

evidence.citation: Faridani et al. 2025, Integration of Sentinel-1 and -2 imagery ... hillside vineyard soil moisture, Agric. Water Manag. 315:109541
evidence.finding: The only vineyard-specific S1 change-detection study found: 20 m in GEE, two Italian hillside vineyards. S1+S2 R² 0.23-0.41 (vs 0.16-0.21 with S2 only), RMSE 3.6-5.7 vol%.

evidence.citation: Theia S2MP product description (El Hajj, Baghdadi et al.)
evidence.finding: The French plot-scale S1+S2 soil-moisture product (neural network on VV, incidence angle and NDVI) gives estimates only for agricultural areas and grasslands, explicitly excluding vineyards and orchards, and degrades at high NDVI.

evidence.citation: Synthetic Aperture Radar in Vineyard Monitoring: Examples, Demonstrations, and Future Perspectives, Remote Sens. 2024, 16(12):2106; Po Valley vineyard SAR study (2025, ResearchGate)
evidence.finding: Vineyards scatter non-isotropically because of row orientation. The Po Valley study analysed east-west and north-south rows separately and suggests reduced sensitivity when the pass is roughly parallel to the rows. No quantitative row-orientation correction for S1 soil moisture was found.

evidence.citation: Retrieving Soil Moisture from Sentinel-1: Limitations over Certain Crops and Sensitivity to the First Soil Thin Layer, Water 2024, 16(1):40
evidence.finding: S1 senses about 5 cm or less. In dry conditions S1 soil moisture underestimated 10 cm sensors by up to about 20 vol%, a depth mismatch the SWI filter partly addresses.

evidence.citation: Sentinel-1 sensitivity to soil moisture at high incidence angle and the impact on retrieval over seasonal crops (Sapienza, 2020)
evidence.finding: At about 33° VV tracks soil moisture well over wheat and barley. At about 43° the signal mixes soil attenuation and double-bounce. Over volume-scattering crops VV is uncorrelated with soil moisture.

evidence.citation: Rahmati, Balenzano, Brocca, Montzka et al., Soil moisture retrieval from Sentinel-1: Lessons learned after more than a decade in orbit, RSE (2025/2026)
evidence.finding: Remaining obstacles: vegetation, roughness and sampling. Recommends multi-sensor integration (S2, SMAP) and validation on standardised reference sets.

evidence.citation: Sentinel-1 IW GRD-HR equivalent number of looks of about 4.4 at about 20×22 m resolution
evidence.finding: My own estimate, not verified: averaging over a 2.9 ha vineyard (about 66 resolution cells, about 290 looks) gives speckle SD of the mean about 0.25 dB, versus about 0.5 dB for the 50 m station buffer. Parcel averages should be about twice as stable as the station series for speckle.

methods.data_needed: COPERNICUS/S1_GRD (already used in step_07.fetch_s1), vineyard polygons (data/1_AOI_GBOV_CONDOM.geojson), ERA5-Land precipitation, temperature and dewpoint for flags (dewpoint needs one extra band in step_01). Optional: row azimuth per parcel from IGN BD ORTHO (manual digitising) for the row-orientation test. Optional: NASA/SMAP/SPL3SMP_E (9 km, L-band radiometer) as an independent third member for triple collocation.
methods.feasible_in_colab_gee: Yes. reduceRegions over 15 parcels plus the station for about 1800 scenes on 4 orbits takes minutes and is incremental, like the existing tasks. The filter and anomalies are pandas (about 30 lines). It fits the existing task_* and registry design as a new product row type. No new external accounts needed.
methods.expected_gain:
Station-scale: an independent soil-moisture series with R about 0.50-0.56 vs 20-30 cm anomalies (vs 0.38 raw). Combined with ERA5 in M3 it gives about +0.05 R.

Parcel scale: unknown. The honest prior from the literature is weak (vineyard R² 0.23-0.41) with a growing-season bias. Its value is decided by the internal tests below. It costs almost nothing to keep as a confidence or agreement signal on the card even if it does not enter the status logic.
methods.risks:
- Vineyard row structure and trellis cause anisotropic backscatter; the constant part is absorbed by per-orbit references, but phenology-dependent attenuation from June to August is not.
- Growing-season positive bias (Bauer-Marschallinger 2019).
- Dew on 06 UTC descending passes; tillage and roughness changes in the inter-row (spring), which create change-detection artefacts.
- Shallow sensing depth (about 1-5 cm) vs vine roots of 1-2 m or more.
- Sampling halved in 2022-2024 (S-1B loss) and a possible S-1C level offset: compare S1A vs S1C sigma0 on the same orbits before mixing them.
- Short climatology (2016 onward).
- 50 m station result may not transfer to vineyards.
methods.validation_plan:
1. Station (done): SWI(T) vs ISMN with T chosen on 2016-2021 only, then reported on 2022-2024.
2. Vineyard internal consistency without truth:
   - speckle and noise floor from pairs of different-orbit acquisitions within 24 h;
   - cross-geometry agreement: per dekad, Spearman of the 15 parcel anomalies from ascending orbits (30/132, about 17:50 UTC) vs descending orbits (8/110, about 06 UTC). If the median is below 0.3, parcel differences are noise and S1 is used only at AOI level.
3. Triple collocation per parcel with ERA5-Land and SMAP L3E, giving the S1 error SD and SNR per vineyard. Note that the triple-collocation truth is the regional signal.
4. Event check: share of parcels with S1-SWI z ≤ -1 in July-September 2022 (V4 in Plan_v6).
5. Row-azimuth by orbit interaction test on the backscatter residuals.

methods.name: M3. Equal-weight z-score fusion of ERA5-Land and S1-SWI for the warning layer (EDO/GDO ensemble-SMA style); weights from triple collocation only if stable across stations
methods.description:
Compute the soil-moisture anomaly for the warning as the mean of standardised anomalies: z_SM = mean(z_ERA5-RZ, z_S1SWI), with optional extra members such as SMAP L4 or SIM2 from M4. Re-standardise the mean to unit variance using the climatology. Use equal weights by default.

Use weights from triple collocation (w proportional to R²/(1-R²) of each member's correlation with the truth) only if the multi-station analysis in M1 shows stable weights.

Keep the member anomalies and their agreement in reason_codes and confidence (e.g. ERA5_S1_AGREE / DISAGREE), so fusion never hides a conflict. Fall back to ERA5 alone when no S1 observation has entered the filter in more than 12 days.
methods.why_better_than_ndvi_only: It adds an observation-based, partly parcel-specific signal to a model-only warning. ERA5-Land has no data assimilation. The fusion helps at the Condom station, the only test site so far: R 0.583 to 0.631, paired +0.047 [+0.006, +0.089]. This is the same design JRC uses operationally (EDO/GDO soil moisture anomaly = weighted mean of standardised LISFLOOD, ESA CCI and MODIS LST), so it is defensible to drought-monitoring experts.

evidence.citation: Own computation (a4_tc_fusion.py, a7_events_ci.py)
evidence.finding: mean(ERA5 0-100 cm, S1-SWI) R=0.631 [0.555, 0.696] vs 0.583, paired +0.047 [+0.006, +0.089]. mean(ERA5 0-28 cm, S1-SWI) 0.690, no gain over 0-28 cm alone. Weights from triple collocation (0.78/0.22) give 0.708; with weights fitted on the other years only, 0.703. April-October: fusion 0.645-0.652 vs ERA5 0.627-0.640. HSS: fusion with 0-100 cm 0.499 vs 0.457 (difference CI [-0.09, +0.21]).

evidence.citation: Cammalleri et al. 2017, Assessing the value of combining satellite and model soil moisture for drought monitoring in Europe, HESS 21:6329; GDO soil moisture factsheet
evidence.finding: Triple collocation of LISFLOOD, MODIS LST and ESA CCI feeds a weighted-average ensemble of standardised anomalies. Remote sensing performs better in dry, sparsely monitored regions; LISFLOOD better in well-monitored areas. Operational at 0.1°, 30-day moving window, every dekad.

evidence.citation: Yilmaz, Crow, Anderson, Hain 2012, An objective methodology for merging satellite- and model-based soil moisture products, Water Resour. Res. (DOI 10.1029/2011WR011682); author list from my own memory, not confirmed
evidence.finding: Least-squares merging with weights from triple collocation beat each single input, but a simple equal-weight average was at least as good.

evidence.citation: Gruber et al. 2017, IEEE TGRS 55(12):6780 (ESA CCI SM merging); Stradiotti et al. 2025
evidence.finding: Inverse error-variance weights from triple collocation are optimal under independent errors. Seasonally varying weights gave no significant difference from stationary weights.

methods.data_needed: Outputs of M2 (S1-SWI per site) and the existing ERA5-Land anomalies. Optional members from M4.
methods.feasible_in_colab_gee: Yes. About 40 lines in step_04: a new era5_anomalies-like function plus a build_status option. It runs in Colab on registry data with no extra GEE calls.
methods.expected_gain: At Condom, +0.03 to +0.05 in anomaly R for the 0-100 cm warning layer. Event-skill gain is not provable at one station (HSS +0.04, CI spanning zero), so it needs the multi-station test in M1. Parcel differentiation of the warning becomes possible, which is now impossible with one shared ERA5 cell. This holds only if M2's vineyard tests pass.
methods.risks:
- Sentinel-1 summer errors (vegetation, dew) could add false warnings exactly in July-August.
- The short S1 climatology makes z unstable in the early years.
- Fusion could mask a real ERA5 vs S1 disagreement, so the members must be exposed on the card.
- Weights from triple collocation at one station are unstable (sample-size uncertainty, Formanek et al. 2024).
methods.validation_plan: Decision rule written before the multi-station run: adopt fusion for the warning if (a) pooled ΔR > 0 with a 95% station-block-bootstrap CI excluding 0 over at least 8 Atlantic SMOSMANIA stations, and (b) pooled FAR of percentile-matched dekadal events does not increase while POD does not fall by more than 0.05. Otherwise keep ERA5 alone and show S1 only as agreement or confidence.

methods.name: M4. Independent model members: Météo-France SIM2 (SAFRAN-ISBA, 8 km, French rain-gauge forcing) and SMAP L4 root zone (GEE, 9 km, L-band assimilation)
methods.description:
Add two alternative root-zone soil-moisture series at each site and station:
- SIM2 daily soil wetness index (SWI) from the open Météo-France SIM data (meteo.data.gouv.fr / data.gouv.fr, yearly compressed CSVs, 0.072° grid, back to 1958), nearest grid point. It gives a full 1991-2020 climatology.
- SMAP L4 root-zone soil moisture (NASA/SMAP/SPL4SMGP/008 in GEE, 3-hourly, 9 km, 2015 onward), aggregated to daily.

Compute day-of-year anomalies, then:
- validate each against the multi-station set from M1, paired with ERA5-Land;
- use them as extra members in M3, or as the third member in triple-collocation triplets (model / active / in situ, or ERA5 / SMAP L4 / S1).
methods.why_better_than_ndvi_only: It attacks ERA5-Land's main known error source: precipitation. ERA5-Land is an offline replay with no data assimilation, forced by ERA5 precipitation. SAFRAN interpolates the dense French gauge network. SIM2 SWI is also the index Météo-France uses for the CatNat drought declarations, so it is institutionally meaningful in France and good for the EO-career narrative. SMAP L4 adds satellite L-band information through assimilation and is available in GEE. NDVI cannot correct a precipitation error at all.

evidence.citation: Beck et al. 2021, HESS 25:17
evidence.finding: Ranking of open-loop models: HBV-MSWEP, HBV-ERA5, ERA5-Land, and so on. The ranking largely reflects the quality of the precipitation forcing. HBV-MSWEP is the best overall (median R 0.78).

evidence.citation: Muñoz-Sabater et al. 2021, ERA5-Land, ESSD 13:4349
evidence.finding: ERA5-Land is an offline land-surface integration forced by downscaled ERA5 meteorology, with no assimilation. It adds value for soil moisture relative to ERA5/ERA-Interim.

evidence.citation: Szczypta et al. 2011, Verification of the new ECMWF ERA-Interim reanalysis over France, HESS 15:647
evidence.finding: ERA-Interim daily precipitation over France correlates well with SAFRAN but is underestimated by about 27% (13% after GPCP correction). In SW France, ISBA forced by rescaled ERA-Interim approaches SAFRAN-forced scores. This shows forcing matters; it says nothing direct about ERA5-Land.

evidence.citation: Météo-France SIM open data (data.gouv.fr: Données changement climatique - SIM quotidienne; Météo-France : données SIM)
evidence.finding: Daily Safran-Isba fields on the 8 km SAFRAN grid (0.072°), yearly CSV files for metropolitan France, updated twice a month (60-day rolling daily). Includes SWI_Q and its departure from the 1991-2020 normal. SIM2 is described as representing soil moisture at different depths better. SWI covers about 2 m relative to available water capacity; check whether the field is the uniform-soil CatNat variant.

evidence.citation: Reichle et al. 2017, Assessment of the SMAP Level-4 surface and root-zone soil moisture product using in situ measurements, J. Hydrometeorol.; GEE catalog NASA/SMAP/SPL4SMGP/008
evidence.finding: Unbiased RMSE 0.038 (surface) and 0.030 m3/m3 (root zone) at 9 km core sites (mostly US), better than the model-only run. GEE v008 has 0-5 cm and 0-100 cm bands. The system runs model-only during SMAP outages: 19 June - 23 July 2019 and 6 August - 20 September 2022.

methods.data_needed: SIM2 yearly CSVs 1991-2026 (download in Colab; filter the 1-2 grid points nearest each site and station, store a small CSV on Drive). NASA/SMAP/SPL4SMGP/008 via GEE point extraction. ISMN stations from M1.
methods.feasible_in_colab_gee: Yes. SMAP L4 is a direct GEE point extraction like ERA5. SIM2 is not in GEE but is a plain HTTPS CSV download, readable with pandas in Colab; each year is a large national file, so stream and filter. Run it once per year plus a rolling update. License is Etalab open; verify the column dictionary (SWI definition) first.
methods.expected_gain: Uncertain until tested. If precipitation error dominates ERA5-Land's misses in Gers, SIM2 could improve anomaly R by about 0.0-0.1 at Atlantic stations; that range is my prior. SMAP L4 mostly helps as an independent third member for triple collocation and for the fusion. Either way, the validation table gains a professional multi-product comparison (ERA5-Land vs SIM2 vs SMAP L4 vs S1-SWI).
methods.risks:
- SIM2 SWI may be defined with uniform soil and vegetation parameters, which suits a weather-driven anomaly but may not match the local soil.
- 8 km grid; data latency of a few days.
- Large national files.
- SMAP L4 has only a 2015 climatology and model-only outage periods.
- ERA5 and the SMAP L4 forcing (GEOS) share some atmospheric information, so their errors may correlate and bias triple collocation; prefer triplets with in situ or S1.
methods.validation_plan: Same pre-registered protocol as M1: paired ΔR, Spearman and HSS vs ERA5-Land per station and pooled, test years 2022-2024. A member is added to the fusion (M3) only if its pooled correlation with the truth (triple collocation) is at least 0.7 and its pooled ΔR vs ERA5 is not significantly negative. Replacing ERA5-Land outright requires a significant pooled ΔR > 0.

methods.name: M5. Anomaly-definition and threshold protocol: day-of-year climatology for status, 35-day anomalies only as a diagnostic, percentile thresholds and matched baselines
methods.description:
Codify how the anomaly window and thresholds are chosen:
- Status (warning) uses the day-of-year climatology over the 1991-2020 reference (±15 days; the window width is not critical), as EDO's SMA does.
- The 35-day moving anomaly (QA4SM/pytesmo convention) is reported only in validation, as a diagnostic of short-term dynamics, never as a drought index.
- Thresholds: report the percentile next to z, and optionally define the warning as the climatological percentile ≤ 16 instead of z ≤ -1. Soil moisture is bounded and skewed (skew up to 0.95 in October), so z = -1 means percentiles 14.5-19.9 depending on the month.
- Validation events: use percentile-matched thresholds with each series on its own common-period climatology.
- Report the 1991-2020 to 2016-2024 shift explicitly: 20.6% of days are at z ≤ -1, vs about 16% expected, mostly 2017, 2019 and 2022.
methods.why_better_than_ndvi_only: It is not an NDVI alternative but a precision fix. It removes a validation inconsistency in the current POD/FAR, which mixes baselines. It also prevents a common reviewer objection ("why 35 days?", "why z on a bounded variable?") with numbers from our own data.

evidence.citation: Own computation (a5_window_neighbors.py)
evidence.finding: ERA5 0-100 cm vs ISMN: day-of-year climatology R 0.583 (±7 d 0.581, ±30 d 0.591). 35-day anomaly R 0.410. The slow component (35-day mean of the climatology anomaly) has R 0.664 and holds 89% of the ERA5 0-100 cm anomaly variance (64% for 0-28 cm, 61% for ISMN). Against 1991-2020, the share of days with z ≤ -1 in 2016-2024 is 0.206 (2017 0.76, 2022 0.32, 2024 0.00). Trend: -0.0012 m3/m3 per decade (small vs interannual SD 0.020).

evidence.citation: Own computation (a6_season_partial.py)
evidence.finding: Operational events (product on 1991-2020, ISMN on 2016-2024): 0-100 cm POD 0.617, FAR 0.554, HSS 0.416; 0-28 cm POD 0.447, FAR 0.562, HSS 0.342. With matched common-period baselines: 0-100 cm HSS 0.457, 0-28 cm HSS 0.508. Event skill depends strongly on the baseline convention.

evidence.citation: pytesmo documentation, Calculating anomalies and climatologies
evidence.finding: Two anomaly types: vs climatology, or vs current seasonality via a 35-day moving window (±17 days), separating short-term anomalies from the seasonal signal.

evidence.citation: Gruber et al. 2020, RSE 244:111806
evidence.finding: Good-practice guidance on pre-processing (incl. anomalies) and statistical reporting for soil-moisture validation. The specific 35-day recommendation is not confirmed from the snippet.

methods.data_needed: Existing ERA5-Land 1991-2026 and ISMN data; nothing new.
methods.feasible_in_colab_gee: Yes. Pure pandas changes in step_04.clim_anomaly (percentile is already computed) and step_07.validate_anomalies (percentile-matched events).
methods.expected_gain: No change in R. It gives consistent, interpretable thresholds (the percentile of a dry dekad) and an unbiased POD/FAR/HSS for all later comparisons. It removes a known source of apparent skill differences: 0-28 cm looks worse or better than 0-100 cm depending only on the baseline convention.
methods.risks: Percentile thresholds on short series (S1, SMAP L4: about 10 years) are coarse, so use z or CDF matching to ERA5 for those. Changing the threshold definition changes historic statuses, so version it (clim_id).
methods.validation_plan: Re-run the 2016-2024 status with both conventions and report the class agreement and the share of dekads in warning per year. Validate events only with percentile-matched thresholds within M1.

research.top_recommendation:
Do M1 first (3.5 person-days): run the 21 SMOSMANIA stations already in the repo through one validation, with consistent depths and climatology baselines, percentile-matched drought events and triple collocation.

At Condom the ERA5-Land layer is already close to what a single point sensor can confirm. The station's own correlation with the true signal is about 0.75 (triple collocation), and its 20-30 cm sensors show implausible near-zero readings in summer. With one station, no change is statistically provable for drought events.

Then build M2 + M3 (about 6.5 days): a parcel-level Sentinel-1 Soil Water Index (existing per-orbit change detection plus an exponential filter, T about 10 days, all in GEE). Fuse it with ERA5-Land 0-100 cm by equal-weight z-score averaging, as the EDO/GDO ensemble soil moisture anomaly does. At Condom this raises anomaly R from 0.583 to 0.631 (paired +0.047 [+0.006, +0.089]), and Sentinel-1 alone already reaches R=0.555.

Adopt the fusion in the warning logic only if a decision rule written before the multi-station run passes. Before that, check cross-orbit consistency at the vineyards to see whether Sentinel-1 carries real parcel-level signal or only noise.

Keep ERA5-Land 0-100 cm as the operational warning layer for now. The 0-28 cm depth-matched layer scores higher overall (R=0.69), but the gain is almost entirely in winter. For dekadal drought events with the 1991-2020 climatology it does worse (HSS 0.342 vs 0.416), so report 0-28 cm in validation but do not switch to it yet.

Add SIM2 and SMAP L4 (M4) as independent members and test them in the same framework.
not_recommended: Raw (unfiltered) Sentinel-1 change-detection soil moisture as a status input at parcel level: R=0.38 vs 5 cm at Condom (35-day anomalies). Change detection gives positive biases during the growing season (Bauer-Marschallinger 2019). Use it only after the exponential filter (M2).

Exponential filter applied to ERA5-Land layer 1 to mimic the root zone: best R 0.656 (T=2-5 days), below ERA5's own layer 2 (0.693). The filter is for satellite surface data, not for a model that already has deeper layers.

Switching the operational warning from 0-100 cm to 0-28 cm on the strength of the single-station annual R (0.583 to 0.691). The gain is concentrated in November-March (0.52 to 0.77). In April-October it is only 0.627 to 0.640. For dekadal events with the 1991-2020 climatology it is worse (HSS 0.342 vs 0.416). Decide only after the multi-station test (M1).
35-day moving-window anomalies as a drought index: R drops to 0.41 because about 89% of the ERA5 0-100 cm anomaly variance is slow. Keep them only as a validation diagnostic (QA4SM convention).

Weights from triple collocation fitted at one station: they are unstable and give no gain over equal weights (0.703 with weights fitted on other years vs 0.708 fitted on all years, vs 0.690 equal). Yilmaz et al. 2012 also found equal-weight averaging as good.
SMAP/Sentinel-1 L2 1-3 km (SPL2SMAP_S): not in GEE (NSIDC only). In SW France it was weaker than SMAP 9/36 km (El Hajj et al. 2018).

Replacing ERA5-Land with CGLS SSM 1 km: surface only (about 5 cm), mixed land cover in a 1 km pixel, median R about 0.53-0.54 (Madelon 2023, Balenzano 2021), not in GEE. CGLS SWI 1 km (Z10) is acceptable only as an external benchmark. It contains Sentinel-1, so its errors correlate with our S1-SWI and it cannot be the third member for triple collocation with it.

Water Cloud Model inversion or the Theia S2MP product for vineyards: S2MP explicitly excludes vineyards and orchards, and the homogeneous-canopy assumption fails for row crops. One study (Faridani 2025) reports R² of only 0.23-0.41 in vineyards.

Machine-learning downscaling of ERA5 to parcels trained on Condom alone: one station cannot support parcel-level learning or leave-one-station-out validation. Revisit only with multi-station training data.

Using the Condom 5 cm sensor for climatology-anomaly validation: it shows sensor drift (annual maxima 0.39 to 0.31 m3/m3 after 2020) and a sensor change in 2019; its climatology-anomaly R with 20-30 cm is 0.27. Keep 35-day anomalies within each sensor segment, as the repo does.
ERA5-Land layer 4 (100-289 cm) in the status logic: relevant for deep vine roots, but no sensor below 30 cm exists to validate it. At most show it as information on the card.

research.direction: Statistics and validation design for a professional drought-anomaly product at a single site (AgriWatch v1.0 to v1.1): anomalies from short S-2 records, autocorrelation-aware inference, event skill, the right validation target for a vineyard water-stress indicator, and a pre-registered protocol with acceptance criteria.
research.summary:
I re-analysed the v1.0 registry data locally. Scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-1-geoworldlook-agriscreen/0b6bc240-34e1-5fd3-a139-3c46967fd603/scratchpad/analysis/ (a1_baseline_neff.py, a2_veg_anomaly.py, a3_paired_floor_neighbours.py, a6_spei_wb_alert.py, a6b.py, a7_frost.py, a8_placebo.py, a9_nref.py); the repo was only read. The baseline reproduces exactly: ERA5 RZ R=0.583 (n=2976) and SR NDVI R=0.433 (n=245). The findings below are new relative to F3 Z1-Z15.

(1) The vegetation-layer uncertainty is understated.
- With season (year) blocks, the 95% CI of NDVI R is [0.06, 0.64], not the reported [0.24, 0.59]. The Bretherton effective N is about 7 for 245 scenes.
- R is mostly between-year: 0.59 on 9 seasonal means, 0.29 within seasons.
- A year-derangement placebo still confirms the signal is real: the null 99th percentile is 0.297 and p<0.001.
- For ERA5 the 30-day blocks are adequate: 30-365 day blocks and a year jackknife all give about [0.50, 0.67].
- The default pytesmo bootstrap is i.i.d. (no blocks), so it is not suitable here.

(2) The S-2 z-scores are mis-calibrated.
- The reference pool has a median of 51 scenes but only 10 distinct years, and it over-weights the S-2C years (48-49 clear scenes per season in 2025-26 vs 10 in 2016).
- As a result |z|>2 occurs in 9.4% of cases against a nominal 4.6%. Predictive-t theory for 9 reference years gives exactly 9.4%. z<=-1 fires 19.6% of the time instead of 15.9%.
- A year-weighted climatology plus predictive-t calibration brings these to 3.2% and 18.0%, with R unchanged.

(3) A paired year-block dR settles several method questions.
- SR vs 10 m: dR = +0.004 [0.000, 0.009], i.e. equivalence is proven.
- Robust z: dR = +0.026 [-0.004, 0.068], not significant.
- NDMI vs NDVI: dR = -0.023 [-0.095, 0.034], inconclusive.
- A causal (near-real-time) weighted Whittaker reaches R = 0.488 on n=230. This is promising but must be re-tested paired.
- A GDD-aligned climatology is worse (0.377).
- Retrospective smoothing evaluated on all days inflates n to 1749 and lowers R to 0.31. This is pseudo-replication.

(4) The ISMN 20-30 cm probe is a weak target for vine water stress.
- In August-October, 21-30% of days sit within 0.02 m3/m3 of the 2% quantile (the probe floor). The August standard deviation is 0.030 vs 0.11 in May.
- Monthly R of NDVI with the probe collapses to 0.12 in August.
- On the identical 245 scene days, vineyard NDVI anomalies agree better with a simple vine FTSW bucket model (R=0.553; dR vs probe +0.12 [0.015, 0.258]) and with ERA5 RZ (0.58) than with the probe (0.433).
- Against probe dry dekads in IV-X, the alert class has precision 0.25 and POD 0.14. Warning-or-alert has precision 0.39 and POD 0.59. Adding vegetation therefore can only look worse when it is scored against soil moisture. The alert needs a vine-response target.

(5) Event skill has more structure than POD/FAR show.
- At z<=-1, ERA5 over-forecasts dry dekads (frequency bias 1.34). Other scores: HSS 0.385 [0.11, 0.57], PSS 0.44, SEDI 0.61, AUC 0.852 [0.76, 0.91].
- A threshold of -1.2 gives bias 0.96 at a similar HSS.
- At event level (dry runs of at least 2 dekads): 8 of 11 observed events are hit, 5 of 12 predicted events are false, and the median onset lag is +5 days.

(6) Representativeness limits any single-probe score.
- In-situ anomaly R between Condom and its Gers neighbours is only 0.34-0.54 at 31-69 km.
- Extended triple collocation with a neighbour composite puts ERA5 at R about 0.62 [0.43, 0.80] against the common signal. Treat this as a demonstration only; the recommended triplet adds SMAP L4.

(7) Confounders affect the 2022 positive control.
- The 3-4 April 2022 frost is visible in ERA5-Land (Tmin -2.5 C). The Gers tax office used a median 70% bud loss, plus hail in June 2022.
- 2022 is therefore not a drought-only event. The 2 alert dekads in 2023 occur with no probe-dry dekads. A downy-mildew year is a hypothesis to check.

SPEI: SciPy MLE log-logistic fits fail KS at 75-100% of days-of-year and degrade SPEI-3 to R=0.20. An empirical (Gringorten) SPEI beats SPI only slightly (SPEI-1 IV-X 0.509 vs 0.456; vs NDVI, SPEI-3 0.494 vs SPI-3 0.469).

How EDO validates the CDI:
- Sepulcre-Canto 2012 used major 2000-2011 drought events (EM-DAT) and Eurostat yields, plus a false-alarm check.
- Cammalleri 2021 compared the revised and old CDI on 20 years of real events and reported about 70% fewer stage-sequence inconsistencies. A reviewer called that evaluation largely descriptive.
- So EDO-style validation is event and impact consistency, not pixel truth. AgriWatch can exceed it by adding pre-registered quantitative event skill with CIs.

methods.name: M1. Inference that respects the data: season-block bootstrap, effective N, placebo and paired-difference tests with equivalence margins
methods.description: Replace the 30-day calendar-block CI for vegetation metrics by a year (season) block bootstrap with B>=2000; on S-2 the year is the independent unit. Report the following for every metric: n, N_eff (Bretherton 1999; equation taken from the original paper, see the corrigendum note), Pearson and Spearman, and the year-block 95% CI. For ERA5/in-situ daily series, keep the moving-block bootstrap but choose the block length automatically (Politis-White 2004 with the Patton 2009 correction; Python arch.bootstrap.optimal_block_length, StationaryBootstrap). Report a leave-one-year-out (LOYO) R range. Every A-vs-B decision (SR vs 10 m, NDMI vs NDVI, smoothing variants, seasons) uses the paired year-block bootstrap of dR = R_B - R_A on identical days. Decision rules: superiority if the lower 90% bound of dR > 0; non-inferiority/equivalence by TOST with margin +-0.05 if the 90% CI lies within (-0.05, +0.05). Add a year-derangement placebo: pair the vegetation anomaly of year A with the soil-moisture anomaly of year B at the same DOY and use the resulting null distribution of R. This tests significance without assuming independence within a season. Zou 2007 analytic CIs for overlapping correlations are a cross-check only, since they assume i.i.d. data.
methods.why_better_than_ndvi_only: It does not change the index; it changes what can be claimed about any index. With N_eff of about 7 for vegetation, almost every NDVI-vs-NDMI-vs-CRSWIR difference reported so far is statistically undecidable. Without this layer, the effort on more complex indices cannot be defended to EO reviewers.

evidence.citation: Own computation on gwl_observations.csv + ISMN Condom (a1_baseline_neff.py, a2_veg_anomaly.py, a3_paired_floor_neighbours.py, a8_placebo.py)
evidence.finding: ERA5 RZ R=0.583: Bretherton N_eff=56; Fisher CI with N_eff [0.38, 0.73]; MBB 30-365 d about [0.51, 0.67]; year jackknife [0.50, 0.67]. SR NDVI R=0.433: year-block CI [0.06, 0.64], N_eff about 7. LOYO R ranges 0.34-0.52. Paired dR: SR vs 10 m +0.004 [0.000, 0.009] (equivalent); NDMI vs NDVI -0.023 [-0.095, 0.034]; -CRSWIR vs NDVI -0.062 [-0.165, 0.016]. Placebo null mean -0.05, 95th pct 0.19, 99th pct 0.30, observed 0.433.

evidence.citation: Bretherton C.S. et al. 1999, J. Climate 12:1990-2009, effective number of spatial degrees of freedom of a time-varying field
evidence.finding: Effective sample size for correlating two autocorrelated series; used by xskillscore/climpred. A corrigendum to Vecchi et al. 2013 warns that the formula is often mis-transcribed.

evidence.citation: Politis D.N. and White H. 2004, Econometric Reviews 23:53-70; Patton, Politis and White 2009, Econometric Reviews 28:372-375 (correction)
evidence.finding: Automatic, data-driven block-length selection for block/stationary bootstrap; the corrected version is implemented in Python arch.bootstrap.optimal_block_length.

evidence.citation: Zou G.Y. 2007, Psychological Methods 12:399-413
evidence.finding: Closed-form CIs for differences between overlapping (dependent) correlations; good small-sample performance (i.i.d. assumption).

evidence.citation: pytesmo 0.18.1 source, metrics/confidence_intervals.py (installed locally)
evidence.finding: with_bootstrapped_ci resamples individual pairs i.i.d. (np.random.choice(n)), so QA4SM-style default CIs ignore temporal autocorrelation.

methods.data_needed: Already local: gwl_observations, gwl_anomalies, gwl_status, ERA5 CSV, ISMN .stm files. No new downloads.
methods.feasible_in_colab_gee: Yes, pure Python in task_validate (step_07.validate_anomalies). arch is pip-installable. Runtime is minutes on CPU. No GEE needed.
methods.expected_gain: No gain in R. Gains: credible CIs; decisive rules for H-SR2 and index selection (the SR question is now closed by equivalence); protection against over-claiming. This is the single change an EO reviewer will look for first.
methods.risks: Wider CIs will make the vegetation layer look weaker than currently reported. With 9-10 seasons the year bootstrap is coarse, so use B>=2000 and the BCa or percentile method and report both. Bretherton N_eff with a truncated ACF sum is conservative and sensitive to S-2 gaps, so report it only as a diagnostic.
methods.validation_plan: Re-run all rows of gwl_validation_metrics with the new CI columns (ci_method = year_block | mbb_auto). Unit test: on synthetic AR(1) pairs with known rho, the empirical coverage of the 95% CI must be 93-97%. Pre-register the margins (+-0.05) before computing new dR.

methods.name: M2. Calibrated anomalies from a short S-2 record: year-weighted climatology, predictive-t standardisation, causal Whittaker compositing
methods.description: Rebuild scene_anomaly in four steps. (a) Build the climatology per year, not per scene. For each other year, take one value at the target DOY: the mean of the clear scenes within +-15 d, or the year's weighted-Whittaker curve value. Then compute mean/SD over years, which removes the oversampling of S-2B/2C-era seasons. (b) Convert z to a calibrated probability with the predictive t-distribution, p = F_t(n_years-1)(z / sqrt(1 + 1/n_years)), and then to a normal score (SPI-style). Store both the raw z and the calibrated z_cal; thresholds act on z_cal. Optionally shrink the per-DOY SD toward a smooth seasonal SD (harmonic regression of SD on DOY) to cut the 26% scene-to-scene SD noise. (c) Value series in operational mode: a causal (end-point) weighted Whittaker using only data up to the scene date, with weights = clear_frac squared. Keep the retrospective smoother only for maps and reanalysis. Validate exactly the near-real-time version that the status uses. (d) Keep a percentile with Weibull/Gringorten plotting positions as a second display variable. Report robust z (median/MAD x 1.4826) as a sensitivity only. Do NOT validate on interpolated daily values (pseudo-replication).
methods.why_better_than_ndvi_only: This makes whatever index is used (NDVI, NDMI, NDWI/EVI, fAPAR) mean what its threshold claims. z<=-1 should be a 1-in-6 event and |z|>2 a 1-in-20 event. Today they fire 20% and 9% of the time, which inflates alert frequency and false alarms regardless of the index chosen.

evidence.citation: Own computation, a9_nref.py and a2_veg_anomaly.py (VINEYARD_06, S2SR_2.5m NDVI, IV-X)
evidence.finding: Reference pool: median 51 scenes but 10 distinct years. Clear scenes per season: 10 (2016) to 48-49 (2025-26). Raw z: SD 1.16, |z|>2 9.4% (theory for t8 gives 9.4%), z<=-1 19.6%. Year-weighted + predictive-t: SD 1.03, |z|>2 3.2%, z<=-1 18.0%, R unchanged (0.428). Robust z R 0.459 (dR +0.026 n.s.). Causal Whittaker lam=50: R 0.488 (n=230). Retrospective at scene days: 0.429. All daily values: 0.31 with n inflated to 1749. GDD-aligned: 0.377. Trailing 30-d mean: 0.407.

evidence.citation: Klisch A. and Atzberger C. 2016, Operational drought monitoring in Kenya using MODIS NDVI time series, Remote Sensing 8:267
evidence.finding: Operational modified Whittaker smoother producing near-real-time NDVI with constrained end-point extrapolation. Per-pixel uncertainty comes from a hindcast of NRT vs offline optimal filtering and narrows as more observations arrive. Used to trigger contingency funds.

evidence.citation: Cai Z. et al. 2017, Remote Sensing 9(12):1271; Kandasamy S. et al. 2013, Biogeosciences 10:4055
evidence.finding: No smoother is universally best. Local filters (SG, Whittaker) need calibrated parameters; function-fitting is more robust uncalibrated. Smoothing/gap-filling performance depends on gap fraction and length.

evidence.citation: Eilers P.H.C. 2003, Analytical Chemistry 75:3631 (Whittaker smoother); Atzberger and Eilers 2011
evidence.finding: Penalised least squares with weights handles irregular, cloud-gapped series; lambda controls smoothness.

methods.data_needed: Existing S2SR_2.5m and S2_10m observations and clear_frac. For full Whittaker weights per parcel, the per-scene clear fraction already in gwl_observations.
methods.feasible_in_colab_gee: Yes. A few dozen lines in step_04 (scene_anomaly) and step_05 (_veg_anomalies), sparse solver from scipy. No GEE change. Runtime is seconds per parcel, including 15 vineyards.
methods.expected_gain: Threshold calibration of about -4 percentage points for z<=-1 and -6 for |z|>2, which reduces spurious alerts. A possible +0.03 to +0.05 in R from causal compositing (to be confirmed paired, M1). A citable method statement: year-weighted predictive standardisation for short records.
methods.risks: Seasons with few clear scenes (2016) leave gaps in the causal value series, so require at least 3 observations in the trailing 30 days or mark the value as low confidence. The predictive-t step assumes approximately normal inter-annual variability per DOY. Check with a PIT histogram, or fall back to the empirical percentile.
methods.validation_plan: Pre-registered: (i) calibration: the share of z_cal<=-1 over 2016-2024 must lie in 13-19% and |z_cal|>2 in 2.5-7% (PIT histogram chi-square p>0.05). (ii) Paired year-block dR vs the current z on identical days: adopt the causal Whittaker only if the lower 90% bound of dR > -0.05 (non-inferior) and the dekad-to-dekad class flip rate does not increase. (iii) Re-score the dry-dekad events (M3) with the new z.

methods.name: M3. Event-based verification with base-rate-independent scores, ROC/PR curves and pre-registered threshold choice
methods.description: Extend the POD/FAR rows to a full verification table per layer (SMA warning, alert, watch) and per season (IV-X vs XI-III). Contingency scores: POD, FAR, POFD, CSI, ETS, HSS, Peirce (PSS), SEDI (Ferro and Stephenson 2011; base-rate independent, suited to rare dry events, base rate about 15%), and frequency bias. Continuous-score skill: ROC AUC and PR-AUC (average precision) with year-block CIs. Event (run) level: dry spells of at least 2 consecutive dekads matched by overlap, with hit ratio, false-event ratio and onset/offset lag in days. Thresholds are no longer fixed by convention alone. Choose them in a calibration period (2016-2021) by maximising PSS subject to frequency bias in 0.8-1.25, then freeze them and evaluate in a test period (2022-2026) with LOYO cross-validation as a sensitivity. Keep EDO's -1 as the published default when the selected value is within its CI. For the user-facing 'check vineyard' message, add a cost/loss relative-economic-value curve (Richardson 2000) as the reason for preferring specificity.
methods.why_better_than_ndvi_only: The product is a categorical warning, so it must be scored as one. A correlation of continuous anomalies does not tell a user how often a warning is false or late. SEDI and PSS remain meaningful for rare events, where CSI/HSS degrade.

evidence.citation: Own computation, a1_baseline_neff.py (312 dekads 2016-2024, ERA5 SMA vs ISMN 20-30 cm z<=-1, base rate 0.151)
evidence.finding: Threshold -1: POD 0.574, FAR 0.571, POFD 0.136, CSI 0.325, ETS 0.238, HSS 0.385 [0.11, 0.57], PSS 0.439 [0.12, 0.66], SEDI 0.606, bias 1.34. Threshold -1.2: bias 0.96, HSS 0.363. Threshold -0.8: HSS 0.401, bias 1.87. AUC 0.852 [0.76, 0.91]; PR-AUC 0.45. Event level: 8 of 11 observed events hit, 5 of 12 predicted events false, median onset lag +5 d (range -51 to +41 d). HSS: IV-X 0.34, XI-III 0.46.

evidence.citation: Ferro C.A.T. and Stephenson D.B. 2011, Weather and Forecasting 26:699-713, extremal dependence indices
evidence.finding: EDI/SEDI: verification measures for rare binary events that do not degenerate with rarity, are base-rate independent and harder to hedge. Used operationally by ECMWF and the UK Met Office.

evidence.citation: Wilks D.S., Statistical Methods in the Atmospheric Sciences (3rd/4th ed.); Jolliffe and Stephenson, Forecast Verification; Richardson D.S. 2000, QJRMS 126:649 (relative economic value)
evidence.finding: Standard definitions of HSS/PSS/ETS, ROC and the cost/loss value framework for categorical warnings.

methods.data_needed: Existing gwl_status and ISMN dekads. Later, the multi-station references (M4) and the vine-response references (M5).
methods.feasible_in_colab_gee: Yes. Extend step_07.validate_anomalies section 4 (events_dekad) with sklearn.metrics (roc_auc_score, average_precision_score) and about 60 lines of code. No GEE.
methods.expected_gain: Choosing a threshold for bias of about 1 removes about 25% of SMA warnings with a small HSS loss (0.385 to 0.363) and FAR 0.571 to 0.533. Event-level lag statistics give the card a defensible 'typical delay' number. Separate skill for growing season vs winter.
methods.risks: With about 11 events and 9 seasons, threshold optimisation over-fits. Restrict the grid to {-0.8, -1.0, -1.2, -1.5}, select in the calibration years only, and report the test-period result even if worse. Over 180 IV-X dekads the CIs of HSS/PSS will remain wide (about +-0.2).
methods.validation_plan: Pre-register the selection rule and grid. Report a calibration (2016-2021) vs test (2022-2026) table. Acceptance for the SMA warning: test-period AUC >= 0.80 with lower CI >= 0.70; PSS >= 0.40; frequency bias 0.8-1.25; event hit ratio >= 0.7; false-event ratio <= 0.35 (currently 0.42, fails).

methods.name: M4. Multi-reference soil-layer validation: SMOSMANIA multi-station, Gers in-situ composite, triple collocation with SMAP L4 root zone
methods.description: Move V1/V2 from one probe to a reference set. (a) Extract ERA5-Land layers at each of the 21 SMOSMANIA stations in GEE (point series, as in step_01.sync_era5_land_point). Compute anomaly R and event skill per station with the M1 CIs. Report the median and the station distribution. (b) Build a Gers composite reference: the mean anomaly of Condom, PeyrusseGrande, Lahas, CreondArmagnac and Savenes (20-30 cm, after QC). Score ERA5 against the composite and against each station, so the card can state the representativeness ceiling. (c) Triple collocation: use the extended TC of McColl 2014 (pytesmo.metrics.tcol_metrics with bootstrapped CIs) on anomalies of ERA5-Land RZ, ISMN 20-30 cm, and SMAP L4 sm_rootzone (GEE NASA/SMAP/SPL4SMGP/008, 9 km, 2015-present, a different model and forcing with SMAP Tb assimilation). This gives R of each against the unknown truth without treating the probe as error-free. (d) Diagnose the probe floor effect: flag days within 0.02 m3/m3 of the station's 2% quantile and score summer (VII-X) separately, or use 10-30 cm profile-weighted values. This is complementary to Z8 (depth matching) and Z10 (CGLS SWI as an extra source). The new element is that the validation reference itself becomes a quantified, multi-source estimate.
methods.why_better_than_ndvi_only: Every downstream layer (warning, then alert) inherits the soil-layer skill. A single grass-plot probe that bottoms out in August is a weak judge of either ERA5 or vegetation. Multi-reference and TC scores are the community standard (QA4SM/CEOS LPV) that EO employers recognise.

evidence.citation: Own computation, a3_paired_floor_neighbours.py
evidence.finding: Inter-station anomaly R vs Condom: PeyrusseGrande 0.54 (35 km), Lahas 0.53 (65 km), CreondArmagnac 0.35 (31 km), Savenes 0.34 (69 km). ERA5 Condom-cell vs ISMN Condom 0.583. ETC (n=1205; ERA5, Condom, neighbour composite): R_ERA5 = 0.62 [0.43, 0.80]. Probe floor: days within 0.02 m3/m3 of the 2% quantile (0.022) are 18% in Jul, 21% Aug, 25% Sep, 30% Oct. The 20-30 cm SD is 0.030 in Aug vs 0.114 in May. NDVI-vs-probe R is 0.12 in August.

evidence.citation: Gruber A. et al. 2013, Vadose Zone Journal 12, Characterizing coarse-scale representativeness of in situ soil moisture measurements from ISMN
evidence.finding: TC on more than 1400 ISMN stations: representativeness errors of 0.02-0.06 m3/m3, smaller at depth and for anomalies. QC and representative-site selection are needed before using in situ as reference.

evidence.citation: McColl K.A. et al. 2014, GRL 41:6229-6236, extended triple collocation
evidence.finding: TC yields each system's correlation with the unknown target (and error variance) from three collocated systems with independent errors.

evidence.citation: Gruber A. et al. 2016, Int. J. Appl. Earth Obs. Geoinf. 45:200-211; Gruber A. et al. 2020, Remote Sens. Environ. 244:111806 (validation good practices, CEOS LPV endorsed)
evidence.finding: Review of soil-moisture TC assumptions and a recommended validation protocol: anomalies, preprocessing, statistical presentation. Implemented in QA4SM.

evidence.citation: Google Earth Engine catalog, NASA/SMAP/SPL4SMGP/008
evidence.finding: SMAP L4 3-hourly surface and root-zone (0-100 cm) soil moisture, 9 km EASE-2 (about 11 km in GEE), from 31 Mar 2015, public domain. Model-only during outages 19 Jun - 23 Jul 2019 and 6 Aug - 20 Sep 2022.

methods.data_needed: ISMN files for 21 SMOSMANIA stations (already in data/7_isismn_data); ERA5-Land and SMAP L4 point series per station from GEE (about 22 x 2 small extractions).
methods.feasible_in_colab_gee: Yes. A new task_validate_network loops over stations and reuses step_07.insitu_daily_depth and clim_anomaly. The GEE point extractions take minutes. TC via pytesmo.metrics.tcol_metrics.
methods.expected_gain: Turns 'R=0.58 at one probe' into 'median R across N stations, plus R vs truth from TC', the format of published product validations. The summer floor flag explains the August collapse and stops the vegetation layer being judged on uninformative days. Likely shows that ERA5's true skill is higher than the probe suggests.
methods.risks: TC needs independent errors. ERA5 and SMAP L4 share some forcing (reanalysis meteorology), which biases TC toward inflated R for both. Report the cross-correlated-error caveat and, as a sensitivity, a triplet with S-1 or CGLS SWI. Station QC: CreondArmagnac shows R of about 0 with the Condom-cell ERA5 and sensor segments ML3 to ML2x, so apply the Condom QC rules to every station. Only 0.583 vs 0.62 may separate the methods.
methods.validation_plan: Acceptance (pre-registered): median station anomaly R >= 0.50, and at least 70% of stations have a lower CI bound > 0.30. TC R of ERA5 RZ >= 0.60 with lower CI >= 0.45. Report summer-only (VII-X) skill separately, with no threshold, and flag floor days.

methods.name: M5. The right target for a vine water-stress alert: a validation ladder (soil, modelled vine water balance, must delta13C, ApeX shoot growth, impacts)
methods.description: Stop validating the alert class against soil moisture: alert = soil dry AND vine responds, so a soil target can only penalise it. Validate each layer against the quantity it claims to represent. L0 (soil, warning): M4. L1 (modelled vine water status, pseudo-reference): a vine FTSW water-balance model (Lebon 2003 bilinear transpiration vs FTSW; FTSW to predawn LWP relation of Pellegrino 2004/2005) driven by ERA5-Land P and FAO-56 PM ET0, with TTSW 100-200 mm as a sensitivity range. Report agreement of the vegetation anomaly with FTSW anomalies (not circular w.r.t. the S-2 layer; partly circular w.r.t. SPI). L2 (integrated vine water status, parcel-specific, annual): carbon isotope ratio delta13C of grape must sugars at harvest for the 15 parcels. Classes: below -26 permille no deficit; -26 to -24.5 mild; -24.5 to -23 moderate; -23 to -21.5 moderate-strong; above -21.5 severe. Request it from Cave de Condom (cooperatives routinely sample must) or run about 15 analyses per year. This is the only realistic parcel-level truth for the parcel-specific S-2 claim. L3 (in-season vine response): ApeX iG-Apex shoot-tip observations (50 apices, weekly June-August) at the 15 parcels, validated vs predawn LWP in the -0.2 to -0.8 MPa range (Pichon et al. 2023). Ask the national ApeX-Vigne database (2019-2025, 34k observations) for observations near Condom. L4 (impacts, qualitative): Agreste/Douanes Gers vine yield (hl/ha), the VigiEau/Propluvia restriction history for the Condom alert zone (Etalab open data), and calamites agricoles decisions. Use these only as a pre-registered season-level event catalogue, with confounders flagged: frost (ERA5-Land Tmin <= -1 C after budburst, e.g. 3-4 Apr 2022), hail and mildew years.
methods.why_better_than_ndvi_only: This directly answers the known limitation. NDVI vs a grass-plot probe is an indirect target, and the data show it is the weakest available reference: the S-2 anomaly agrees better with modelled FTSW and ERA5 RZ. delta13C and iG-Apex measure the vine itself, so any richer vegetation index (NDMI, NDWI/EVI, fAPAR, LST in Z11-Z14) can finally be ranked by what matters: vine water status.

evidence.citation: Own computation, a6_spei_wb_alert.py and a6b.py (identical 245 scene days, VINEYARD_06 SR NDVI anomaly)
evidence.finding: R of NDVI anomaly with: ISMN 20-30 cm 0.433; simple FTSW bucket (TTSW 150 mm, Hargreaves ET0) 0.553 (dR +0.12 [0.015, 0.258]); ERA5 RZ 0.580 (+0.148 [0.002, 0.311]); SPEI-3 (empirical) 0.494; SPI-3 0.469. Alert vs ISMN dry dekads in IV-X: 16 flagged, precision 0.25, POD 0.14. Warning-or-alert: precision 0.39, POD 0.59. Alert dekads: 2017 6, 2019 2, 2022 6, 2023 2 (2023 has 0 probe-dry dekads). ERA5-Land Tmin -2.2/-2.5 C on 3-4 Apr 2022.

evidence.citation: Lebon E. et al. 2003, Functional Plant Biology 30:699-710; Pellegrino A. et al. 2004/2005, Plant and Soil 266
evidence.finding: Vineyard water-balance model with bilinear relative transpiration vs FTSW; a close, site-stable FTSW-predawn LWP relationship (same for Syrah in southern France and Gewurztraminer in Alsace), valid if TTSW is correctly estimated.

evidence.citation: van Leeuwen C. et al. 2009, J. Int. Sci. Vigne Vin 43(3):121-134; class thresholds as tabulated in Rienth 2023 review (after Carbonneau 1998)
evidence.finding: Must-sugar delta13C and stem water potential are accurate plot-scale vine water status tools. delta13C below -26 permille means no deficit, above -21.5 permille severe; it integrates the season (measured at harvest).

evidence.citation: Pichon L. et al. 2023, OENO One (ApeX method validation); 2026 OENO One crowdsourcing study (ApeX-Vigne 2019-2025)
evidence.finding: iG-Apex validated vs predawn LWP on 55 fields (Tavel, 2008-2012), operational for -0.2 to -0.8 MPa; not specific to water. The national crowdsourced database holds 34,233 observations, 11,481 fields, 771 contributors.

evidence.citation: DDFiP Gers, TFNB degrevement 2022 (perte de recoltes); data.gouv.fr Donnee Secheresse VigiEau/Propluvia
evidence.finding: Gers vineyard 2022: spring bud-loss survey median 70%, aggravated by summer drought, plus hail in June, so 2022 is not drought-only. The VigiEau dataset gives yearly CSVs of all drought restriction decrees (Etalab 2.0); coverage before 2015 is uneven.

evidence.citation: Agreste Occitanie, Memento 2024 (vine production by departement)
evidence.finding: Gers 2022: about 1.365 Mhl on about 20,361 ha (about 67 hl/ha, all wines; column alignment to be checked). Departemental yields are available yearly but mix frost, hail, market and drought effects.

methods.data_needed: L1: ERA5-Land DAILY_AGGR extra bands (temperature_2m_max, surface_solar_radiation_downwards_sum, u/v wind, dewpoint) for FAO-56 PM; soil TTSW from the BDGSF/ESDAC available-water map or a literature range. L2: must delta13C per parcel from the cooperative, or 15 samples per year at about 20-40 EUR each (own estimate, unverified). L3: an ApeX app protocol at 15 parcels in 2027, or a data request to the ApeX-Vigne team. L4: VigiEau CSVs, Agreste/Douanes yields, Meteo-France bulletins.
methods.feasible_in_colab_gee: L1 is fully feasible (GEE bands + about 80 lines of Python). L4 desk data are free. L2/L3 need a partner (Cave de Condom / GIEE, Chambre d'agriculture du Gers / IFV Sud-Ouest), fitting the 2027 pilot already in Plan_v6 (V5). Nothing needs paid data.
methods.expected_gain: Converts the 'alert not validated' limitation into a staged, citable plan, with an immediate quantitative L1 result. With 15 parcels x 2-3 seasons of delta13C (n of about 30-45 parcel-years), a Spearman rho of 0.5 would be detectable: power about 0.8 at alpha 0.05 for n of about 30 (own estimate). This is the only design that can validate between-parcel differences, which are the S-2 layer's real job.
methods.risks: FTSW shares forcing with SPI/ERA5, so it is not independent for the warning layer. delta13C is annual (no timing) and confounded by nitrogen status and rootstock. ApeX is operator-dependent and not water-specific. Yields and administrative records are confounded (2022 frost and hail). Partner data may not be released. Keep L4 qualitative.
methods.validation_plan: Pre-register. L1: report R and the event agreement of the S-2 anomaly vs FTSW anomaly (VI-IX) next to the probe result. L2: Spearman rho between the per-parcel season mean of calibrated veg z (VI-IX) and must delta13C, acceptance rho >= 0.5 with year-block CI lower > 0, plus a between-parcel test (parcel ranks within a year). L3: alert dekads vs iG-Apex <= 0.25 within +-10 days, precision reported. L4: a season-level event catalogue fixed before scoring, hit/miss with an exact binomial CI, confounded seasons excluded or flagged.

methods.name: M6. SPEI done properly (FAO-56 PM ET0, L-moment or GEV fit, goodness-of-fit gate) as the climatic-water-balance driver
methods.description: Z9 already proposes SPEI-3 on the card; this is the statistical recipe and the test. Ingest temperature_2m_max/min, radiation, wind and dewpoint from ERA5-Land DAILY_AGGR. Compute FAO-56 Penman-Monteith ET0 (Hargreaves only as a fallback; the Tmax = 2 Tmean - Tmin approximation is not needed once Tmax is ingested). Compute SPEI-1/3 on P - ET0 with the 1991-2020 reference, fitted by L-moments (log-logistic as in the SPEI R package / Begueria 2014) and GEV as an alternative (Stagge 2015). Gate: Shapiro-Wilk on the resulting index per DOY window and the PIT histogram. If more than 10% of windows fail, use the empirical Gringorten-plotting-position SPEI. Test it like any indicator: paired dR vs SPI with M1 CIs, against the in-situ composite (M4) and against vegetation anomalies, plus heat-drought attribution flags.
methods.why_better_than_ndvi_only: It adds atmospheric demand (heat) to the driver chain. 2022 and 2026 were heat-droughts, and a vegetation decline under high ET0 but normal precipitation is otherwise mis-attributed. Statistical rigour in the fit avoids a common pitfall that silently degrades the index.

evidence.citation: Own computation, a6_spei_wb_alert.py (ERA5-Land Condom cell, ET0 Hargreaves with approximate Tmax, ET0 949 mm/yr vs P 733 mm/yr)
evidence.finding: The SciPy MLE 3-parameter log-logistic fit failed KS at 75% (SPEI-1) and 100% (SPEI-3) of DOY windows and degraded R with ISMN to 0.27 / 0.20. Empirical SPEI: SPEI-1 R 0.521 (IV-X 0.509) vs SPI-1 0.504 (0.456); SPEI-3 0.425 (IV-X 0.466) vs SPI-3 0.403 (0.404). Dry-dekad AUC IV-X: SPEI-1 0.686 vs SPI-1 0.653; ERA5 RZ 0.822. vs NDVI anomaly (same days): SPEI-3 0.494 vs SPI-3 0.469 (dR +0.025, n.s.).

evidence.citation: Begueria S., Vicente-Serrano S.M., Reig F., Latorre B. 2014, Int. J. Climatol. 34:3001-3023, SPEI revisited
evidence.finding: Log-logistic fitted by L-moments (scale, shape, origin) on P - PET. PET method choices: Thornthwaite, Hargreaves, Penman. Occasional fit failures yield NaN.

evidence.citation: Stagge J.H. et al. 2015, Int. J. Climatol. 35:4027-4040, candidate distributions for SPI and SPEI
evidence.finding: Recommends GEV for SPEI in Europe (gamma for SPI). Later work uses normality tests of the index as a diagnostic. The choice of distribution is debated (Vicente-Serrano and Begueria 2016 reply).

evidence.citation: Bachmair S. et al. 2018, Environ. Res. Lett. 13:034042
evidence.finding: Across Europe, short accumulation SPI/SPEI best track crop vegetation stress (NUTS3, satellite VIs), with large regional differences.

methods.data_needed: Extra ERA5-Land DAILY_AGGR bands (Tmax, solar radiation, 10 m u/v wind, 2 m dewpoint), 1991-present at the parcel point.
methods.feasible_in_colab_gee: Yes. A small change to step_01.sync_era5_land_point (more band names; the cache needs a refetch), PM ET0 in numpy (about 40 lines), and lmoments3 or scipy genextreme with a GOF gate.
methods.expected_gain: A modest gain in skill (+0.02 to +0.05 R, n.s. at one site) but better attribution (heat vs rain deficit) on the card, and a statistically defensible index rather than a mis-fitted one.
methods.risks: Small gains may not survive M1 CIs. Do not put SPEI into the status logic unless its paired test passes. ERA5-Land radiation and wind biases enter ET0. The reference-period choice (1991-2020) must match SPI.
methods.validation_plan: GOF gate as above. Paired year-block dR vs SPI on the in-situ composite (M4) and on the vegetation anomaly. Enters the status (replacing SPI-3 in 'watch') only if the lower 90% bound of dR > 0 and dry-dekad AUC does not decrease. Otherwise it stays a card driver only.

methods.name: M7. External benchmark consistency with Copernicus EDO/GDO products (CDI, LISFLOOD SMA, fAPAR anomaly)
methods.description: Download the EDO CDI v4, Soil Moisture Anomaly (LISFLOOD, 5 km, baseline 1995-2020) and MODIS/VIIRS fAPAR anomaly (1/24 deg) dekadal grids from the JRC Data Catalogue for the cells covering Condom and the 15 parcels. Compute: (a) Cohen's weighted kappa and a confusion matrix between AgriWatch status and EDO CDI class per dekad (2016-2026), with the recovery classes grouped; (b) anomaly R (M1 CIs) between ERA5-Land SMA and LISFLOOD SMA; (c) R between the S-2 vineyard anomaly and the EDO fAPAR anomaly, i.e. parcel vs landscape. Also mirror how EDO evaluates CDI: run the M3 event catalogue through both systems and compare hit and false-alarm rates. Position this as consistency with the operational reference, not truth.
methods.why_better_than_ndvi_only: It shows an EO reviewer that the product reproduces the official European indicator where it should (soil, landscape vegetation) and deviates only where it adds parcel information. The S-2 minus fAPAR-anomaly residual is a parcel-specific signal that NDVI alone cannot separate from regional greenness.

evidence.citation: Sepulcre-Canto G. et al. 2012, NHESS 12:3519-3531, development of the Combined Drought Indicator
evidence.finding: CDI evaluated on the major European drought episodes 2000-2011 using EM-DAT and Eurostat annual yields, including early-warning capability and robustness against false alarms.

evidence.citation: Cammalleri C. et al. 2021, NHESS 21:481-495, revision of the CDI used in EDO
evidence.finding: Revised vs old CDI compared on actual European drought events of the last 20 years, with about 70% fewer temporal stage-sequencing inconsistencies. A referee requested a more quantitative assessment.

evidence.citation: JRC Data Catalogue, EDO fAPAR anomaly / SMA / CDI datasets
evidence.finding: fAPAR anomaly: 10-day MODIS, standardised vs 2002-last full year, 1/24 deg. SMA: 5 km, baseline 1995-2020. CDI v4.0.0 with GeoTIFF/NetCDF/WMS. Free download.

methods.data_needed: EDO CDI, SMA and fAPAR anomaly dekadal rasters 2016-present for a small bbox (a few MB).
methods.feasible_in_colab_gee: Yes. A direct download from the JRC catalogue in Colab (requests + rasterio), not via GEE. One new task, benchmark_edo.
methods.expected_gain: A citable agreement number (kappa, R) with the Copernicus reference, plus a parcel-minus-landscape vegetation residual that can be tested in M5.
methods.risks: EDO grids are 5 km and 1/24 deg, so the comparison is consistency only. EDO versions and baselines change (v4.1 rules), so record the version. fAPAR from MODIS at 500 m mixes land covers around Condom.
methods.validation_plan: Report without a pass/fail threshold, except as sanity checks: kappa of warning-or-worse vs EDO warning-or-worse >= 0.4, and SMA anomaly R >= 0.6. Large disagreements trigger an investigation (ERA5 vs LISFLOOD) rather than a model change.

methods.name: M8. Protection against the garden of forking paths: pre-registration, held-out seasons, multiple-testing control, multiverse plot, negative controls
methods.description: F3 already queues about 15 variants (5 water indices x 2 resolutions x edge buffers x seasons x smoothing). To make the eventual choice defensible: (a) freeze a pre-registration file (YAML in docs/evidence) listing hypotheses, metrics, margins and decision rules before each run (this extends the existing 'zapisane przed testem' practice into a machine-readable form); (b) select index, season (Z2) and threshold by LOYO cross-validation on 2016-2023, and confirm on held-out 2024-2026 seasons; (c) control multiplicity across the candidate set with Holm (few tests) or Benjamini-Hochberg FDR (Wilks 2016) on placebo-based p-values; (d) publish a multiverse (specification-curve) plot of R and HSS across all reasonable pipeline choices, not just the best one; (e) negative controls: an irrigated parcel if any, a woodland or permanent-grass polygon, and the year-shuffled placebo, all of which must not respond like the vineyard to dry years; (f) stability metric: the dekad-to-dekad class flip rate.
methods.why_better_than_ndvi_only: Moving beyond NDVI multiplies the number of tested variants. Without this control, the best of 15 indices will look better by chance. With N_eff of about 7, a +0.05 gain is well inside the noise.

evidence.citation: Wilks D.S. 2016, BAMS 97:2263-2273, The stippling shows statistically significant grid points
evidence.finding: Naive per-test significance overstates results. FDR control is recommended, being only mildly sensitive to autocorrelation.

evidence.citation: Steegen S. et al. 2016, Perspectives on Psychological Science 11:702-712, multiverse analysis
evidence.finding: Run all reasonable processing choices and report the distribution of results, which shows how much conclusions depend on arbitrary choices.

evidence.citation: Own computation, a8_placebo.py and a2_veg_anomaly.py
evidence.finding: Year-derangement placebo null for NDVI-vs-probe R: 95th pct 0.19, 99th pct 0.30. Observed 0.433. R without 2022: 0.394; without 2017 and 2022: 0.393, so the result is not driven by a single year.

methods.data_needed: Existing data. A list of candidate variants. Optional negative-control polygons drawn in the AOI.
methods.feasible_in_colab_gee: Yes. Orchestration only (loop over configs in task_validate), plus a matplotlib multiverse plot. The negative-control polygons reuse site_stats.
methods.expected_gain: Protects every future claim (Z2-Z14) from selection bias. Produces two figures (multiverse plot, placebo histogram) that read as professional to EO and data-science reviewers.
methods.risks: Held-out seasons are few (3), so the confirmation has low power. State this explicitly and treat confirmation as a 'no contradiction' check. Pre-registration adds overhead to each experiment (about 15 minutes).
