methods.validation_plan: Each experiment report includes: the pre-registration hash, the CV-selected choice, the held-out result, an adjusted p (Holm/BH), the multiverse percentile of the chosen variant, the negative-control response, and the flip rate.

research.top_recommendation:
Adopt a written protocol AgriWatch Validation Protocol v1.1 before adding any new index. Order of work: M1 + M8 (1.5 + 1.5 d), then M2 (2 d), then M3 (1.5 d), then M4 (3 d), then M5-L1 (part of 3 d), with M6/M7 after. About 12-15 person-days, all in Colab/GEE with free data.

P0, applies to every metric:
- Report n, N_eff, Pearson and Spearman, and a season-block bootstrap 95% CI (B >= 2000).
- Product and reference use the same climatology definition.
- Decisions use the paired dR with superiority if the lower 90% bound is > 0, or TOST equivalence at +-0.05.
- Run a year-shuffle placebo.
- Pre-register in YAML, select variants by LOYO-CV on 2016-2023, confirm on 2024-2026, and apply Holm/BH across candidates.

V1, soil layer:
- Condom anomaly R >= 0.50 with lower CI >= 0.40 (now 0.583 [0.51, 0.67], pass).
- SMOSMANIA median R >= 0.50, with at least 70% of stations having a lower CI > 0.30.
- TC R (ERA5-Land, ISMN, SMAP L4) >= 0.60.
- Report summer floor days separately.

V2, dry-dekad events:
- Test-period AUC >= 0.80 with lower CI >= 0.70 (now 0.852 [0.76, 0.91], pass).
- PSS >= 0.40.
- Frequency bias 0.8-1.25 (now 1.34, fail; a -1.2 threshold gives 0.96).
- Event hit ratio >= 0.70 (now 0.73, pass) and false-event ratio <= 0.35 (now 0.42, fail).
- Also report SEDI, HSS, ETS and onset lag.

V3, vegetation layer:
- Placebo p < 0.01 (pass) and year-block lower CI > 0 (pass, barely: 0.06).
- Calibration: z<=-1 frequency 13-19% (now 19.6%, fail) and |z|>2 frequency 2.5-7% (now 9.4%, fail). Fix both with a year-weighted climatology and predictive-t.
- A new index or variant enters the status only if it is paired-superior to NDVI, or is equivalent and has another advantage. SR vs 10 m already shows equivalence (+0.004 [0.000, 0.009]), so SR is justified only for maps and edge handling.

V4, alert (vine response): do not score it against soil moisture.
- L1: agreement with a vine FTSW water-balance model, reported now (S-2 anomaly vs FTSW R = 0.553 vs 0.433 for the probe).
- L2: Spearman rho >= 0.5 between per-parcel season vegetation z and must delta13C, over at least 30 parcel-years.
- L3: alert precision vs ApeX iG-Apex in the 2027 pilot.

V5, events:
- Fix a season-level catalogue in advance from VigiEau, Agreste, Meteo-France and EDO.
- Score it with exact binomial CIs.
- Flag confounders: frost (3-4 Apr 2022), hail, mildew.

The single most valuable next action is two-fold. First, re-run v1.0 under P0, M2 and M3; this costs about 4 days and needs no new data. Second, email Cave de Condom about harvest must delta13C or sampling for the 15 parcels: it is the only affordable parcel-level truth for the parcel-specific S-2 claim.
not_recommended: Reporting vegetation-anomaly CIs from 30-day calendar blocks or from i.i.d. bootstrap (the pytesmo default): with N_eff of about 7 they are about 2x too narrow (reported [0.24, 0.59] vs year-block [0.06, 0.64]).
Correlating smoothed or interpolated daily S-2 series over all days: this is pseudo-replication (n jumps from 245 to 1749 while R drops to 0.31), and both n and p become meaningless.

Validating the 'alert' class against soil moisture (ISMN or ERA5): alert = soil AND vine, so a soil target can only penalise it. Using ERA5 RZ as the reference for the alert is also circular, because ERA5 defines the warning.
Treating the 20-30 cm grass-plot probe as the sole truth in VII-X: 21-30% of days sit at the sensor floor and monthly R collapses (August 0.12).
Using 2022 as a clean drought positive control: Gers had a 3-4 April frost (median bud loss 70%) and June hail. Flag it or exclude it from drought-only tests (V4 in Plan_v6 needs this caveat).
A GDD (thermal-time) aligned climatology for vineyard NDVI anomalies: tested, worse than DOY (R 0.377 vs 0.433).

Fitting a 3-parameter log-logistic SPEI by SciPy MLE without a goodness-of-fit gate: KS failed in 75-100% of DOY windows and R fell from about 0.43 to 0.20. Use L-moments or GEV, or an empirical fallback.
Selecting season, threshold or index on the full 2016-2024 record and reporting skill on the same data (e.g. Z2 VI-IX without LOYO-CV): over-fitting with about 11 events and 9 seasons.
Claiming SR 2.5 m improves detection: the paired test shows equivalence (dR +0.004 [0.000, 0.009]), not superiority. State 'equivalent; used for maps and edge handling'.

Triple collocation with two in-situ references (Condom plus a neighbour composite) as final evidence: representativeness errors are not independent. Use ERA5 + ISMN + SMAP L4 (or SWI) and report the cross-correlated-error caveat.

Departemental yield statistics (Agreste) or calamites agricoles as a quantitative skill target: n of about 10 seasons, confounded by frost, hail, market and pruning. Use them only as a qualitative event catalogue.
Raw z-thresholds on S-2 anomalies without calibration: z<=-1 fires 19.6% and |z|>2 fires 9.4% instead of the nominal 15.9% and 4.6%.

result.best_variant: None clearly wins. V6 (phenology-relative harmonic anomaly, LOYO) gives the only consistent small gain: +0.016 R, CI [-0.002,0.033], better in 6/9 years, same sign at 10 m and for the grass plot. It is worth adopting for its more stable climatology, not as an accuracy claim. For the alert, the causal 30-day mean (V1c) is the only variant whose alert precision is not below warning, but that difference is not significant either.
result.conclusion: I reproduced v1.0 exactly: NDVI SR R=0.433 [0.24,0.59] (n=245), and the status matches the registry for all 324 dekads. None of the 15 physically motivated variants beats plain NDVI against ISMN 20-30 cm. The variants were smoothing or gap-filling (Whittaker, causal or not, and a 30-day mean), water indices (NDMI, NDRE, CRSWIR), composites (mean-z, PC1), the vine-minus-grass contrast, lags, a phenology-relative climatology and a within-season decline. Every CI includes the baseline or lies below it. NDMI, NDRE and CRSWIR score lower than NDVI, so F3's hypothesis that a water index will beat NDVI is not supported for this parcel. NDVI is also not the main limitation. (1) About half of R=0.43 comes from differences between years: R of the yearly means is 0.59 (n=9 years), while R within years is 0.29 [0.04,0.50] and negative in 2016, 2017, 2019 and 2022. The vegetation anomaly is a seasonal signal, not a dekadal one. (2) Vegetation adds no detectable soil-moisture information beyond ERA5: partial R given ERA5 RZ is 0.11 [-0.19,0.34]. (3) Scene-level events are poorly detected: veg z<=-1 vs ISMN z<=-1 gives POD 0.06, FAR 0.91, HSS -0.10. At the dekadal level, vegetation confirmation lowers precision from 0.39 (warning) to 0.25 (alert). (4) ISMN 20-30 cm is a weak truth for summer vine stress. The soil reaches its floor every August (0.07 m3/m3, SD 0.035), so the 2022 drought shows only z of about -0.5 at that depth. All VI-IX alerts (2022) therefore score as false, and vines may draw water from deeper than 30 cm. Recommendations: keep NDVI at 10 m or SR (they are equivalent) as the alert layer, and optionally switch to the LOYO harmonic climatology (V6) for stability. Present the vegetation anomaly as an 'impact/response' layer on a monthly scale (30-day causal mean), not as a dekadal confirmation of soil drought. Stop judging the alert against soil moisture, and get a vine-relevant truth before claiming the alert detects vine stress: stem water potential or must δ13C, for example from regional IFV or Chambre d'agriculture networks (not checked), or yield records. With only one ERA5 cell, the most promising parcel-specific route is a spatial anomaly against the other 14 AOI vineyards, which needs their S-2 statistics in the registry.
caveats: Single station and 9 years (2016-2024). The year-block CIs are wide (B0: 0.09 to 0.63), so differences under about 0.05 in R cannot be resolved.
15 signal variants plus 4 extra lag targets and 12 alert-level runs were tested, all reported. With this many comparisons, the small V6 gain (CI lower bound -0.002) is not significant.

The reference is indirect: ISMN 20-30 cm under a grass plot 136 m away, not vine water status. Its summer floor effect counts the 2022 vineyard anomalies as false alarms. Neither the alert nor the vine-specific variants (V4, V7) can really be validated with this reference.
The 10 cm ISMN sensor only covers 2016 to 2020-11 (n about 127).

Whittaker lambda was chosen on S-2 data only (LOO-CV, flat between 300 and 3000), so there is no leakage from the target. The non-causal smoothers use future scenes and are not operational. The real-time versions lose about 15 early-season dates.
Vineyard NDVI drifts upward from 2016 to 2024 (spring NDVI 0.3 to 0.6), probably from inter-row management. That drift lines up with the ISMN dry-to-wet sequence and may inflate the between-year R.

The literature context was only partly checked: one web search on S-2 vs Ψstem (Cheret et al. 2021, Remote Sensing 13:1837; red-edge/SWIR multi-band models reach R2 about 0.40; seen as a search summary). A 2017 spring-frost explanation for the spring 2017 anomalies is not supported by ERA5-Land Tmin, so I dropped it.
result.implementation_notes: All code is under the exp_veg directory and imports the repo read-only. common.py reuses step_04.scene_anomaly, clim_anomaly, build_status and era5_anomalies, and step_07.insitu_daily_depth and _block_bootstrap_ci, so the definitions are identical to v1.0. smooth.py holds a weighted robust Whittaker smoother (Tukey bisquare, 2 iterations) on a daily Apr-Oct grid, its causal variant, and the other-year climatology. variants.py has the builders for B0 and V1-V8, with LOYO for PC1 and the harmonic fit. Every variant is evaluated on the B0 scene days, with a paired R difference (shared 30-day-block resamples), a year-block CI, per-year wins, partial R given ERA5, and scene-level and dekadal event skill. Run order: a0_baseline, a1_lambda_cv, a2_eval, a3_lag, a4_alert (+a4b, a4c), a5_decomposition, a6_context. Total runtime is about 2 minutes. If V6 is adopted, it is a drop-in replacement for scene_anomaly in step_04: fit a 3-harmonic curve per site, product and index on the other years' clear scenes, and use the residual SD within +-30 d of other years.

verdict.experiment: A: vegetation / vine-water signal variants from S-2 parcel statistics (VINEYARD_06) vs ISMN Condom 20-30 cm climatological anomaly, 2016-2024. Reviewed scripts and outputs in exp_veg/; re-ran the key computations independently in exp_veg_verify/ (v0_base.py, v1_trend.py, v2_v6robust.py, v3_misc.py, v4_alert.py, v5_2022.py, v6_oper.py).

claims.claim: The v1.0 baseline is reproduced exactly: NDVI SR R=0.433 [0.24,0.59] n=245, NDVI 10 m 0.426, NDMI SR 0.409, CRSWIR -0.370, ERA5 RZ dekadal POD/FAR 0.574/0.571 (n=312), and the status matches the registry for all 324 dekads (18 alerts).
claims.reason: My own re-implementation (my scene anomaly, ISMN climatology and bootstrap; only the repo's ISMN QC reused) gives identical numbers: 0.433 [0.242,0.594] n=245; 10 m 0.426 n=247; NDMI 0.409; NDRE 0.382; CRSWIR -0.370. build_status on my B0 series agrees 100% with gwl_status.csv (324 dekads, 18 vs 18 alerts). Depths are matched exactly (0.20 and 0.30 m files), and the reference period and windows match validate_anomalies.

claims.claim: None of the 15 variants beats plain NDVI against ISMN 20-30 cm. Every paired CI includes 0 or lies below it.
claims.reason: Comparisons use the same dates (filtered to B0 scene days, with B0 R recomputed on the common days) and a paired bootstrap with shared resamples. My V6 re-implementation reproduces dR=+0.016 [-0.002,0.032] (year blocks), and no CI is clearly above 0. The negative result is robust.

claims.claim: V6 (3-harmonic, LOYO, pooled residual SD over +-30 d) gives a consistent small gain and is worth adopting for its more stable climatology.
claims.reason: The gain does not come from the 'phenology-relative' harmonic mean. Harmonic mean with the boxcar SD gives dR=+0.003; boxcar mean with the harmonic residual SD (+-30 d) gives +0.013. So nearly all of it comes from pooling the SD denominator. With a +-15 d SD window the gain falls to +0.006, and K=1 is worse (-0.018 to -0.028). The year-block CI never excludes 0 for any K or window. The 10 m and grass-plot 'replications' share the same scenes, years and ISMN target, so they are not independent. This is the best of 15 variants, not significant after selection.

claims.claim: Water indices (NDMI, NDRE, -CRSWIR) score lower than NDVI, so F3's hypothesis that a water index beats NDVI is not supported for this parcel.
claims.reason: Reproduced: NDMI 0.409, NDRE 0.382 (dR CI below 0), CRSWIR 0.370 (dR CI below 0). This only holds against a soil-moisture reference at this parcel. On the station grass plot at 10 m, NDMI beats NDVI (0.404 vs 0.372), so the index ranking is site-dependent and says nothing about leaf water content itself.

claims.claim: About half of R comes from between-year differences (yearly-mean R=0.59, n=9). Within-year R is 0.29 [0.04,0.50], negative in 2016, 2017, 2019 and 2022. The vegetation anomaly is a seasonal signal, not a dekadal one.
claims.reason: The numbers are reproduced. The between-year share of the covariance is 0.58, and my within-year R is 0.294 with a 30-d block CI of [0.08,0.49]. Because that CI excludes 0, 'not a dekadal signal' is overstated: the within-season signal is weak but positive. Monthly breakdown (new): R is 0.12 in April (n=25), 0.12 in August (n=43), 0.65 in September and 0.80 in October. The correlation is driven by September-October and by year offsets, not by the peak-stress period.

claims.claim: Vegetation adds no detectable soil-moisture information beyond ERA5: partial R given ERA5 RZ = 0.11 [-0.19,0.34].
claims.reason: Reproduced 0.106. The 30-d block CI [-0.11,0.30] also includes 0, so the result does not depend on the CI method. Extra check: in leave-one-year-out regression, adding NDVI z to ERA5 z lowers the held-out R with ISMN from 0.558 to 0.536 and raises RMSE from 0.759 to 0.777.

claims.claim: Scene-level events are poorly detected (POD 0.06, FAR 0.91, HSS -0.10). At dekadal level, vegetation confirmation lowers precision from 0.39 (warning) to 0.25 (alert).
claims.reason: Reproduced: 182 in-season dekads, 29 dry; warning 44 flags with precision 0.386; alert 16 flags with precision 0.25. A random 16-of-44 subset of warnings gives precision of 0.25 or lower with p=0.14. So 'does not raise precision' is solid, but 'lowers precision' is not statistically established.

claims.claim: ISMN 20-30 cm is a weak summer truth because of a floor effect: the soil reaches its floor every August (0.07 m3/m3, SD 0.035), so the 2022 drought shows only z of about -0.5, and the VI-IX 2022 alerts are false because of the reference.
claims.reason: Partly wrong. August means range from 0.037 to 0.097, and 2016, 2020, 2021 and 2024 are not near a floor, so 'every August' is false. A floor does exist at 30 cm in dry summers (2017, 2019 and 2022 minima 0.012, 0.011 and 0.014; z30 about -0.7 in each). But in 2022 the 20 cm sensor was not at its floor: the July to mid-September minimum was 0.059 vs 0.021-0.031 in 2017-2019, and z20 was about -0.26. June had 89 mm and August 51 mm of rain. The mild 2022 combined z comes mainly from a relatively moist 20 cm layer, not a floor at both depths. ERA5 RZ calls 2022 the driest summer (z -1.23). So the two products genuinely disagree in 2022; this is not simply a saturated reference.

claims.claim: The vineyard NDVI drift (spring NDVI 0.3 to 0.6) may inflate the between-year R.
claims.reason: The drift is real: April NDVI rises from 0.30 to 0.62, and corr(year, yearly veg z)=0.72. Its effect on R is modest. Removing linear trends changes the between-year R only from 0.59 to 0.55, and a leave-one-year-out detrended scene R is 0.388 vs 0.433. The larger consequence of the drift, which the experiment did not test, is on operational skill (next claim).

claims.claim: The reported R values (B0 and all variants, including V6) represent the skill the pipeline would have operationally.
claims.reason: Implicit claim, not tested by the experiment. Every vegetation anomaly uses an all-other-years climatology, including future years. With the strong upward NDVI trend, a past-years-only climatology (what the pipeline would have had at the time) gives R=0.337 vs 0.507 for B0 on the same 200 scene days (2018-2024). The paired difference is -0.17, year-block CI [-0.27,+0.01]. The hindcast R=0.43 overstates real-time skill, and V6 has the same non-stationarity problem.

claims.claim: Whittaker lambda was chosen without leakage, and the real-time variants lose about 15 early-season dates.
claims.reason: Lambda was chosen by S-2-only leave-one-out CV, and the curve is flat between 300 and 3000. The 15 dropped dates are all early April plus 2016-05-04, and on them B0 R=-0.26. The paired same-day comparison (B0 = 0.508 on 230 days) was the right call; the raw 0.477 vs 0.433 would have been misleading. One minor mismatch: the real-time endpoint value is standardised against non-causal smoothed curves from other years.

claims.claim: The lagged or integrated ISMN target (trailing 30 d) gives no significant gain.
claims.reason: All CIs include 0. The leave-one-year-out 'selected' R (0.405) pools targets with different variances (lag-0 z vs 30-d mean z) across folds, so it is not a clean comparison. That does not change the conclusion.

verdict.reran_check: Independent re-implementation (exp_veg_verify/v0_base.py): my own scene anomaly (other years, +-15 d circular DOY, clear_frac>=0.9, at least 5 reference scenes), my own ISMN climatological z (2016-2024, min_n=20) on the repo's QC'd 20/30 cm daily means, and my own 30-d and year-block bootstraps. Results: NDVI SR 0.433 [0.242,0.594] n=245; 10 m 0.426; NDMI 0.409; NDRE 0.382; CRSWIR -0.370. Status recomputed via s4.build_status: 100% agreement with the registry, 18 alerts. Alert and warning precision reproduced (0.25 vs 0.386). Partial R 0.106 reproduced. Additional tests: V6 sensitivity over K in {1,2,3,4,6}, SD window in {15,30,45} and mean/SD decomposition; plain boxcar window variants; the dates dropped by V1b and R by month; past-only (operational) climatology vs leave-one-year-out; linear detrending; per-depth ISMN z and ERA5/rain for summer 2022; autocorrelation (NDVI z at 30 d about 0.73, ISMN z about 0.32, so 30-d blocks are short and the year-block CIs are the more honest ones).
issues: Hindcast vs operational: every vegetation anomaly (B0, V6, all variants) uses an all-other-years climatology that includes future years. Combined with the strong upward NDVI trend, a past-only climatology lowers R from 0.51 to 0.34 on the same days (dR -0.17 [-0.27,+0.01]). The experiment does not test this, so neither the 0.433 baseline nor V6 shows operational skill.

V6 is mislabelled. Its small gain comes from pooling the SD denominator over +-30 d of harmonic residuals, not from a phenology-relative mean (the mean alone gives +0.003). The gain depends on that window choice (+-15 d gives +0.006) and is never significant. 'small_gain' should be 'no_clear_gain'.

The floor-effect explanation for the 2022 VI-IX 'false alarms' is partly wrong. 'Floor every August' is false, and in 2022 the 20 cm sensor stayed relatively moist (z about -0.26) while 30 cm was at its floor. The conclusion that the reference is to blame is not established, and ERA5 and ISMN genuinely disagree for summer 2022.
'Vegetation confirmation lowers precision' (0.39 to 0.25) is not significant (random-subset p=0.14; year-block CI [-0.30,+0.03]). Phrase it as 'does not raise precision'.

'Not a dekadal signal' is overstated: the within-year R of 0.29 has a 30-d block CI of [0.08,0.49], which excludes 0. Monthly R is dominated by September-October (0.65 and 0.80) and is 0.12 in August, so the relation is strongest outside the peak vine-stress period. The experiment did not report this.

30-day blocks are short relative to the persistence of the NDVI anomaly (autocorrelation about 0.73 at 30 d). The year-block CIs (B0 [0.08,0.63]) are the more defensible headline. Both are reported, and the paired dR CIs are similar under either method, so conclusions do not change.
The cross-site 'replications' of V6 (vineyard 10 m, grass plot SR and 10 m) share the same scenes, years and ISMN target. They are not independent evidence.
Leave-one-year-out lag selection in a3 pools targets with different variances across folds (lag-0 z vs 30-d mean). The 0.405 vs 0.442 comparison is not clean, though the conclusion holds.

The real-time Whittaker value (a noisier endpoint estimate) is standardised against climatology from interior smoothed values of other years, which slightly penalises V1b and V8b. This is minor and does not change the verdicts.
The experiment correctly reports all 15+ variants and does not cherry-pick. Multiple comparisons are acknowledged.
verdict.corrected_conclusion:
The core negative result holds. v1.0 is reproduced exactly (NDVI SR R=0.433 [0.24,0.59], n=245; status identical to the registry), and none of the 15 vegetation variants (smoothing, NDMI/NDRE/CRSWIR, composites, vine-minus-grass, lags, harmonic climatology, within-season decline) beats plain NDVI against ISMN 20-30 cm. Water indices score lower than NDVI at this parcel. NDVI adds no soil-moisture information beyond ERA5-Land (partial R 0.11, CI includes 0; adding NDVI to ERA5 does not improve held-out prediction of ISMN). Vegetation confirmation does not raise dekadal precision over 'warning' (0.25 vs 0.39, not significant).

Corrections:
(1) V6 is not a real improvement. Its +0.016 comes from pooling the SD over +-30 d, not from a phenology-relative mean. It depends on that window choice and is never significant, so it should not be presented as a gain. Adopt a pooled or residual SD only as a stability choice, if at all.
(2) The headline R values are hindcast numbers built on a climatology that uses future years. With the upward NDVI management trend (April NDVI 0.30 to 0.62), a past-years-only climatology lowers R to 0.34 vs 0.51 on the same days. Any change to the vegetation layer must be judged with a causal climatology, and the trend needs handling: for example a detrended climatology, a recent-years window, or a spatial anomaly against the other AOI vineyards, which cancels parcel-wide management and climate trends.
(3) The 2022 'false alarms' are not explained by a 20-30 cm floor effect. The 30 cm sensor was at its floor, but 20 cm stayed relatively moist after June and August rain, so ISMN and ERA5 genuinely disagree for summer 2022.
(4) The NDVI-ISMN relation is mostly between-year (58% of the covariance) and concentrated in September-October (R 0.65 and 0.80), with R of only 0.12 in August. A weak within-season signal remains (R 0.29, CI excludes 0).

The defensible recommendations still stand: keep NDVI (10 m and 2.5 m SR are equivalent), present it as a monthly impact/response layer rather than a dekadal confirmation of soil drought, stop validating the alert against soil moisture alone, and get vine-relevant truth (stem water potential, must δ13C, yield) before claiming the alert detects vine stress.

result.conclusion:
The S-2-driven FAO-56 water balance adds no parcel-specific skill beyond ERA5 and should not replace the NDVI anomaly as the parcel layer.

1. As a soil-moisture anomaly it matches ERA5 overall: R 0.563 vs 0.583, dR [-0.066, 0.024]. It is significantly worse in the growing season (IV-X dR -0.10 [-0.17, -0.03]; dry-dekad POD 0.21 vs 0.59) and better in winter. Dekadal POD/FAR are 0.36/0.53 vs 0.574/0.571.
2. The S-2 part of the signal is negligible. Observed vs climatological Kcb gives dR -0.005 [-0.014, 0.004], and the two anomaly series correlate at r = 0.997. SR 2.5 m and 10 m give identical results, and doubling the Kcb deviations does not help.
   - Physical reason: the regime is water-limited. With literature parameters, Ks < 1 about 177 days a year and mean August relative soil water is 0.09. Annual ETa is the same (~660 mm) for vine Kcb ~0.6 and grass Kcb ~0.8, so depletion is controlled by supply, not by canopy.
   - A lower NDVI lowers modelled ET, which damps the modelled deficit. So NDVI inside a water balance cannot act as a stress detector.
   - Since the vineyards share one ERA5 cell and Kcb barely moves the anomaly, the only real parcel-specific lever in a water balance is TAW (soil and rooting depth). TAW is unknown per parcel and cannot be validated with one station.
3. SPEI-like P-ET0 indices are not better than ERA5 (30 d: 0.542; 90 d: 0.439, significantly worse).
4. Two cheaper improvements came out of the diagnostics.
   - Matching the ERA5 layer to the probe depth (0-28 cm): R 0.691, better in 8 of 9 years. The gain is mostly in winter, and the probes say nothing about the deeper vine root zone.
   - Putting both anomalies on the same reference period when validating events: FAR drops from 0.571 to 0.467 with POD 0.511, so part of the v1.0 FAR is a definitional artefact.
5. Where a water balance does have value: it gives physically interpretable outputs (FTSW, Ks, deficit in mm, days-to-stress with a forecast) for a typical vineyard on this soil.
   - The current literature parameters put stress from April-May and an almost empty bucket every August. That is implausible for rainfed Gers vines.
   - So any absolute FTSW shown to a grower needs ET and TAW calibration against independent data first (ICOS ET, vine leaf water potential).
caveats: Single station and ~9 years. The reference sits under the station's grass plot at 20-30 cm, not under the vineyard, so 'parcel-specific' skill cannot be validated directly. The vine root zone (about 1 m or deeper) is also deeper than the probes.

Hargreaves ET0 uses Tmax approximated as 2*Tmean - Tmin, because there is no t2m_max. ERA5 Tmean is a 24-hour mean, so the diurnal range and ET0 are biased (annual ET0 ~950 mm, likely high or low by about 10%). With no wind, humidity or radiation, Kc_max uses the FAO standard climate value of 1.2. No runoff is modelled (clay soil, summer storms).

Literature verification is limited because fao.org and most publisher sites were blocked. Campos 2010 Kcb = 1.44 NDVI - 0.10 was confirmed only from abstract or index snippets. FAO-56 Table 19 clay values and the grapes p = 0.45 are from memory and were not verified online. Lebon 2003 and Pellegrino 2006 TAW ranges are at abstract level, via Plan_v5. A 2022 EGU abstract reports that the linear NDVI-Kcb method transferred poorly to another vineyard.

The vineyard NDVI mixes vine rows and the inter-row cover crop. Applying the Campos relation to it, plus an interpolated winter Kcb of ~0.7, probably overstates ET. Together with the small TAW, this gives the unrealistic early and persistent stress. It matters for absolute FTSW products, not much for anomalies.

Kcb before 2016 and in Nov-Mar comes from a circular day-of-year climatology of the S-2 Kcb. This is defensible here because the S-2 component of the anomaly is negligible (r 0.997 between observed-Kcb and climatological-Kcb runs). Operational and common-reference results for V1 are identical.
Dekadal event CIs are very wide (47 observed dry dekads; 29 in IV-X). No POD/FAR difference is significant.

Multiple comparisons: 12 configurations, 9 of them pre-registered. Comparisons were made against ISMN 20-30 cm and 10 cm, all-year and by season. There was also a 5-value Zr grid inside the CV and 2 robustness runs. V10 and V11 are post-hoc. Only V8 (worse) and diagnostic D (better) have CIs clear of zero for the all-year R.
The 30-day block bootstrap may understate uncertainty given seasonal autocorrelation. Year-block CIs are reported for the main dR values and are similar.
result.implementation_notes:
The model is a numpy loop mirroring pyfao56 v1.4.3 Model._advance (default soil method 'D', constant Zr, no runoff, p adjusted by ETc, Ks from FAO-56 Eq. 84). It was regression-tested against pyfao56 on 2016-2018: max |dDr| = 0.003 mm and |dETa| = 9e-5 mm (test_vs_pyfao56.py; pyfao56 installed to scratchpad/pkgs/pyfao56_lib, nothing system-wide).

Inputs:
- NDVI: clear_frac >= 0.9, IV-X only for the vineyard, 3-scene running median, linear interpolation in time. Gaps over 30 days fall back to climatology.
- Spin-up: start at field capacity on 1991-01-01.
- Relative soil water = 1 - Dr/TAW. All anomalies use step_04.clim_anomaly.

Statistics:
- Per-variant R uses step_07._block_bootstrap_ci.
- Paired dR uses my own same-block bootstrap (2000 resamples, 30-day and year blocks).
- POD/FAR CIs use a by-year bootstrap of dekads.

Repo modules were imported read-only and nothing in /home/user/1_geoworldlook-agriscreen was modified (git status clean). If adopted in v1.x:
(a) add maximum_2m_air_temperature, solar radiation, dewpoint and wind to step_01, so ET0 can be FAO-56 Penman-Monteith (pyfao56 refet);
(b) put the water balance on the dashboard as an interpretable 'typical vineyard on this soil' FTSW/deficit, not as a validated parcel anomaly;
(c) consider ERA5 0-28 cm for validation against the probes, and a common reference period for event validation.

Sources:
- [Campos et al. 2010, IDEAS record](https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/agiwat/v98y2010i1p45-54.html) (abstract)
- [EGU22-10231](https://meetingorganizer.copernicus.org/EGU22/EGU22-10231.html) (transferability of the linear NDVI-Kcb method)
- [Rallo et al. 2021, updated vine Kcb (AGRIS)](https://agris.fao.org/search/en/records/6887995d7fd4d06c32a95b9f) (values not retrieved)
- [Brekel et al. 2023, pyfao56 v1.1 (USDA ARS)](https://ars.usda.gov/ARSUserFiles/57795/Brekel2023%20-%20pyfao56%20v1.1.pdf)

verdict.experiment:
EXPERIMENT B: a prototype FAO-56 dual-Kc root-zone water balance for VINEYARD_06, with Kcb from S-2 NDVI (Campos 2010) and forcing from ERA5-Land precipitation and Hargreaves ET0. It is compared with the ERA5-Land 0-100 cm anomaly (v1.0), SPEI-like P-ET0 indices and LOYO combinations, using ISMN Condom 20-30 cm and 10 cm anomalies and dekadal POD/FAR. A diagnostic also tests ERA5 0-28 cm.

I checked it in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-1-geoworldlook-agriscreen/0b6bc240-34e1-5fd3-a139-3c46967fd603/scratchpad/exp_wb_verify/:
- v1_baseline_and_depth.py: my own ERA5 loading, anomaly code, block bootstraps (calendar blocks of 30, 90 and 365 days, moving blocks of 60 and 180 days), seasonal splits and event scores.
- v2_wb_independent.py: my own ET0 and Kcb rebuild, and a full 1991-2026 run in pyfao56 1.4.3 instead of the author's loop. It includes a causal (real-time) NDVI-to-Kcb variant and a leave-one-year-out Kcb climatology.
- v3_sensitivity.py: rooting depth (Zr) 1-3 m and ET0 x0.8, run for both the observed-Kcb (V1) and climatological-Kcb (V3) versions.

The repo is untouched (git status is clean).

claims.claim: The baseline was reproduced exactly: ERA5-Land 0-100 cm anomaly vs ISMN 20-30 cm R = 0.583 [0.50, 0.665], n = 2976; dekadal POD 0.574, FAR 0.571 (27 hits, 20 misses, 36 false alarms, n = 312).
claims.reason: My own anomaly code matches step_04.clim_anomaly to 5e-15. It gives R = 0.5834 with n = 2976 on the same days, and identical event counts from both the registry gwl_status and the recomputed operational z. The CI holds with 90-day, 365-day and moving-block bootstraps: [0.48-0.52, 0.66-0.68].

claims.claim: Side finding: putting both anomalies on 2016-2024 cuts the event FAR from 0.571 to 0.467 (POD 0.511), so part of the v1.0 FAR is a reference-period artefact.
claims.reason: The numbers reproduce, but the cause is not a drier 2016-2024 period. The operational ERA5 z over 2016-2024 has mean +0.05 and std 1.10, so 20.6% of days fall at z <= -1 (63 predicted dry dekads vs 45). The change only moves the threshold trade-off; discrimination is unchanged. Peirce skill (POD minus false-alarm rate) is 0.438 vs 0.432. So the lower FAR is a frequency-bias effect of the validation design, not better skill.

claims.claim: V1 (S-2 Kcb water balance) does not beat ERA5: R = 0.563 [0.481, 0.643], dR = -0.020 [-0.066, 0.024].
claims.reason: The independent pyfao56 run gives R = 0.5630 (z differs from the author's by at most 7e-5) and dR = -0.0205 [-0.071, 0.026] with 30-day blocks and [-0.068, 0.034] with year blocks. The 2016-2018 regression test against pyfao56 re-ran and passed.

claims.claim: The water balance is significantly worse than ERA5 in the growing season (IV-X dR about -0.10) and better in XI-III. Dekadal POD in IV-X is 0.21 vs 0.59.
claims.reason: Reproduced: IV-X dR = -0.097 [-0.165, -0.033] with 30-day blocks and [-0.204, -0.030] with year blocks. It holds in all 8 sensitivity settings I added (Zr 1-3 m, ET0 x1 or x0.8), with dR from -0.06 to -0.15 and every CI below zero. IV-X event counts confirmed: 6 of 29 hits.

claims.claim: The S-2 part of the anomaly is negligible: V1 minus V3 dR = -0.005 [-0.014, 0.004], the two anomaly series correlate at r = 0.997, and the S-2 component has std about 0.1 z.
claims.reason: Reproduced in pyfao56. It does not depend on non-causal processing: a causal Kcb (trailing median, last value carried forward up to 30 days) gives dR = +0.001 vs the original. A Kcb climatology that leaves out the evaluation year gives dR (V1 - V3) = -0.003. It also holds for TAW 140-420 mm and ET0 x0.8: r(z_V1, z_V3) >= 0.994 and S-2 component std 0.10-0.14 z. In two settings S-2 Kcb makes R significantly worse (for example Zr 1.0 m with ET0 x0.8: -0.018 [-0.035, -0.005]).

claims.claim: Physical reason: the regime is water-limited (Ks < 1 about 177 days a year, August RSW 0.09), so depletion is controlled by supply, not canopy.
claims.reason: The diagnostic numbers reproduce (177 days, 0.086, ETa about 660 mm for both vine and grass), but water limitation does not explain the result. With Zr 3 m and ET0 x0.8, Ks < 1 drops to 83 days a year and August RSW rises to 0.45, yet the S-2 component stays at 0.12 z (r 0.995). The interannual S-2 Kcb deviations are not small: IV-X std 0.12 and seasonal dKcb x ET0 from -82 to +108 mm. They mostly cancel because high NDVI comes in wet years and low NDVI in dry years, so the observed Kcb acts as a negative feedback that damps the anomaly. The z normalisation and the climatological Kcb used from November to March also contribute.

claims.claim: A lower NDVI lowers modelled ET, which damps the modelled deficit, so NDVI inside a water balance cannot act as a stress detector.
claims.reason: The direction is right and the data agree: years with positive Kcb deviations (2023, 2024) are wet years. But the scene-level correlation of the S-2 component with the NDVI anomaly is about 0.06, so the damping was not shown directly. 'Cannot' is also too general; it holds for this FAO-56 NDVI-to-Kcb setup, not for every way of combining a water balance with remote sensing.

claims.claim: SR 2.5 m and 10 m NDVI give identical results (V1 vs V2).
claims.reason: R 0.563 vs 0.562, identical event counts, per-year R differences of at most 0.015.

claims.claim: SPEI-like P-ET0 indices are not better; the 90-day version is significantly worse (dR -0.144).
claims.reason: Confirmed from the result files. The 90-day version is worse in all 9 years, and its CI excludes zero for both block types.

claims.claim: V9 (ERA5 + water balance, LOYO OLS) gives no clear gain: dR +0.009 [-0.009, 0.027] vs ERA5 refitted with LOYO.
claims.reason: Confirmed. The claim leaves out two things. V9 against raw ERA5 is -0.016 [-0.036, 0.004]. In IV-X it is significantly worse: -0.045 [-0.076, -0.017].

claims.claim: The post-hoc V10 gain (ERA5 + SPEI30) disappears once ERA5 depth matches the probe (partial r 0.06 given ERA5 0-28 cm).
claims.reason: Partial correlations confirmed (0.27 given 0-100 cm, 0.057 given 0-28 cm). The claim correctly labels V10 post-hoc and not a gain.

claims.claim: Diagnostic D, ERA5 0-28 cm, is a clear gain: R = 0.691, +0.108 [0.049, 0.167], better in 8 of 9 years, and one of two cheaper improvements.
claims.reason:
The daily-R gain against the probe is real and robust:
- dR +0.108 with CIs [0.040, 0.179] across 30-day, 90-day and year blocks.
- Better in 8 of 9 years.
- ERA5 layer 2 (7-28 cm) alone gives 0.693, and even 0-7 cm (0.627) beats 0-100 cm.

It is not an improvement to the drought product:
- The gain is entirely in XI-III: +0.249 [0.16, 0.34].
- IV-X: +0.013 [-0.10, 0.09]. VI-IX: -0.012.
- Operational (1991-2020 reference) events are worse. All dekads: POD 0.489 vs 0.574, Peirce skill 0.39 vs 0.44. IV-X: POD 0.379 vs 0.586, Peirce 0.23 vs 0.41.

It is valid as a validation-depth diagnostic only.

claims.claim: V1 beats ERA5 in 4 of 9 years.
claims.reason: From results_r_by_year.csv it is 5 of 9 (2016, 2018, 2019, 2020 and 2022, the last by +0.002). This is trivial and does not change the conclusion.

claims.claim: V5 (Zr chosen by leave-one-year-out) has lower FAR (0.375) but lower POD (0.426); CIs overlap the baseline. IV-X dR -0.151.
claims.reason: Confirmed. The leave-one-year-out loop is clean (Zr picked on 8 years, applied to the 9th); the choices alternate between 0.5 and 0.75 m, whose training R values are almost identical.

claims.claim: V11 PSMD is invalid in this climate: the deficit drifts to more than 5000 mm and R = -0.07.
claims.reason: Numbers confirmed: the deficit reaches 4488-5634 mm by 2016-2024. But this is a flaw of the unbounded, never-reset version that was built. A deficit reset each winter, or bounded by TAW, would not drift. 'Invalid in this climate' overstates it.

claims.claim: No data leakage, and the water balance is operationally implementable in Colab.
claims.reason: Validation anomalies use the repo's common 2016-2024 climatology for both series (same as the baseline). Running the NDVI processing causally and using a leave-one-year-out Kcb climatology changes R by at most 0.001. The model is a 13,000-day loop that runs in seconds. One remaining issue: before 2016 Kcb is climatological, so an operational 1991-2020 reference mixes climatological and observed Kcb. This is harmless here because the S-2 effect is negligible.

3. Sensitivity, Zr 1-3 m by ET0 x1 or x0.8 (v3_sensitivity.py, .json):
   - The S-2 component stays at 0.10-0.14 z (r(z_V1, z_V3) >= 0.994) even when Ks < 1 only 83 days a year.
   - IV-X dR vs ERA5 is significantly negative in all 8 settings.
   - Post hoc, ET0 x0.8 with Zr 1.0 m reaches R 0.586 (V1) and 0.604 (V3) overall, but stays worse in IV-X.

4. Depth diagnostic:
   - ERA5 0-28 cm: R 0.691. Layer 2 alone: 0.693.
   - dR by season: all +0.108, XI-III +0.249, IV-X +0.013 (CI includes 0), VI-IX -0.012.
   - Operational events: POD 0.489, FAR 0.531. IV-X: POD 0.379 vs 0.586.

5. Autocorrelation and block length:
   - Lag-30 autocorrelation is 0.32 for the ISMN z and 0.25 for the residual; lag-60 residual is 0.10.
   - So 30-day blocks are slightly short, but 90-day, 365-day and 180-day moving blocks give nearly the same CIs.
issues: The causal explanation is partly wrong. Water limitation is not the main reason the S-2 Kcb has no effect: the effect stays at about 0.12 z even when the bucket is rarely stressed. The more likely reason is a negative feedback, where high-NDVI years are wet years and the observed Kcb damps the anomaly, plus Ks damping and the climatological Kcb used November to March.

The ERA5 0-28 cm diagnostic is presented as an 'improvement' with verdict clear_gain. Its whole gain is in XI-III. In IV-X it adds nothing to daily R, and with the operational reference it gives worse growing-season event detection (POD 0.38 vs 0.59, Peirce 0.23 vs 0.41). It should be framed as a validation-depth effect, not a product improvement.

The common-reference FAR reduction (0.571 to 0.467) is a frequency-bias change: 63 vs 45 predicted dry dekads, and Peirce skill 0.438 vs 0.432. It is not better discrimination, and the cause is the higher variance of 2016-2024, not a mean shift.
V9 is reported only against ERA5 refitted with LOYO. Against raw ERA5 it is worse overall (-0.016) and significantly worse in IV-X (-0.045 [-0.076, -0.017]).
Small factual slip: V1 beats ERA5 in 5 of 9 years, not 4.
'No water-balance variant beats ERA5' depends on the literature parameters. A post-hoc ET0 x0.8 already gives overall parity (V3 0.604). Only the IV-X deficit holds across all parameter settings.
The water-balance 'advantage' against the 10 cm probe is irrelevant: ERA5 0-28 cm gives R 0.671 against 10 cm, above every water-balance variant (0.53-0.55).
V11 is labelled 'invalid in this climate', but it is invalid because of how it was built (unbounded, never reset), not as a concept.
verdict.corrected_conclusion:
The experiment's negative result holds and is reproduced, but two interpretations need correcting.

1. The baseline is reproduced exactly: R = 0.583, n = 2976; POD 0.574 and FAR 0.571 on 312 dekads.

2. The FAO-56 dual-Kc water balance with S-2 NDVI Kcb does not beat ERA5-Land 0-100 cm. Overall: V1 R = 0.563, dR -0.020 [-0.07, 0.03]. In the growing season it is significantly worse: IV-X dR about -0.10 [-0.17, -0.03], and IV-X dekadal POD 0.21 vs 0.59.
   - This growing-season deficit holds for every Zr from 1 to 3 m and for ET0 x0.8.
   - Only the overall all-year R depends on the parameters (post-hoc ET0 x0.8 gives parity).

3. The S-2 Kcb contributes nothing measurable.
   - Observed vs climatological Kcb: dR -0.005, r 0.997.
   - This does not change with real-time NDVI processing, a Kcb climatology that leaves out the evaluation year, or less water-limited parameters.
   - In some settings the S-2 Kcb makes R slightly but significantly worse.
   - The likely reason is a negative feedback, not just water limitation. Greener canopies occur in wetter years and raise modelled ET, so the observed Kcb damps rather than amplifies the anomaly.
   - SR 2.5 m and 10 m give identical results. Under this setup, NDVI-driven water balances are not a route to parcel-specific drought skill.

4. SPEI-like indices: the 30- and 60-day versions are no better than ERA5, and the 90-day version is significantly worse.

5. The two diagnostic 'improvements' are validation effects, not better products.
   - ERA5 0-28 cm matches the 20-30 cm probe better: R 0.691, +0.11, robust to block length. But the whole gain is in XI-III. In IV-X it adds nothing to daily R, and with the operational 1991-2020 reference it gives worse growing-season event detection.
   - Use it to choose the right ERA5 depth when validating against probes, not to replace the 0-100 cm root-zone warning layer.
   - The common-reference FAR (0.467) only reduces the over-forecasting of dry dekads; Peirce skill is unchanged at about 0.43-0.44.

6. Use for the dashboard: a water balance can still be shown as an interpretable 'typical vineyard on this soil' FTSW or deficit. It is not a validated anomaly, and its absolute values need calibration first because the current setup empties the bucket every August.

result.experiment: C: soil-moisture layer and event skill. ERA5-Land layer/depth matching, anomaly definition, Sentinel-1 change detection with an exponential-filter SWI, ERA5+S1 fusion (equal weights and triple-collocation weights), and the sensitivity of dry-dekad event detection to threshold and persistence rules. Reference is ISMN Condom 20-30 cm, 2016-2024.

baseline_reproduced.description: R between the ERA5-Land 0-100 cm DOY-climatology z and the ISMN Condom 20-30 cm z, with both climatologies on 2016-2024 (hw 15, min_n 20), using step_04.clim_anomaly and step_07._r_with_ci (30-day blocks, 1000 draws, seed 42). The dry-dekad events also reproduce exactly. That check used the status sma_rz (1991-2020 base) from gwl_status.csv and a recomputation from era5_land_daily.csv, which agree to 1e-15: hits 27, misses 20, false alarms 36, correct negatives 229, so POD 0.574, FAR 0.571, CSI 0.325, n=312.
baseline_reproduced.note: Exact match: R=0.583 [0.500,0.665], n=2976, POD/FAR/n identical. Year-block bootstrap CIs for the baseline events are very wide: POD [0.21,0.83], FAR [0.42,0.80], CSI [0.12,0.51]. There are only 47 observed dry dekads. One definitional asymmetry was found. The operational sma_rz uses a 1991-2020 base, while the ISMN reference can only use 2016-2024. Measured against 1991-2020, ERA5 is at z<=-1 on 20.6% of days in 2016-2024, versus 15.0% against its own 2016-2024 base. This gives a frequency bias of 1.34, which accounts for part of the FAR.

result.conclusion:
1) The v1.0 R=0.58 is mostly a depth mismatch, not a weak model. Against the 20-30 cm sensors, ERA5-Land layer 2 (7-28 cm) gives R=0.69 [0.62,0.75] vs 0.58. The paired gain is +0.11 [0.05,0.17]; it holds in 9/9 years, holds under LOYO layer selection (+0.14) and survives multiple-comparison correction. Layer 3 (28-100 cm), 72% of the 0-100 cm mean, is the weak part (R=0.48).

2) ERA5 L2 is now close to what one point sensor can confirm. Extended triple collocation puts the Condom sensor's own correlation with the shared signal at 0.72-0.78, and ERA5 L2's at about 0.89-0.90. As a benchmark, the nearest independent station (PeyrusseGrande, 35 km) reaches only R=0.54 with Condom.

3) The choice of climatology base changes events, not R. The operational 1991-2020 base flags 20.6% of 2016-2024 days against 15% on the sensor's own base. That alone inflates FAR (0.571 vs 0.491 on a consistent base). The 35-day moving anomaly removes the drought signal (R 0.30 vs the drought target), so it should not drive status.

4) Sentinel-1 change detection at the station is weak. Raw R with the 5 cm sensor is 0.19; ERA5 L1 beats it on the same days. The SWI with T≈10 d (chosen leave-one-year-out) reaches R 0.55, the same as ERA5 0-100 cm, and adds nothing to depth-matched ERA5. In the depth-consistent TC, ERA5 gets weight 0.73-0.93, and the fusion ΔR is -0.001. The only fusion gain (+0.05, equal weights with 0-100 cm) just compensates the depth mismatch and does not survive correction. TC with depth-mismatched products was unstable.

5) Thresholds and persistence do not cut FAR without losing POD. At z<=-1.5 FAR stays at 0.53 while POD falls to 0.17. The 2-dekad persistence rule gives POD 0.45 and FAR 0.54. EDO hysteresis and LOYO-tuned thresholds are no better out of sample. False alarms cluster in August-October. In those months the 20-30 cm sensor sits within 0.02 m3/m3 of its dry floor on 18-30% of days, so late-summer reference events are unreliable.

Recommendation for the v1.1 soil-moisture layer:
- Keep ERA5-Land as the only soil source: daily, gap-free, with a 1991-2020 climatology.
- Switch the warning trigger to the L2 (or 0-28 cm) z <= -1. Show 0-100 cm as deep-reservoir context: it cannot be validated with sensors that stop at 30 cm, and in 2017 it gave 29 warning dekads against 13 for L2.
- Keep the -1 threshold. Do not add persistence or S-1.
- In validation, add: depth-matched rows, events on a consistent base, Spearman, the TC ceiling, the neighbour benchmark, and a low-confidence flag for VIII-X events.
- Event-level skill differences remain statistically unresolved: 47 events, year-bootstrap CIs about ±0.2.
caveats: One station and 9 years. There are only 47 observed dry dekads, so no event-level difference (POD/FAR/CSI) has a CI that excludes zero. The event table is a sensitivity analysis, not proof.

The reference stops at 30 cm. 'L2 is better' means better at 7-30 cm. It does not show that L2 is a better indicator of vine water status: vine roots go well below 1 m, and the 0-100 cm/deep-layer signal remains unvalidated rather than wrong. In summer 2017 the 0-100 cm z tracked the 20-30 cm dry anomaly better than L2 did.
The 20-30 cm sensor sits at its dry floor in VII-X (18-30% of days within 0.02 m3/m3 of p2), so z there amplifies noise. Late-summer false alarms and misses are partly reference error.
The ISMN climatology covers only 2016-2024 and the operational ERA5 uses 1991-2020. Event scores depend on which base is used, and both are reported.

Triple collocation: the third source (PeyrusseGrande, 35 km) has representativeness error that may correlate with ERA5's, and SWI at the station shares local signal with Condom. TC weights are only indicative. TC is invalid for depth-mismatched triplets (0-100 cm with 20-30 cm).

S-1 change detection comes from a 50 m buffer over a grass station plot (calibrated on 2016-2021 percentiles; 10% of values clipped at 0 or 1). It is not representative of vineyard row canopies. The Sentinel-1B loss halved acquisitions in 2022-2024.
The 5 cm sensor was swapped in 2019 (ML3 to ML2x), so 5 cm climatological anomalies are meaningless (R about 0 with everything). Only 35-day anomalies per segment were used at 5 cm.
The soil-moisture layer cannot be parcel-specific: all 15 vineyards share one ERA5-Land cell. The station is 136 m from VINEYARD_06 and is not inside it.

Literature was available only as search snippets (publisher sites were blocked): Albergel et al. 2008 HESS 12:1323 (exponential filter on SMOSMANIA, 30 cm reference); Gruber et al. 2017 IEEE TGRS 55:6780 (TC-based merging); Gruber et al. 2020 RSE 244:111806 (validation practice and representativeness); Stradiotti et al. 2025 (seasonal vs stationary TC weights give similar merges); Formanek et al. EGU 2024 (TC sampling uncertainty); a 2026 Remote Sensing study (Yunnan) also found ERA5-Land 7-28 cm best for root-zone dynamics. The T values Albergel reports per station could not be checked.

verdict.experiment: C: ERA5-Land soil-moisture layer and event skill against ISMN Condom 20-30 cm, 2016-2024. Covers layer matching, anomaly base, Sentinel-1 change detection with SWI, ERA5+S1 fusion, and threshold/persistence rules for dry-dekad events. I re-ran the checks in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-1-geoworldlook-agriscreen/0b6bc240-34e1-5fd3-a139-3c46967fd603/scratchpad/exp_sm_verify/ (v0_core.py, v1_events.py, v2_years.py, v3_opbase_season.py).

claims.claim: The v1.0 baseline was reproduced faithfully: R=0.583 [0.50,0.665], n=2976; events POD 0.574, FAR 0.571, n=312.
claims.reason: The definitions match the repo: step_04.clim_anomaly with hw 15 and min_n 20 on 2016-2024, the mean of 20 and 30 cm from step_07 QC, and dekad_end. I got the same R/n and the same 27/20/36/229 contingency. My own .stm parser (flag G, at least 12 h per day) gives R_rz=0.600 and R_l2=0.695 (dR +0.096), so the result does not depend on the repo's QC.

claims.claim: All-year, ERA5-Land L2 (7-28 cm) anomalies correlate better with the 20-30 cm sensors than 0-100 cm does: R 0.693 vs 0.583, dR +0.109 [0.05,0.17].
claims.reason: The paired dR CI excludes zero for 30, 90, 180 and 365-day blocks ([0.055,0.170] to [0.059,0.175]). It holds on the operational 1991-2020 base (+0.100 [0.046,0.155]) and under LOYO. It is physically plausible as depth matching. Bonferroni over all 52 variants pushes the lower bound just below zero (-0.004 at 90 d, -0.011 at 180 d), but this was the primary, physically pre-specified hypothesis. Note that the code divides by 21 tests while the text says 22.

claims.claim: The v1.0 R=0.58 is mostly a depth mismatch, and L2 is the better layer in general.
claims.reason: The gain is almost all in the cold season. On the operational base, XI-III dR is +0.221 [0.14,0.30]; IV-X is +0.024 [-0.05,0.09]; VII-X is -0.024 [-0.13,0.06]. Under LOYO it is IV-X +0.049 and VII-X +0.004. In the growing season, 0-100 cm tracks the 20-30 cm sensor about as well as L2 does. So the mismatch is about recharge timing in winter (0-100 cm lags), not a uniform depth error.

claims.claim: Switching the operational warning trigger to L2 z<=-1 (0-100 cm becomes context only) improves the vineyard warning.
claims.reason: Alerts can only fire in IV-X (S2_MONTHS). In IV-X on the operational base, L2 does worse: hits/misses/false alarms 12/17/22 vs 17/12/27 for RZ, CSI 0.235 vs 0.304 (dCSI -0.07 [-0.31,0.18]). In VII-X, L2 hits 1 of 13 observed events and RZ hits 8 (dPOD -0.54 [-0.86,0.00]). In the 2017 summer drought the 20-30 cm sensor sat at z<=-1 from June to August; RZ flagged it and L2 stayed between -0.4 and +0.4. That is a miss at the very depth L2 is meant to match. In IV-X 2017, RZ hit 12 of 13 observed events and L2 hit 4. The experiment's all-season summary hid this; its own c5_events.csv shows the IV-X reversal.

claims.claim: Under LOYO layer selection, L2 is picked in 8/9 folds, with dR +0.141.
claims.reason: Confirmed. The +0.141 is inflated relative to operations, though. LOYO climatology costs RZ much more (0.583 to 0.547) than L2 (0.693 to 0.689), because deep-layer anomalies persist across years. The operational (1991-2020 base) gain is +0.10.

claims.claim: The base period alone inflates FAR (0.571 on 1991-2020 vs 0.491 on a consistent base); the false alarms come from evaluation design, not product error.
claims.reason: The direction is plausible: 20.6% vs 15.0% of days at z<=-1. But dFAR = -0.081 [-0.29,0.04] includes zero. The base shift also differs by layer (L2 is 17.2% vs 15.5%), which confounds the L2-vs-RZ FAR comparison on the operational base. Some of the 'false alarms' (for example RZ in Jul-Sep 2022) are probably real droughts that the floor-limited sensor cannot express.

claims.claim: Extended triple collocation puts the point-sensor ceiling at R_truth 0.72-0.78 and ERA5 L2 at about 0.89-0.90, so L2 is close to what one sensor can confirm.
claims.reason: The numbers reproduce from the outputs. But the SWI comes from a 50 m buffer at the station, so it shares local signal with Condom. That violates TC error independence and biases the estimates: Condom's R_truth goes up and ERA5's goes down. The value also changes with the third member (RZ 0.81 vs 0.66). Treat it as indicative only. L2 reaches about 0.69/0.78 of the ceiling, which is not quite 'close'.

claims.claim: Neighbour benchmark: the nearest independent station (PeyrusseGrande, 35 km) reaches only R=0.54 with Condom.
claims.reason: From the .stm header coordinates, CreondArmagnac is nearer (30.7 km vs 35.5 km) and its R with Condom is 0.354. PeyrusseGrande is the best-correlated of the four neighbours, not the nearest. It was also chosen as the TC third source by its R with the target, which is a mild selection effect.

claims.claim: Sentinel-1 change detection or SWI adds nothing beyond depth-matched ERA5; fusion gains do not survive correction.
claims.reason: Raw R vs 5 cm is 0.19. On the same days, ERA5 L1 gets 0.59 and S-1 0.35. The SWI LOYO R is 0.549, about equal to RZ. The TC-weighted L2+S1 fusion gives dR -0.001. T selection and climatology are LOYO, and the filter is causal, so there is no leakage of concern. The S-1 calibration on 2016-2021 percentiles is only in-sample for S-1 itself and favours S-1, which does not change the null result.

claims.claim: Threshold, persistence and hysteresis rules do not improve event skill; LOYO-tuned thresholds do not generalise.
claims.reason: All CSI differences have year-bootstrap CIs that span zero, and the LOYO rule selection gives CSI 0.288 vs 0.325. With only 47 events and 9 year-blocks, this is 'no evidence of improvement', not 'evidence of no improvement'.

claims.claim: Late-summer reference events are unreliable because the 20-30 cm sensor is at its dry floor on 18-30% of VII-X days.
claims.reason: The c7 output confirms it. 2022 also shows it: an extreme drought, yet the sensor z was only -0.4 to -0.8 in Jul-Sep. The caveat cuts both ways, though. It also means the reference cannot show that L2 is better in the vine-relevant season, and the experiment leaned on it only to discount RZ's late-summer false alarms.

verdict.reran_check:
I reproduced R_rz=0.583 and R_l2=0.693, both n=2976 (repo QC). My own .stm parser gives R_rz=0.600 and R_l2=0.695 (n=3120). I reproduced the events exactly: 27/20/36, POD 0.574, FAR 0.571, and RZ/L2 z<=-1 day shares of 0.206/0.150 and 0.172/0.155.

The dR(L2-RZ) 95% CI is [0.055,0.170] with 30-day blocks and [0.059,0.175] with 365-day blocks. The Bonferroni CI for 52 variants is [-0.004,0.221] with 90-day blocks.

Seasonal R on the operational 1991-2020 base:

| Season | RZ | L2 | dR (L2-RZ) [90-day-block CI] |
|---|---|---|---|
| XI-III | 0.526 | 0.747 | +0.221 [0.14,0.30] |
| IV-X | 0.621 | 0.645 | +0.024 [-0.05,0.09] |
| VII-X | 0.598 | 0.574 | -0.024 [-0.13,0.06] |

The LOYO series give the same picture: IV-X 0.596 vs 0.645, VII-X 0.561 vs 0.565.

Events on the operational base, paired 3000-draw year bootstrap:

| Season | L2 hit/miss/false alarm | RZ hit/miss/false alarm | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| IV-X | 12/17/22 | 17/12/27 | dCSI -0.068 [-0.31,0.18] |
| VII-X | 1/12/20 | 8/5/22 | dPOD -0.54 [-0.86,0.00] |
| XI-III | 12/6/3 | 10/8/9 | dCSI +0.20 [0.00,0.28] |

The 2017 dekad table shows obs z<=-1 from late June through August. RZ_op was mostly <=-1 over that span (-0.88 to -1.61) and L2_op was -0.36 to +0.40 from July to August. The station headers show CreondArmagnac at 30.7 km and PeyrusseGrande at 35.5 km. step_01_ingest.py already ingests volumetric_soil_water_layer_2, so L2 is operationally trivial to use.
issues: Selective reporting: the headline and recommendation use all-season R and events. The experiment's own c5_events.csv shows that in IV-X (the only months an alert can fire) L2 has lower CSI and POD than RZ on the operational base. This was not surfaced.
The L2 gain is seasonal: XI-III dR is about +0.22, IV-X about +0.02 (n.s.), VII-X about -0.02. Calling it a general 'depth mismatch' overstates it. It is cold-season recharge timing.

2017 summer drought: L2 misses July-August dry anomalies that the 20-30 cm sensor itself shows (z -1.2 to -1.5) and that RZ captures. The '29 vs 13 warning dekads in 2017' framing implies RZ over-warns, but in IV-X 2017 RZ had 12 hits out of 13 observed events against L2's 4.

The late-summer 'reference floor' argument is used one-sidedly, to excuse RZ's false alarms. It equally means there is no evidence L2 is better in the vine-stress season. Vine roots are deep, so 0-100 cm is the physically more relevant layer in summer.
Factual error: PeyrusseGrande is not the nearest neighbour. CreondArmagnac (30.7 km, R=0.35) is. PeyrusseGrande was the best of four, chosen by its R with the target.

Bonferroni bookkeeping: the text says 22 tests, the code uses 21, and 52 variants were tried. With 52, the lower bound for L2 vs RZ touches zero (-0.004 at 90 d). This is acceptable only because L2 was the primary physically pre-specified hypothesis.
The LOYO dR of +0.141 is inflated by LOYO climatology penalising the persistent deep layer more. The operational-base dR of +0.10 is the relevant number.

The base-period FAR attribution is stated as fact ('that alone inflates FAR'), but dFAR's CI includes zero. The layers also differ in base shift (L2 17.2% vs RZ 20.6% of days at z<=-1), which confounds the operational-base FAR comparison.
The ETC ceiling depends on the S-1 SWI and Condom being at the same station, which gives them correlated local errors. The estimates are indicative only and change with the triplet.
The event-level CIs come from only 9 year-blocks and 47 events, so percentile CIs are coarse. All event differences are underpowered.

Leakage: none of concern was found. Predictor climatologies, SWI T and TC weights are fitted on training years in the LOYO variants. The SWI filter is causal. The reference ISMN climatology uses all years, which is standard and symmetric for both sides.
verdict.corrected_conclusion:
1) The baseline is faithfully reproduced (R=0.583; POD 0.574, FAR 0.571) and the code is clean. I found no data leakage of concern.

2) Over the whole year, ERA5-Land L2 (7-28 cm) tracks the 20-30 cm sensors better than 0-100 cm: R 0.68-0.69 vs 0.58, dR about +0.10, robust to block length and to an independent ISMN parse. The gain is almost entirely in November-March (dR about +0.22), when the deep 28-100 cm layer lags winter recharge. In the growing season the two layers are statistically equivalent: IV-X dR +0.02 [-0.05,0.09], VII-X -0.02.

3) Event skill does not support switching the warning trigger to L2 for a vineyard monitor. In IV-X on the operational 1991-2020 base, L2 detects fewer observed dry dekads (12 vs 17 of 29; CSI 0.24 vs 0.30). In VII-X it detects 1 of 13 vs 8 of 13. It also missed the July-August 2017 drought that the 20-30 cm sensor itself recorded. All event CIs are wide (47 events, 9 years), so neither layer is proven better in season. The defensible statement is: 'L2 improves agreement in the cold season; there is no evidence of improvement, and some evidence of worse detection, in the season when alerts can fire.'

4) Recommendation for v1.1:
- Keep ERA5-Land 0-100 cm as the IV-X warning trigger.
- Add L2 as a depth-matched validation row, reported both all-year and seasonally (XI-III / IV-X / VII-X).
- If a layer change is wanted, pre-register a season-aware rule (for example L2 in XI-III, RZ in IV-X) and test it on independent stations or years before adopting it, since choosing it from these results would be post-hoc.

5) Sentinel-1 change detection, SWI and their fusion add nothing over ERA5 at this station. Thresholds, persistence and hysteresis do not help out of sample. Both conclusions stand.

6) Smaller corrections:
- The neighbour benchmark should say 'best-correlated of four neighbours (PeyrusseGrande, 35.5 km, R=0.54); the nearest, CreondArmagnac at 30.7 km, has R=0.35'.
- The TC 'ceiling' is indicative only.
- The base-period effect on FAR is plausible but not statistically established.
- The 20-30 cm reference saturates at its dry floor in late summer. That limits validation of any layer in exactly the vine-stress period, so deeper or vine-water-status references are needed before re-ranking layers for viticulture.
